proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, cross-working-group review gates, and runtime safeguards for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, privacy-preserving execution models, and runtime safeguards for autonomous agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]. Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group functions as an intersecting review and guidance layer across all AAIF working groups, assessing vulnerabilities in memory, tool execution, delegation, and identity[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Operations

The working group operates on a bi-weekly cadence and is open to all foundation membership tiers, with chair and co-chair leadership reserved for Gold and Platinum members[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]. Working group outputs span formal specifications, reference architectures, best practice guides, and security review checklists, such as the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].

- **Chair**: Alex Frazer (elected March 2026)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Co-Chair**: In recruitment among eligible member representatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Primary Workstreams**: Finalizing mission and scope, curating an internal security taxonomy prior to harmonization, and submitting the formal working group charter to the governing board[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

## Scope and Domain Boundaries

The group coordinates boundaries across related technical domains:

- **Governance and Ethics**: Questions involving value judgments, AI bias, and corporate ethics are deferred to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Agentic Commerce**: Commercial workflows are scoped strictly to security guardrails—such as preventing unauthorized fund draining, mitigating credential leaks, and scoping financial agent capabilities—in dialogue with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Reliability vs. Derailment**: Evaluation metrics for non-adversarial hallucinations are directed to the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), while non-malicious agent misbehavior, agent derailment, and blast radius containment remain active investigation areas within Security and Privacy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **External Alignment**: The working group coordinates alignment with external industry initiatives, including the OWASP Agentic working group[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

## Priority Technical Themes

The group's initial charter brainstorming identified core focus areas for technical artifacts:

1. **Execution and Host Sandboxing**: Runtime tool-calling mediation, capability-based access controls, and prompt injection mitigation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].
2. **Private Agentic Workflows**: Hardware-isolated enclaves (TEEs), zero-knowledge verification patterns, and encrypted vector databases protecting confidential session state[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
3. **Sensitive Data and Secrets Management**: PII obfuscation, token isolation, and differentiating static credentials from proprietary training context[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
4. **Blast Radius and Forensics**: Auditability, causal action traceability, and containment patterns for rogue or derailed agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-17**: Orientation and community ideation meeting convened by Linux Foundation leadership; governance structure outlined and initial deliverable backlog drafted[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].
- **2026-03-03**: Alex Frazer elected as Chair; milestone schedule adopted; explicit scope boundaries established regarding ethics deferrals and commerce security guardrails[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing landscape and gap analyses across global AI policy, regulatory frameworks, risk assessment protocols, and governance standards for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with evaluating international policy, regulatory frameworks, and risk assessment methodologies to develop concrete governance guidance and technical benchmarks for agentic AI deployments. Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and governed by the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md), the group bridges jurisdictional compliance requirements—such as the EU AI Act, eIDAS 2, and sector-specific privacy mandates—with the operational realities of autonomous and multi-agent systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]

# Architecture / Specification

## Operational Scope and Focus Areas
The working group operates on a biweekly cadence and focuses on pre-competitive analysis of emerging regulatory and compliance intersections for agentic AI[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:
- **Regulatory Framework Mapping:** Evaluating the impact of emerging statutory frameworks (including the EU AI Act and eIDAS 2) and international regulatory sandboxes (such as Singapore co-creation initiatives) on autonomous agents.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]
- **Risk Assessment Protocols:** Formulating probabilistic risk assessment frameworks, auditability criteria, and agent-human oversight patterns such as [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [hard-constraint-gate](../patterns/hard-constraint-gate.md).[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]
- **Compliance and Privacy Controls:** Addressing data protection mandates (e.g., GDPR, PII handling, and cross-border data transfer) across autonomous agent reasoning loops, memory stores, and tool execution boundaries.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]

## Three-Step Working Model and Deliverables
The working group has formally adopted a phased three-step execution model to structure its work product[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:
1. **Landscape Analysis:** A comprehensive review mapping existing industry frameworks, standards, and jurisdictional regulations relevant to agentic systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]
2. **Gap Analysis:** An analytical assessment identifying specific operational and safety risks posed by autonomous agents that are unaddressed by existing frameworks.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]
3. **Distilled Guidance and Principles:** A consolidated set of governance recommendations, organizational principles, and potential technical implementation guidance for deploying agentic systems in regulated environments.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]

## Repository and Record-Keeping Standards
Working group records are maintained in descending date order in accordance with standardized meeting notes templates and agent automation instructions[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654]. Each session record tracks AI summaries, LFX recordings, transcripts, decisions, deliverables, and assigned action item tables[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a].

# Lifecycle History
The working group held its initial kickoff meeting on February 19, 2026, establishing its initial operational structure, antitrust boundaries, and leadership nomination process[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]. On March 5, 2026, under co-chairs Ryan and Junjie, the working group ratified its three-step operating model and launched work on the initial landscape and gap analysis deliverables[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing technical vision, project lifecycle transitions, working groups, and architectural recommendations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), operating under the authority of the AAIF Governing Board (GB) within The Linux Foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. Formally chartered on March 3, 2026, the TC is tasked with evaluating incoming technical project proposals, steering cross-project priorities, chartering and archiving working groups, and enforcing the foundation's project lifecycle rules[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Architecture / Specification
## Composition and Appointments
The Technical Committee is composed of designated representatives appointed by AAIF member organizations: each Platinum Member of the AAIF is entitled to appoint one voting representative to the committee[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. The committee annually elects a TC Chair, and optionally a Co-Chair, who presides over meetings and administrative proceedings until their resignation or replacement by the TC[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Responsibilities and Mandate
The TC functions as the technical coordination hub connecting community projects, working groups, and the Governing Board. Core operational duties include[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
- Establishing, managing, and archiving AAIF Working Groups across technical domains relevant to the foundation's scope.
- Coordinating technical collaboration and harmonizing architectural vision across foundation initiatives.
- Formulating recommendations to the Governing Board regarding project proposal acceptance as official Technical Projects.
- Applying and maintaining the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) and deciding status transitions for existing technical projects.
- Recommending foundation resource allocations and infrastructure priorities to the Governing Board.

## Governance and Voting Rules
While the TC operates primarily as a consensus-based community, formal determinations adhere to strict procedural rules[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
- **Vote Allocation:** Each appointed voting member holds exactly one vote.
- **Quorum:** Quorum requires at least fifty percent (50%) of active voting members present; non-quorum meetings may proceed for discussion but cannot execute binding decisions.
- **Lazy Consensus:** Procedural approvals may proceed under lazy consensus ("silence-as-agreement"), whereby an item is automatically approved if no formal objection is recorded within 72 hours.
- **Electronic Balloting:** If an objection is raised against a lazy consensus proposal, electronic votes conducted outside a meeting require an absolute majority vote of all active TC voting members.
- **Escalation and Amendments:** Deadlocked disputes may be referred to the Governing Board for resolution. Amending the TC Charter requires a two-thirds supermajority vote of the TC alongside Governing Board approval.

# Lifecycle History
The Technical Committee Charter was formally adopted on March 3, 2026, codifying Platinum Member representation, lazy consensus mechanics, and project lifecycle enforcement powers under the Linux Foundation directed fund structure[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat models, security design patterns, and privacy engineering controls across the agentic AI ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]. Guided by co-chairs Alex Frazer and Junjie Bu (Google), the group develops vendor-neutral threat models, shared architectural taxonomies, and design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups adopt to distribute responsibility for trustworthy AI agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

# Architecture / Specification
## Mission and Mandate
On March 31, 2026, the working group formally adopted its mission statement establishing security and data protection as collaborative ecosystem responsibilities rather than isolated vendor concerns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]. The working group focuses on privacy engineering and technical controls—such as data minimization, memory isolation, prompt injection resistance, and audit logging—rather than interpreting legal statutes or prescribing compliance mandates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

## Scope Areas and Deliverables
The working group's scope and deliverable roadmap encompass five core workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]:
- **Agentic AI Taxonomy:** A living vocabulary and definition index harmonized across foundation workstreams.
- **Threat Modeling Framework:** Practical attack surface mapping and threat analysis methodologies covering prompt injection, tool poisoning, and subagent delegation risks.
- **Security Architecture and Design Patterns:** Structural blueprints covering runtime isolation, kill switches, and security boundaries, explicitly incorporating agent skills into the architecture scope[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **Security Best Practices Guide:** Builder-focused operational recommendations for credentials isolation, sandboxing, and context redaction.
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Evaluation criteria shared across foundation workstreams to review security implications in peer group deliverables.

## Inter-Group Coordination
To prevent redundant standardization, the Security and Privacy Working Group maintains targeted interfaces with peer bodies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]:
- **Identity and Trust:** Delegates core authentication mechanisms to [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md) while supplying logging, containment, and audit requirements.
- **Observability and Traceability:** Coordinates on runtime behavioral anomaly detection and audit trace requirements with [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md).
- **Agentic Commerce:** Coordinates through cross-membership liaisons to assess payment guardrails and transaction boundary risks with [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md).
- **Governance, Risk, and Regulatory:** Coordinates regulatory tracking through [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) while focusing internally on privacy engineering controls.

# Lifecycle History
In March 2026, Junjie Bu joined Alex Frazer as working group co-chair[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]. On March 31, 2026, the group voted without objection to adopt its formal mission statement and added skills governance to its design patterns scope[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, workflow execution traces, and cross-framework observability conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to establish a shared understanding of agent observability across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Led by Chair Pavan Sudheendra, the working group serves as an open coordination forum rather than a competing standards organization, aligning fragmented tracing ecosystems and defining multi-turn, workflow-level conventions without duplicating upstream specifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Architecture / Specification
## Operating Philosophy and Mandate
The OT-WG is explicitly structured as an alignment and gap-identification forum rather than a competing specification body[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Its charter establishes key operational principles:
- **Coordinate First, Specify Only When Necessary:** Direct effort toward existing standards efforts (such as the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context) and produce new specifications only when an unaddressed gap is formally demonstrated.
- **Interoperability Over Innovation:** Prioritize cross-framework data exchange and composability over novel schemas to avoid vendor lock-in.
- **Observable by Default:** Advocate out-of-the-box telemetry across multi-agent workflows, tool calls, and model interactions.
- **Neutrality:** Prevent architectural bias toward proprietary commercial platforms.

## Focus Areas and Workstreams
The working group targets the systemic divide between low-level LLM call tracing and session-level agent behavior[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** Founding focus area establishing vendor-neutral semantic conventions for multi-turn sessions, context assembly, and tool boundary interactions.
- **Multi-Modal Lineage:** Investigating content lineage, fidelity, and grounding verification across modality transformations where existing standards lack coverage.
- **Protocol Boundary Observability:** Standardizing contextual trace propagation across protocol boundaries such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent interfaces.

## Foundation and Upstream Alignment
The working group acts as AAIF's technical interface to external standards bodies, funneling practitioner requirements upstream to OpenTelemetry and related initiatives[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Within AAIF, the OT-WG collaborates with [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md) on anomaly detection telemetry and audit forensics, and with [Workflows and Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md) on workflow-level execution primitives.

# Lifecycle History
The working group's charter was advanced in April 2026 under the leadership of Primary Contact Pavan Sudheendra, establishing its focus group operating model and alignment to OpenTelemetry GenAI standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat models, security design patterns, privacy engineering guidelines, and cross-working group review baselines across the agentic lifecycle.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing architectural threat models, privacy-preserving execution patterns, builder security guidelines, and baseline review processes across the agentic AI lifecycle [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. The group provides actionable security criteria and shared design patterns that enable multi-agent systems and tooling frameworks to mitigate systemic operational and privacy risks.

The working group coordinates with external ecosystem efforts—such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors standardization initiative and Linux Foundation Project Glasswing—to integrate runtime mediation hooks and defense mechanisms into standardized agent architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's purview and deliverables are structured across five primary workstreams scheduled for an initial 3–6 month delivery horizon [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:

1. **Taxonomy**: A living reference document standardizing terminology related to agent security, boundaries, and threat surfaces, feeding directly into the foundation-wide effort curated by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
2. **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: A comparative research initiative ([Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)) evaluating existing frameworks (such as OWASP and NIST) against agent-native attack surfaces, including expanded lethal trifecta dynamics, memory store poisoning, identity delegation, and weight plasticity [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns**: A builder-oriented catalog ([Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md)) defining concrete patterns for human-in-the-loop authorization, runtime interceptor hooks, semantic constraints, and privacy-preserving execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
4. **Agentic Security Best Practices**: Practical operational guidance ([Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)) addressing baseline security hygiene, secrets management, and safe external tool invocation for agent builders [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
5. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: An operational evaluation checklist ([Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)) inspired by IETF review workflows, assisting peer working groups in identifying architectural security and privacy implications early in their lifecycles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-04-14, the working group held a formal vote unanimously approving its operational charter, scope of purview, and five initial deliverables for the 3–6 month horizon [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. Formal ratification of the charter and deliverable ownership is slated for presentation to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative research deliverable evaluating traditional cybersecurity frameworks against agentic attack surfaces, lethal trifecta dynamics, and shared memory vulnerabilities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a research deliverable initiated by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to assess existing cybersecurity methodologies against unique agentic operational vulnerabilities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. The analysis evaluates established frameworks from OWASP, NIST, and CSA MAESTRO to identify coverage gaps in multi-agent environments and determine requirements for a dedicated agentic threat modeling framework [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Architecture / Specification
The gap analysis investigates threat dimensions specific to autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:

- **Modernized Lethal Trifecta**: Extending classic vulnerability models to capture complex multi-agent environments involving overlapping internal/external trust boundaries, cross-session identity delegation, and shared persistent memory stores [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- **Adaptive and Plastic Neural Architectures**: Examining forward-looking threat vectors stemming from models with learning plasticity or runtime weight adaptations that create non-static execution behaviors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- **Framework Differentiation**: Identifying domain-specific boundaries that distinguish agentic threat modeling from general application and LLM security paradigms (such as standard OWASP Top 10 or NIST AI RMF) rather than duplicating existing work [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Lifecycle History
The deliverable was unanimously approved as part of the initial five-deliverable 3–6 month roadmap during the Security and Privacy Working Group meeting on 2026-04-14, preceding formal charter presentation to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate formal unanimous WG approval and IETF-inspired cross-review workflow scope from the April 14, 2026 meeting.

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Working Group Security Review Checklist
proposed_concept.description: Operational review checklist and intake framework guiding early identification of security and privacy implications across AAIF working group deliverables.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Cross-Working Group Security Review Checklist is an operational evaluation instrument developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to ensure peer working groups identify and address security and privacy implications early in their specification lifecycles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. Modeled on proven IETF review conventions, the checklist serves as a self-assessment and triage mechanism to engage security reviews prior to final specification releases [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Architecture / Specification
The checklist defines early review triggers across specification, standard, and pattern proposals [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:

- **Early Engagement Triggers**: Criteria identifying when external tool execution, cross-boundary protocol handoffs, credential transit, or multi-agent memory sharing mandate SP WG consultation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- **Review Service Evolution**: Establishes a lightweight self-service boundary checklist intended to scale toward formal security and privacy review services across AAIF workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Lifecycle History
The checklist was formally voted on and unanimously approved as an initial 3–6 month deliverable during the Security and Privacy Working Group meeting on 2026-04-14, pending charter confirmation by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem catalog and open-source map tracking agentic AI projects, member initiatives, and open standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive visual catalog and open-source map providing visibility into prominent agentic AI software projects, frameworks, open standards, and foundation members[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Maintained in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape focuses specifically on open-source implementations and open standards, excluding closed-source products and proprietary commercial distributions[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Generator Engine and Data Sources
The landscape compilation pipeline is powered by the CNCF Landscape2 engine (`cncf/landscape2`)[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Canonical metadata and project entries are stored alphabetically in `landscape.yml`, accompanied by vector logos stored in the repository's `hosted_logos` directory[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Organizational and funding context is enriched via Crunchbase under Linux Foundation Data Access Terms[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

## Inclusion and Entry Criteria
Submissions to the landscape must satisfy explicit community and technical requirements[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:
- **Open-Source Stance**: Only open-source projects and open standards are eligible. Closed-source products, proprietary standards, and commercial wrappers of open-source software are excluded[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Adoption Threshold**: Open-source repositories must demonstrate clear community traction, generally requiring at least 1,000 GitHub stars[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Single Category Assignment**: Each organization's project is placed into a single primary category representing its principal offering to prevent duplicate listings across multiple sections[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Trademark and Ownership Attribution**: Crunchbase profiles must match the governing organization or trademark holder controlling the project[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Asset Standards**: Logos must be submitted in SVG format with English typography, using stacked orientations when multiple variants exist, and maintaining non-reversed, non-transparent background color schemes[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

## Publication Cadence
The landscape is generated daily, ensuring approved pull request contributions deploy to the production site within 24 hours of merge[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat models, security design patterns, privacy engineering guidelines, and protocol-level boundary defenses for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to establishing threat models, privacy-preserving architectures, and security engineering guidelines across autonomous AI agents and execution environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Operating under the technical governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group standardizes runtime boundary defenses, secret isolation, memory privacy, and cross-framework threat mitigations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Key Initiatives and Scope

## Threat Modeling and Defensive Patterns
The working group curates systematic vulnerability taxonomies and design patterns addressing threats unique to autonomous systems, such as tool poisoning, contextual data leakage, and untrusted execution surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. These deliverables coordinate closely with resources such as the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md) and cross-working-group security review checklists [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

## Protocol Boundary Security
The working group evaluates the architectural and security implications of emerging agent protocols and extensions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Specific tracking initiatives include Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors—which introduce interception hooks for data redaction and privacy enforcement—and MCP Apps, which bridge dynamic UI rendering into host agent contexts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

## Cross-Working Group Taxonomy Collaboration
In alignment with foundation leadership, the SP WG established taxonomy as the first foundational cross-working group collaboration deliverable [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. The SP WG's existing draft security and privacy vocabulary was selected as the foundational baseline across peer groups, coordinating with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to harmonize definitions across all AAIF workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Governance and Operations

## Charter Review Status
The formal working group charter was submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in April 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. While platform service interruptions affected formal quorum during the initial review, the charter received affirmative votes without substantive scope objections, and the working group proceeds under consensus approval [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

## Operational Cadence
The working group operates under an asynchronous-first cadence supported by self-organizing workstreams for specific deliverables, transitioning bi-weekly all-hands meetings into concise coordination checkpoints across global time zones [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing technical vision, project lifecycles, and working group charters.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), responsible for steering foundation-wide technical architecture, approving project lifecycle transitions, and chartering working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. The committee provides administrative oversight and review gates ensuring that open-source initiatives and standards groups adhere to foundation principles and member consensus [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5][^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

# Responsibilities and Authority

## Working Group Chartering and Intake
Working groups seeking official recognition within the AAIF must submit formal charters to the Technical Committee for review and voting [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Intake for candidate working groups is managed through standardized repository issue templates under `aaif/working-group-proposals`, requiring submitter affiliation with an AAIF member organization and membership tier declaration [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-1][^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]. Formal Technical Committee review cycles for newly submitted working group proposals begin on June 1, 2026 [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

## Technical Lifecycle and Project Stewardship
The Technical Committee enforces project milestone progression under the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) and [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. It also arbitrates cross-group alignment, establishing foundational inter-group efforts such as the cross-working-group taxonomy initiative launched with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Leadership
Executive technical direction for the foundation is stewarded by the AAIF Chief Technology Officer (CTO) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. As of April 2026, Manik serves as the AAIF CTO, succeeding initial CTO Matt [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral specifications, authority delegation chains, and cross-organizational trust models for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body advancing vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and architectural viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Its purpose is to ensure that agents can be discovered across disparate platforms and prove their identity, operator lineage, authority chains, and associated human approvals across organizational boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's charter defines six core technical domains and explicit operational boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:

- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: Mechanisms for establishing agent identity, runtime authentication handshakes, and verifiable software context provenance [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- **Delegation and Authority Chains**: Data models representing agents acting on behalf of humans, organizations, roles, services, or processes, including boundaries on delegated authority [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- **Authorization and Consent Models**: Short-lived, fine-grained authorization patterns, policy-as-code constraints, and recorded human approval records [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust**: Verification frameworks allowing receiving systems to evaluate external agents and confirm execution permissions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- **Agent Discovery and Trust-Relevant Metadata**: Descriptive metadata schemas supporting interoperability, trust bootstrapping, and coordination with [../standards/agent-identity-primitives.md](../standards/agent-identity-primitives.md) and [observability-and-traceability.md](observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- **Deployment Scenarios**: Architectural coverage across both enterprise multi-tenant systems and consumer agent environments [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

Out-of-scope activities include ratifying formal specifications as a standards development organization, defining general execution security architectures (delegated to [security-and-privacy.md](security-and-privacy.md)), and building production-grade identity infrastructure or centralized certification programs [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Lifecycle History

The working group operates under the leadership of Grant Miller as Working Group Chair and Primary Contact [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. The working group maintains coordination with [../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md](attestation-and-evidence.md) on evidence representation and [../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md](security-and-privacy.md) on threat models [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical coordination working group establishing common telemetry conventions, cross-framework agent tracing, and accountability specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to establish shared visibility and telemetry conventions for AI agent execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Operating primarily as an ecosystem coordination forum rather than an isolated standards body, the working group aligns fragmented tracing initiatives across OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context to solve multi-turn workflow auditing, content lineage, and cross-framework vendor lock-in [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group executes against core architectural mandates and focus areas [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]:

- **Coordinate First, Specify Only When Necessary**: Defaulting to aligning with and contributing upstream to established specifications; new work is initiated only when documented gap analyses prove existing bodies do not cover required agent capabilities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Session and Workflow Level Traceability**: Extending observability beyond isolated LLM request/response spans into holistic multi-turn conversations, tool invocations, and multi-modal state transitions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Founding Focus Area**: Developing the [../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) to define common agent execution entities, operational lifecycle events, and telemetry correlation models [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Lifecycle History

The working group charter was ratified internally by the working group on 2026-04-15 and approved under AAIF governance on 2026-05-13 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. The working group is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra and collaborates closely with [identity-and-trust.md](identity-and-trust.md) and [../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md](accuracy-and-reliability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure governing project proposal intake, technical evaluation, Contribution Agreements, and intake form requirements.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Proposal Process governs the intake, technical evaluation, and admission reviews for open-source software projects seeking formal hosting under the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. The procedure establishes standardized submission channels, triage gates, and alignment with the [project-lifecycle-policy.md](project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Architecture / Specification

Project proposals are submitted through structured issue forms maintained in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. The intake form distinguishes between mandatory criteria and optional maturity disclosures [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]:

- **Mandatory Requirements**: Submission of core project details, codebase licensing verification, governance structure, and alignment with AAIF foundation goals [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].
- **Optional Disclosures**: In strict alignment with the [project-lifecycle-policy.md](project-lifecycle-policy.md), publishing a forward-looking roadmap and achieving an OpenSSF Best Practices badge are classified as optional fields [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Early-stage and sandbox applicants are not blocked from proposal submission if these badges or roadmaps are not yet finalized [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Lifecycle History

Following community observation that proposal forms blocked early-stage applicants by marking policy-optional fields as mandatory, PR #23 updated the proposal configuration to designate roadmap and OpenSSF badge fields as explicitly optional [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Intake reviews are conducted under the purview of the [../governance/technical-committee.md](../governance/technical-committee.md).

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat models, architectural design patterns, containment controls, and privacy standards for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPAA) operates within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) to establish security and privacy as a shared, ecosystem-wide discipline across agentic architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. Formed to address challenges that traditional security frameworks fail to adequately resolve—such as prompt injection, confused deputy scenarios, authorization boundary violations, tool invocation risks, and agent memory vulnerabilities—the working group produces open threat models, taxonomies, and reusable design patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope Boundaries

The working group's scope covers five core technical areas [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]:

- **Threat Modeling and Attack Analysis:** Identifying failure and adversarial modes across single-agent and multi-agent systems.
- **Security Architecture and Design Patterns:** Producing hardened, reusable patterns such as those cataloged in `../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md`.
- **Agent Control and Containment:** Defining sandboxing, runtime boundary controls, and containment strategies.
- **Data Protection and Privacy:** Establishing privacy-preserving mechanisms for autonomous workflows handling sensitive data across services.
- **Cross-WG Collaboration:** Providing security reviews via instruments like the `../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md`.

Explicitly excluded from scope are ethics and value-judgment questions (deferred to governance bodies), prescriptive interpretations of regulatory compliance, and formal certification programs for agentic software [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

## Governance and Operations

The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. Operations rely on open biweekly meetings, consensus-driven decision-making with fallback to simple majority voting (subject to a 51% quorum threshold), and formal escalation to the `../governance/technical-committee.md` when consensus cannot be reached [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

# Lifecycle History

Formally chartered and approved on May 13, 2026, the group was initialized through draft PR#1 and formalized in charter documentation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

proposed_concept.title: Blog Content Intake and Publication Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Editorial intake standards, contributor eligibility criteria, review workflows, and timeline rules governing publications on aaif.io.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) blog serves as a central editorial channel on aaif.io for sharing educational, vendor-neutral technical content, release updates, and case studies across the agentic AI community [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]. Managed end-to-end by the Linux Foundation team, content publication operates under a standard two-week intake review lead time and requires stakeholder pre-approval before intake [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Contributor Eligibility and Content Scope

Submissions are accepted from five distinct contributor categories [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]:

- **Member Companies:** Permitted vendor-neutral articles with a maximum of one or two closing sentences containing a single external link.
- **Project Maintainers and Contributors:** Announcements and technical deep-dives for hosted projects including Model Context Protocol (MCP), `../resources/goose.md`, and AGENTS.md.
- **Working Groups and Technical Committee:** Official updates co-authored with or endorsed by AAIF technical working groups or the `../governance/technical-committee.md`.
- **Community Contributors:** Open community technical posts, limited to two submissions per month.
- **Event Participants:** Recaps and learnings from foundation-affiliated hackathons and community programs.

## Editorial Standards and Intake Workflow

Submissions must follow narrative prose rather than marketing copy or press releases, adhere to vendor neutrality, reflect developments from the past two months, and avoid criticism of open-source projects [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]. The workflow proceeds through submission via the official form, intake triage, review, optional revision loops, scheduling, and publication [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]. Contributors can prepare and validate their submissions locally using the `../skills/aaif-blog-guidelines.md` agent skill [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c][^evt-foundation-pr-2].

# Lifecycle History

Established under foundation policy guidelines and augmented in PR#2 with automated authoring guidance via the `aaif-blog-guidelines` skill [^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c][^evt-foundation-pr-2].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Blog Guidelines Skill
proposed_concept.description: Procedural agent skill packaging AAIF editorial guidelines, story evaluation workflows, neutrality enforcement, and submission packaging.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-blog-guidelines` skill is an automated agent skill maintained under the AAIF public agents registry to assist contributors in drafting, reviewing, neutralizing, and packaging blog content for aaif.io [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]. Distributed for global execution via npx, the skill operationalizes the foundation's content intake policy and ensures compliance with editorial constraints prior to human submission [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-pr-2].

# Architecture / Specification

## Skill Definition and Metadata

Configured as version 1.0 authored by Angie Jones, the skill references `../guidelines/blog-guidelines.md` as its normative foundation [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]. It provides prompt instructions and validation criteria covering release posts for hosted projects like MCP, `../resources/goose.md`, and AGENTS.md, as well as community tutorials and case studies [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed].

## Agent Execution Workflow

The skill guides agents through a seven-step procedure [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]:

1. **Clarify the story:** Identify target audience, news value, and publication timeline.
2. **Check eligibility:** Verify contributor class, pre-existing internal approvals, and draft originality.
3. **Shape the post:** Structure content around narrative progression (recommended 600–1,500 words) instead of promotional summaries.
4. **Enforce neutrality:** Strip promotional prose, vendor bias, and comparative superiority claims.
5. **Strengthen utility:** Embed concrete technical examples and lessons learned.
6. **Package submission:** Compile author bios, headshots, metadata, social amplification copy, and submission links.
7. **Set expectations:** Communicate review timelines (standard two-week lead time) to contributors.

# Lifecycle History

Version 1.0 released in `aaif/public-agents` and cross-referenced in foundation repository guidelines [^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-pr-2].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining threat models, architectural design patterns, runtime containment controls, and security review baselines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group responsible for establishing threat models, architectural design patterns, runtime containment controls, and security review baselines across agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab] The working group focuses on mitigating autonomous execution vulnerabilities, standardizing boundary defenses such as hooks and interceptors, and equipping Foundation projects with actionable review checklists.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]

# Workstreams and Deliverables

The working group organizes execution through specialized workstreams that coordinate asynchronously in dedicated channels and present progress during all-hands sessions:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]

- **Threat Modeling and Gap Analysis**: Primary near-term deliverable evaluating conventional security frameworks against agentic architectural vectors; tracked in [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Technical reference standardizing concrete runtime controls, interceptor hooks, checkpoints, and anti-patterns; tracked in [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: High-level guidance companion to the patterns catalog advising builders on architectural guardrails and cryptographic boundaries; tracked in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Early operational checklist socialized with other working group chairs to seed security and privacy evaluations across all AAIF deliverables; tracked in [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
- **Taxonomy Initiative**: Security terminology efforts contributed directly into the foundation-wide cross-working group initiative curated under [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]

# External Coordination

The working group maintains proactive alignment with adjacent ecosystem standards and bodies to ensure unified security messaging across the industry:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]

- **AARM Alignment**: Liaison with Vanta regarding the AARM standard to unify industry compliance baselines.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: Joint collaboration across the MCP ACS and MCP Apps groups to standardize generalized interceptor hook semantics and error propagation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]
- **Government and Public Frameworks**: Continuous synthesis of published guidance from CISA and upstream cybersecurity authorities.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]

# Lifecycle History

Formal voting on the Security and Privacy Working Group charter was migrated from GitHub pull requests to the Linux Foundation LFX platform for official ratification.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive CNCF Landscape 2 ecosystem catalog and architecture map tracking open-source agent runtimes, protocols, member projects, and curated watchlists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Ecosystem Architecture Map is an interactive, CNCF Landscape 2 market map and catalog categorizing open-source agent runtimes, communication protocols, security guardrails, observability platforms, agentic commerce rails, and global regulatory frameworks [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. Managed in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape visualizes project maturity, organizational relationships, and ecosystem momentum across emerging agentic technologies [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape is built on the CNCF Landscape 2 framework (`cncf/landscape2`), consuming declarative YAML configuration files to build a client-side card and grid view [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]:

- **Configuration and Schema Structure**: The catalog is governed by `landscape.yml` (project entries and category trees), `settings.yml` (branding, color palettes, and tier definitions), and a `hosted_logos` repository asset directory [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].
- **Project Tiers and Member Decoupling**: Project entries are classified across four defined tiers: `Graduated` (`#00f5d4`), `Incubating` (`#9b5de5`), `Member` (`#00b4d8`), and `External` (`#f15bb5`) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. The schema decouples member organizations from software projects using category grouping, enabling member projects to be highlighted without conflating organizational membership with software lifecycle status [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
- **Agentic AI Project Watchlist**: A dedicated watchlist section tracks leading open-source agentic AI software repositories and correlates ecosystem adoption with the Linux Foundation LFX Insights Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
- **Automated Validation and PR Previews**: Continuous integration runs `cncf/landscape2-validate-action@v2` across `landscape.yml` and `settings.yml` on all pull requests and merge groups [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340]. Pull request workflows generate interactive preview comments utilizing overlay parameters on `https://aaif.landscape2.io` to inspect proposed dataset and visual changes prior to merge [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].

# Lifecycle History

Initial deployment was staged under the `ws-taxonomy-landscape` repository as a GitHub Pages export [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. Governance and hosting transitioned to the dedicated `aaif-landscape` repository, introducing automated schema validation actions, PR preview comment automation, member-project grouping decoupling, and the curated OSS project watchlist [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340] [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00] [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Operational intake requirements, submitter eligibility rules, and required proposal sections for chartering new AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines govern the intake, structural requirements, and evaluation criteria for proposing new technical and policy working groups within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Working groups are time-bound collaborations convened to address industry challenges, formulate open standards, and develop guidance aligned with the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Architecture / Specification

Prospective working group proposals must satisfy mandatory intake constraints prior to formal review [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]:

- **Submitter Eligibility**: Submissions are strictly restricted to Foundation Member organizations in good standing across any membership level [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Proposals submitted by non-members are rejected without review [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
- **Mandatory Proposal Sections**:
  1. *Submitter Information*: Full name, organizational affiliation, leadership availability, contact email, and membership tier [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  2. *Working Group Identity*: Concise working group name and an accessible one-sentence summary of scope [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  3. *Problem Statement & Purpose*: Demonstration of relevance to agentic AI, articulation of gaps or opportunities, and alignment with foundation priorities [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  4. *Proposed Scope & Deliverables*: Defined outputs such as whitepapers, normative specifications, benchmarks, datasets, reference implementations, or regulatory recommendations [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  5. *Timeline & Structure*: Meeting cadence and projected duration, structured around a standard 12–24 month charter lifecycle [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  6. *Membership & Expertise*: Target stakeholder profiles, necessary subject-matter expertise, and confirmed participants or interested organizations [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  7. *Impact & Urgency*: Assessment of ecosystem timing and risks of inaction [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
  8. *Resource Considerations*: Tooling, compute, repository, or hosting requirements needed to execute the charter [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Lifecycle History

Published in March 2026 under the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository, formalizing member intake criteria, submission structure, and review gates [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol alignments, and lifecycle interfaces across agentic discovery, checkout, payments, and post-purchase flows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) aligns and harmonizes open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows executed by AI agents on behalf of individuals, enterprises, and software systems [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, the working group was formally approved on May 15, 2026, to provide interoperability guidance across agent-initiated transactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. The group does not author competing payment or commerce protocols; instead, it establishes reference architectures and interoperability bridges for recommendation to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Scope and Deliverables
The working group investigates interfaces, signaling models, and governance boundaries connecting agentic workflows to commercial infrastructure [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]:
- **Discovery & Negotiation**: Interfaces enabling agents and merchants to query offers, item availability, fulfillment parameters, and contractual terms [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Cart & Checkout**: Schemas and handoff conventions managing cart composition, validation, and multi-party checkout sequences [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. See [agentic-checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md).
- **Identity & Delegated Authority**: Cryptographic conveyance of buyer identity, consent tokens, and authority constraints, coordinated with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Agentic Payments**: Interoperability signaling between agents, digital wallets, and payment rails (including card, real-time, and on-chain rails) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. See [delegated-payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md) and [agent-initiated-transaction](../taxonomy/agent-initiated-transaction.md).
- **Risk and Post-Purchase Signals**: Structured signals for risk posture, fraud signaling, order tracking, and dispute/chargeback initiation [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Human-in-the-Loop Safeguards**: Escalation triggers, confirmation boundaries, and explicit autonomy levels for financial commitments [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. See [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).

Internal rail mechanics, merchant fraud mitigation engine execution, end-user terminal hardware, and foundational societal AI policies remain explicitly out of scope [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was officially approved on May 15, 2026, under the primary leadership of Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group defines threat models, architectural security patterns, runtime containment baselines, and review checklists across the Agentic AI Foundation. With its formal charter approved in May 2026, the working group provides foundational security controls, architectural guardrails, and risk assessments for agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical portfolio into four primary deliverable streams staffed by self-selected workstream leads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]:
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Assesses traditional application security and AI model safeguards against autonomous multi-step agent failure modes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. See [agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Establishes implementation guidance for host sandboxing, secrets management, and runtime privilege reduction [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. See [agentic-ai-security-best-practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Formulates reusable architectural templates for verifiable authorization, runtime attestation, and data isolation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. See [security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md).
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Operates an intake evaluation protocol to ensure emerging foundation specifications and reference architectures undergo systematic risk reviews [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. See [cross-wg-security-review-checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).

# Lifecycle History
On May 26, 2026, the working group confirmed that its charter had been formally approved [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. Initial deliverable completion targets were shifted back by one month to adjust for charter review timing, and workstreams adopted self-selecting channel lead models [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative standardizing agentic AI vocabulary and curating an architectural catalog of open-source agent runtimes, frameworks, and developer tools. Junjie Bu serves as co-chair of the Taxonomy workstream and chair of the Landscape workstream, ensuring consistent definitions across sister working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group manages two complementary foundational deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]:
- **Universal Taxonomy**: Maintains normative terminology definitions and automated validation schemas for agent capabilities, boundaries, and failure modes across groups such as [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md) and [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. See [taxonomy-contribution-guide](../guidelines/taxonomy-contribution-guide.md).
- **Agentic AI Landscape**: Organizes open-source projects across orchestration frameworks, agent sandboxes, and developer tooling within an interactive ecosystem map [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. See [agentic-ai-landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md).

Operations are conducted asynchronously via pull requests, complemented by weekly 30-minute coordination syncs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Lifecycle History
In May 2026, Junjie Bu was appointed co-chair of the Taxonomy workstream and chair of the Landscape workstream, aligning taxonomy definitions directly with cross-working-group threat modeling and tooling catalogs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining technical project maturity stages, entry gates, annual health reviews, and acceptance criteria for AAIF open technical projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy governs how open technical projects formally enter, progress through, and retire within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Ratified with an effective date of March 18, 2026, the policy outlines submission requirements, maturity stages, and annual review mechanics overseen by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Proposal Requirements
Candidate projects apply through the AAIF project proposals repository by submitting an architectural intake packet detailing [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- Project mission statement and alignment with AAIF objectives [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Production adoption evidence and representative use cases [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Technical Committee mentor or sponsor, when identified [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- OSI-approved permissive licensing terms and third-party license audits [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Public repositories, transparent release processes, automated validation pipelines, and public issue trackers [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- Documented governance models, maintainer leadership structures, and public communication channels [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

## Maturity Stages
The policy structures project progression across three defined stages [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- **Growth Stage**: Entry tier for promising early-stage technologies and initial implementations building ecosystem traction and seeking formal alignment [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Impact Stage**: Established tier for production-hardened projects with multi-organizational contributor diversity, robust governance, and widespread production adoption [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Emeritus Stage**: Retirement tier for projects that are no longer actively maintained or have concluded their architectural utility [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171][^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

## Annual Review Process
Projects undergo an annual review by the Technical Committee to assess operational health, community growth, governance adherence, and eligibility for stage graduation [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Lifecycle History
The policy took effect on March 18, 2026, establishing standardized governance tiers and proposal intake channels for AAIF projects [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Editorial clarifications to the Emeritus definition were integrated via PR #30 [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure governing intake, technical review, voting thresholds, status tracking, and reapplication for foundation-hosted projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process defines the operating procedure and intake requirements for open-source initiatives seeking to become hosted projects under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Administered via structured issue templates and tracked on a public project board, the evaluation framework routes proposals through review presentations and formal voting by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to classify accepted software into the Growth or Impact stages of the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Intake and Review Workflow
The application process requires candidate maintainers to complete a defined four-step progression[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6][^evt-project-proposals-pr-35]:
1. **Submission Guidance**: Applicants consult foundation guidance regarding project criteria and hosting benefits prior to submission[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6][^evt-project-proposals-pr-35].
2. **Application Filing**: Submissions are filed as a Project Proposal Application issue covering project governance, licensing, and architectural scope[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
3. **Triage and Presentation Preparation**: The submission enters the project backlog on the public tracking board; submitters collaborate with AAIF staff to prepare a formal technical presentation[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
4. **Technical Committee Hearing**: The project is presented during a scheduled public TC meeting for live evaluation and questioning[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Evaluation and Voting Rules
During scheduled meetings, the Technical Committee evaluates candidate proposals against baseline project health and relevance criteria[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- **Maturity Classification**: The TC assesses whether the project enters as a Growth or Impact project[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Voting Threshold**: Acceptance requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) of all seated members of the Technical Committee[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Governing Board Referral**: Projects approved by the TC are formally referred to the AAIF Governing Board for final administrative sign-off[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Application Status Tracking
Project issues on the tracking board are categorized using five standardized labels[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- `New`: The application has been submitted and sits in the backlog awaiting initial triage[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- `Approved`: The application has been accepted into foundation hosting by majority TC vote and board approval[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- `Declined`: The proposal was declined; detailed feedback and rationales are documented in issue comments[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- `Waiting on Comment`: Reviewers have requested supplementary information or technical clarity from maintainers[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- `Too Early`: The project is premature for hosted status, and reviewers provide guidance on milestones needed for reapplication[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Reapplication Timelines and Membership Neutrality
- **Reapplication Cooldown**: Projects that are declined may submit a new application as soon as 3 months following the vote, provided maintainers demonstrate tangible progress resolving prior review feedback[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Membership Neutrality**: Sponsoring organizations and maintainers are not required to hold corporate membership in the AAIF to contribute or host a project[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Governance Boundary**: Project acceptance does not confer foundation membership tiers (such as Silver, Gold, or Platinum) or seat representatives on the Governing Board[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# References
- AAIF Project Proposals Repository: `https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals`
- AAIF Project Submission Guide: `https://aaif.io/blog/how-to-submit-your-project-to-the-aaif/`
