proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy catalog and ecosystem landscape mapping agentic frameworks, protocols, security tooling, and working group alignments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an open ecosystem catalog and architectural map tracking open-source agent runtimes, orchestration engines, communication protocols, security guardrails, and regulatory frameworks across the AI agent domain[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]. Curated under the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape groups technologies into seven functional categories mapped to the corresponding technical working groups of the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Architecture / Specification

## Category Taxonomy and Working Group Alignments
The landscape establishes seven primary operational categories[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:
1. **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**: Captures autonomous agent frameworks (including AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenHands, and ADK) and cyclical orchestration runtimes (including LangChain, LlamaIndex, Dapr, and LangGraph), aligned with the [Workflows & Process Integration WG](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) and [Accuracy & Reliability WG](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
2. **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Tracks inter-agent communication protocols, discovery directories, and routing registries, aligned with the [Identity & Trust WG](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
3. **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Catalogs prompt firewalls, runtime policy enforcers, and execution sandboxes, aligned with the [Security & Privacy WG](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
4. **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Covers distributed tracing engines, telemetry exporters, and profilers, aligned with the [Observability & Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
5. **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Catalogs autonomous commercial transaction protocols, settlement layers, and payment delegation tooling, aligned with the [Agentic Commerce WG](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
6. **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Tracks compliance tooling, AI governance benchmarks, and regulatory mapping frameworks, aligned with the [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment WG](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
7. **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Catalogs automated regression testbeds, reliability suites, and agent evaluation harnesses, aligned with the [Accuracy & Reliability WG](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

## Catalog Item Schema
Entries in `landscape.yml` are structured with standardized attributes including item name, homepage URL, source repository URL, logo asset path, descriptive summary, and project designation distinguishing foundation member contributions (`member`) from external community solutions (`external`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# References
- AAIF Landscape Source: `https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape/blob/main/landscape/landscape.yml`

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body responsible for defining agent-specific threat models, runtime containment baselines, cross-working group security review checklists, and reusable architectural design patterns.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa] The working group coordinates security posture assessments and policy evaluations across AAIF initiatives.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical program across four primary workstreams alongside cross-foundation delegates:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]

- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing operational intake and review standards for AAIF initiatives (see `../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md`).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Matthew Khouzam and Fernando Lucktemberg, maintaining builder guidance on runtime sandboxing, secrets management, and context redaction (see `../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating traditional cybersecurity frameworks against agentic attack vectors (see `../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md`).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Sagar Dashora and Dan Kommatas, cataloging vendor-neutral security and privacy design patterns (see `../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md`).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Jay White and Katherine Druckman serve as the designated delegates representing Security and Privacy within the cross-cutting workstream (see `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-09**: Confirmed workstream leadership slates, appointed Taxonomy/Landscape delegates, evaluated LFX meeting self-service tooling, and adopted asynchronous monthly reporting to the Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase).[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e] The working group analyzes global AI policy developments, regulatory compliance requirements, and risk management frameworks applicable to autonomous agents and multi-agent systems.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group operates under the governance oversight of the Technical Committee (see `../governance/technical-committee.md`) and submits monthly progress reports using a standardized reporting specification (see `../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md`):[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]

- **Reporting Cadence and Path**: Reports are filed at `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` via pull requests titled `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>` by the last business day of the reporting month.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
- **Review Cycle**: The Technical Committee reviews reports asynchronously during a 7-calendar-day window, merging upon sign-off or window conclusion.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
- **Standard Deliverable Structure**: Reports capture Summary, Progress Against Objectives, Blockers and Risks, Decisions Needed from the TC, Next Month's Focus, and Metrics / Links.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body led by Pavan that establishes vendor-neutral telemetry conventions, execution tracing standards, and protocol-level observability specifications across agent harnesses and multi-agent architectures.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group coordinates technical deliverables across dedicated focus groups and cross-workstream efforts:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]

- **Observability and Multi-Agentic Systems**: Led by Ty, conducting regular meetings to address orchestration tracking, distributed agent state, and multi-agent coordination telemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]
- **Observability and Protocols**: Led by Matthew, addressing wire-level protocols, boundary telemetry (including MCP and agent gateways), and cross-boundary context propagation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Coordinated by Pavan with Richard and Kevin, focusing on tracing cognitive cycles, intermediate decision steps, and deliberation chains.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Participating in the cross-working group effort coordinated by `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` to harmonize telemetry vocabulary and maintain asynchronous GitHub workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-11**: Transitioned working document drafting from Google Docs to GitHub pull requests and issues, instituted monthly reporting alignment with the Technical Committee, and established recurring focus group cadences.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template and Review Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Standardized reporting structure, timeline rules, and pull request workflow for AAIF working group monthly updates to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Reporting Template defines the standardized structure, delivery timeline, and pull request review workflow for monthly operational and technical updates submitted by AAIF working groups to the Technical Committee (TC).[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa] It establishes an asynchronous review model that provides TC visibility without turning updates into blocking operational bottlenecks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]

# Architecture / Specification
Working groups follow a uniform procedure when compiling and submitting monthly reports:[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]

## File Location and PR Convention
- **File path**: Reports are staged under `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` (e.g., `reporting/2026-06-report.md`).[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
- **PR Title**: Pull requests must be titled `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>` against the working group repository.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
- **Reviewers**: The pull request must assign the Technical Committee (or designated TC GitHub team) as reviewers.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]

## Review Timeline and Sign-off
- **Submission Deadline**: Reports are due by the last business day of the reporting month.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
- **Review Window**: The Technical Committee review window remains open for 7 calendar days following submission.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
- **Merge Criteria**: The pull request is merged once the TC explicitly signs off or when the 7-day review window closes, whichever occurs sooner.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]

## Required Report Sections
1. **Summary**: 2–3 sentences capturing the month's progress at a glance.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
2. **Progress Against Objectives**: Concrete milestones shipped or advanced against chartered deliverables.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
3. **Blockers and Risks**: External dependencies, governance blockers, or technical risks requiring TC awareness.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
4. **Decisions Needed from the TC**: Explicit, action-oriented requests for Technical Committee decision or guidance.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
5. **Next Month's Focus**: Top 2–3 prioritized objectives planned for the coming cycle.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
6. **Metrics / Links**: References to merged pull requests, published deliverables, meeting minutes, and tracked issues.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Adopted across AAIF working groups to establish uniform asynchronous reporting to the Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-pr-4][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining threat models, architectural design patterns, runtime containment, and security governance for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an AAIF technical body tasked with establishing threat models, architectural design patterns, runtime sandboxing requirements, and practical defense guidance across agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]. Operating under draft charter governance, the working group coordinates workstreams addressing threat modeling, design pattern catalogs, and best practice standards for autonomous and multi-agent deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical activities across dedicated repository directories:
- `charter/`: Contains the working group charter, maintained under draft status until formal committee ratification[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423].
- `deliverables/`: Houses all published deliverables, adhering to strict lifecycle progression rules[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]. New deliverables begin in `Draft` with a `DRAFT-` filename prefix. Transition to `Final` status requires an explicit approval decision recorded in meeting notes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]. Deliverables transitioned to cross-WG initiatives adopt a `Moved` redirect state[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- `meeting-notes/`: Chronological records capturing discussed topics, decisions, deliverables, and action items in `YYYY-MM-DD.md` format[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-eb9c68e792e7-3538ca31].
- `workstreams/threat-modeling/`: Houses the threat modeling gap analysis co-led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), evaluating CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF frameworks against agentic vulnerabilities[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-06-22, the working group transitioned its foundational deliverable, the Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions, to the cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape workstream ([`../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)) to maintain agentic terminology across all AAIF initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

mutations.rationale: Update threat modeling deliverable with workstream co-leads, participating member organizations, and target evaluation framework scope.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Working group research deliverable evaluating existing threat model frameworks against agentic AI vulnerabilities and supply-chain integrity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design is an active research workstream and deliverable of the AAIF Security and Privacy Working Group ([`../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)) evaluating whether existing AI cybersecurity frameworks adequately address agent-specific operational and structural threats[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. The project assesses industry threat models—including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF—to identify structural gaps and determine whether a novel threat modeling framework is necessary for agentic architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Architecture / Specification
The gap analysis investigates vulnerability vectors unique to agentic deployments, including multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation abuse, delegated authorization boundaries, and supply-chain integrity spanning system prompts, model provenance, and tool manifest verification[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. The findings serve as foundational input into downstream deliverables, specifically the Design Patterns Catalog ([`security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md`](security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md)) and the Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide ([`../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

The workstream is co-led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), with cross-industry contributions from participants representing Capsule, Twilio, Semiotic AI, IBM, Global Payments, Huawei, Ericsson, and TELUS[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate the formalized workstream structure, workstream leadership, and taxonomy elevation into the cross-WG effort established in PR #5.

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining threat models, architectural design patterns, runtime containment, and security best practices for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body dedicated to defining threat models, architectural design patterns, runtime containment mechanisms, and practical builder guidance for secure and privacy-respecting agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. The group structures its technical agenda across targeted workstreams and conducts cross-foundation security reviews of other AAIF deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams
The working group organizes its ongoing technical work into specialized workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:

- **Threat Modeling**: Evaluates gaps in existing AI threat frameworks (including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) specifically against agentic threats, serving as the foundational deliverable feeding downstream workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].
- **[Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md)**: Curates reusable, implementation-neutral design patterns across hooks, human-in-the-loop controls, privacy-preserving execution, blast radius containment, secure memory lifecycles, and runtime intervention[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].
- **[Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)**: Provides practical builder guidance on secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. Led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].
- **[Cross-WG Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)**: Establishes a lightweight operational process for evaluating other AAIF working groups' specifications and architectures through a security and privacy lens[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].
- **Taxonomy**: Originally incubated within the SP WG, this workstream has been merged into the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Lifecycle History
The working group initially drafted a standalone security and privacy taxonomy before elevating the effort to an AAIF-wide initiative on 2026-05-12[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. On 2026-06-09, the SP WG named Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) as its permanent delegates to the cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape workstream[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Architectural catalog defining reusable, implementation-independent security and privacy design patterns for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is an Agentic AI Foundation deliverable curating reusable, implementation-independent architectural patterns for engineering secure, privacy-respecting agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Developed within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), each pattern uses a standardized problem, context, solution, and trade-offs structure, pairing solutions with known anti-patterns where relevant[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].

# Architecture / Specification

## Topic Areas
The catalog focuses on core architectural domains essential to agent containment and data protection[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]:
- **Hooks and Checkpointing**: Interception points for monitoring and validating agent operations before and after execution.
- **Human-in-the-Loop Patterns**: Governance controls and checkpoints requiring authorized human interaction for high-risk operations.
- **Privacy-Preserving Execution**: Cryptographic and hardware-enforced boundaries including zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs, trusted execution environments (TEEs), and encrypted vector databases.
- **Blast Radius Containment**: Architectural isolation limiting the scope and impact of potential agent compromise or failure.
- **Secure Memory and Lifecycle Management**: Retention policies, cryptographic deletion, and data sovereignty controls across agent conversation and state stores.
- **Agent Containment and Runtime Intervention**: Out-of-band intervention mechanisms including kill switches, transaction rollback, permission downgrades, and off-task drift detection.
- **Agent Authorization Models**: Fine-grained delegation, credential scoping, and principal-agent authority boundaries.

## Leadership and Contributors
The Design Patterns workstream is co-led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Contributing organizations include Bluerock, Circle, Ericsson, Global Payments, Huawei, IBM, JPMorgan Chase, and TELUS[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. The catalog is sequenced to consume threat inputs from the WG's threat modeling deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].

mutations.rationale: Record workstream leads, contributors, and the formal scope of topic areas defined in the best practices workstream README.

# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a practical, builder-focused manual authored by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. Whereas the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md) specifies structural implementations, this guide provides operational recommendations advising engineers on external frameworks, tooling configurations, and runtime safeguards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Focus Areas
The guide details actionable practices across five primary security disciplines[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]:
- **Secrets Management**: Safe provisioning, storage, runtime injection, and scoping of API keys and credentials used by autonomous agents.
- **Secure Tool Invocation**: Input validation, parameter sanitation, and execution sandboxing for external tool calls and subprocesses.
- **Guardrails**: Model-level and prompt-level boundaries filtering malicious instructions and preventing unauthorized capability usage.
- **Evaluation Frameworks**: Automated and continuous assessment pipelines for testing agent resilience against adversarial inputs and policy violations.
- **Post-Incident Forensics**: Auditing, logging, and trace analysis capabilities enabling investigation of compromised or drifting agents.
- **External Framework References**: Curated pointers to industry frameworks (such as OWASP, NIST AI RMF, and CSA MAESTRO) rather than re-deriving established baselines[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

## Leadership and Contributors
The workstream is led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. Contributing organizations include Bluerock, Capsule, Circle, Equinix, Global Payments, Huawei, IBM, JPMorgan Chase, Keycard, Lenovo, Ocean Security, SAP, TELUS, and Twilio[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative established to build common terminology, harmonize conflicting definitions, and curate the foundation-wide agentic ecosystem landscape[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. It maintains decoupled terminology data updated via pull requests in the `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` repository, with active delegate representation from across all AAIF technical working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Structure
The workstream operates under the leadership of Junjie Bu, who was appointed as chair on 2026-05-26[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Operational rhythms combine asynchronous pull-request reviews on GitHub with weekly 30-minute synchronization meetings[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

Working groups across AAIF designate active delegates to resolve cross-domain terminology conflicts and review contributions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]. For example, the [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) is represented by Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Lifecycle History
The taxonomy effort originally began within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) as a domain-specific draft[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. On 2026-05-12, the initiative was formally elevated to an AAIF-wide cross-working-group program to avoid divergent vocabularies across the foundation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Working groups subsequently appointed official delegates in June 2026 to govern ongoing dictionary reconciliation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with identifying architectural vulnerabilities, defining defense-in-depth threat models, and authoring reusable security baselines for autonomous and multi-agent systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# Operational Structure and Workstreams

The working group manages its deliverables and documentation openly on GitHub as its system of record, maintaining discrete sub-workstreams organized within repository directories:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, benchmarking threat models across industry frameworks (including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF) and analyzing risks such as memory poisoning, rogue agents, excessive agency, and commerce risks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, detailing practical implementation baselines for builders.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, curating reusable architectural mechanisms for runtime isolation and containment.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, providing an intake and review instrument across foundation working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Coordinated with the central [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) via delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman, incorporating agent archetypes and security terms into the foundation-wide taxonomy.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# External Liaisons

The working group actively liaises with external standards and security initiatives, including the OWASP Automated System Indicators (ASI) group, IETF security efforts, the Agentic Architecture Risk Model (AARM), and Model Context Protocol Access Control Specification (MCP ACS) bodies.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# Governance and Reporting

The working group provides monthly status reports to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) during the last week of each month, initiating a formal seven-day acknowledgment and question window.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body developing vendor-neutral telemetry conventions, event schemas, and behavioral trace models for observing agent execution, context propagation, and multi-agent coordination.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

# Focus Groups and Deliverables

The working group organizes its technical investigations across four dedicated focus groups:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

- **LLM Primitives**: Led by Zayne, conducting landscape surveys and gap analyses for underlying model calls and token-level operations, targeting alignment with OpenTelemetry conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]
- **Agent State and Context**: Led by Sergey and Govind, reviewing academic research and production implementations for tracking state changes and context management.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Investigating agent-to-agent interactions, workflow engines, and distributed agent boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Developing observability paradigms for internal reasoning steps, planning loops, and white-box tracing.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

# Taxonomy and Trace Model Alignment

The group maintains a draft taxonomy organized around four observable planes: orchestration, execution, protocol, and reasoning/context.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10] These planes are crosswalked to the core dimensions of the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) (execution structure, reasoning and planning, outcomes and effects) while preserving strict alignment guardrails with OpenTelemetry standards and coordinating with the central [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

# Operations and Governance

Co-chaired by Matt and Pavan, the group conducts bi-weekly meetings with community presentation slots, tracks deliverables via public GitHub Kanban boards, and reports monthly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4] The working group maintains Discord as its active chat platform.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification standardizing agent execution entities, turn boundaries, and behavioral dimensions across orchestration, execution, protocol, and reasoning planes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a candidate telemetry and behavioral correlation standard developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to capture structural, cognitive, and effect-oriented dimensions of AI agent runs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

# Architecture / Specification

The model establishes a crosswalk between four observable taxonomy planes and three core behavioral dimensions:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

- **Taxonomy Planes**: Orchestration, execution, protocol, and reasoning/context planes define the system boundaries across which agent actions and environment interactions occur.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]
- **Behavioral Dimensions**:
  - *Execution Structure*: Traces task dispatch, subprocess calls, tool boundaries, and multi-agent coordination.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]
  - *Reasoning and Planning*: Captures deliberative chains, reflection checkpoints, and decision state transitions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]
  - *Outcomes and Effects*: Records concrete state mutations, external tool effects, and verifiable task artifacts.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

The specification adheres to OpenTelemetry alignment guardrails, ensuring that defined terms represent AAIF extension concepts rather than duplicate replacements for established OTel distributed tracing semantics.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

# Lifecycle History

Under the working group's 12-month charter goals, the model is governed by an evaluation plan designed to determine whether to adopt an existing standard, extend an ongoing industry effort, or produce a de novo specification based on formal gap analysis and landscape survey results.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]

proposed_concept.description: Working group research deliverable evaluating existing threat model frameworks against agentic AI vulnerabilities, cross-framework coverage gaps, and mitigation architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a technical deliverable authored within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9] It benchmarks conventional cybersecurity and AI risk frameworks against the distinct failure modes and attack surfaces of autonomous agent systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# Architecture / Specification

The gap analysis evaluates comparative coverage and overlaps across four established frameworks:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

- **OWASP** (including Top 10 for LLMs and Automated System Indicators)
- **MITRE ATLAS** (Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems)
- **MAESTRO** (Multi-Agent Environment Security Threat Research and Operations)
- **NIST AI RMF** (Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework)

### Analyzed Risk Domains

The evaluation synthesizes findings across foundational and emergent agentic vulnerability classes:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

- Memory and context poisoning
- Multi-agent persuasion and deceptive coordination
- Agent sabotage and rogue agent divergence
- Tool invocation risks and insecure subprocess interfaces
- Excessive agency and blast radius containment failures
- Delegated authorization boundaries and credential leakage
- Supply chain integrity (including tool definition poisoning and rug pulls)
- Autonomous commerce and payment agent execution risks

# Lifecycle History

Covering Working Group Deliverables 2 and 4, the initial report and cross-framework coverage metrics were presented by Fernando Lucktemberg in June 2026, establishing GitHub as the version-controlled system of record for the maturing document.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining failure mode taxonomies, evaluation frameworks, reliable architectures, and state recovery specifications for agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation established to define standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably in enterprise environments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Because agentic workloads are inherently non-deterministic, the working group addresses ecosystem visibility gaps by classifying failure categories, defining controllable factors, identifying applicable resilience mechanisms, and establishing when human intervention is mandated[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

# Scope and Deliverables
The working group organizes its technical program around proactive architecture design and reactive remediation patterns[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **Accuracy and Reliability Frameworks**: Defining evaluation dimensions, failure modes, measurement techniques, and quality thresholds for [accuracy](../taxonomy/accuracy.md) and [reliability](../taxonomy/reliability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **Reliable Architecture Patterns**: Defining structural requirements such as verification loops and grounding mechanisms against authoritative systems of record[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **Recovery and Corrective Actions**: Standardizing specifications for safe-state restoration, rollback mechanisms, automated compensation, and human-in-the-loop intervention handoffs[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

The working group's delivery schedule is structured into canonical deliverables D1 through D6 and internal milestone I1[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6].

### Out of Scope and Boundaries
ARWG maintains clear demarcation lines with adjacent disciplines and groups[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **Model Internals and Training**: Systems are evaluated holistically; foundation model pre-training, fine-tuning, and prompt engineering remain out of scope[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **Telemetry Mechanics**: The group defines what reliability signals must be observable, while trace and log emission formats are delegated to the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **Production Platforms and Orchestrators**: Focuses on vendor-neutral standards, benchmarks, and blueprints rather than building production runtimes or commercial guardrail products[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
- **Legal Compliance**: Produces technical frameworks without prescribing jurisdictional legal or regulatory policy[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

# Architecture / Specification
ARWG specifications rely on four foundational operational dependencies[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
1. **Operational Predictability**: Agent execution runtimes are expected to expose standardized hooks supporting state recovery and execution trajectory management[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
2. **Immutable Agent Identity**: Auditing and benchmark comparisons require uniquely identifiable agent instances across environments and versions[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
3. **Versioning for Reproducibility**: Meaningful evaluation requires model configurations, prompts, and toolsets to be frozen as immutable versioned snapshots[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].
4. **Availability of Trust Anchors**: High-stakes agent actions require authoritative external systems of record against which generated outputs can be systematically reconciled[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

# Lifecycle History
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group charter was formally approved on 2026-05-15 and updated on 2026-06-30 under the leadership of chair Jordan Augé (Cisco)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Deliverable identifiers across phases were subsequently harmonized to establish the canonical D1–D6 and I1 workstream roadmap[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6].

# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing architectural frames, benchmark gap analyses, and formal evaluation protocols for agentic systems.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1] Chartered on May 15, 2026, the working group is co-chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

# Architecture / Specification
ARWG executes its technical charter across three primary deliverable tracks:[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]
- **D1 (Accuracy & Reliability Taxonomy):** A structured architectural framing document establishing standard terminology across evaluation subjects, output quality dimensions, grounding, failure symptoms, root causes, and correction mechanisms.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis and Benchmark Survey):** Led by Sanjeev Suresh, D2 grounds evaluation criteria in enterprise B2B operational needs across multiple personas (product managers, operations engineers, evaluators, and data scientists), evaluating benchmark coverage, tooling deficiencies, and interoperability requirements.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]
- **D6 (Evaluation Protocol):** A downstream evaluation specification directly scoped and informed by the operational gaps identified in D2.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

Cross-workstream terminology alignment is coordinated via formal working group delegates interacting with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

# Lifecycle History
The working group's charter was formally approved on May 15, 2026.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1] In June 2026, ARWG established a biweekly meeting cadence alternating plenary assemblies with dedicated deliverable working sessions focusing on D2.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative dedicated to eliminating siloed terminology, standardizing universal agent definitions, and curating a high-level ecosystem directory.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] It coordinates with designated delegates and domain editors across all technical working groups to harmonize cross-cutting terms and benchmark definitions against established international standards from ISO and NIST.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90]

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates an asynchronous, GitOps-driven intake architecture governing vocabulary definitions and ecosystem maps:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
- **Metadata Schema:** Baseline taxonomy records utilize a CNCF-style metadata structure requiring both a concise summary and an expanded scope description to serve introductory and specialist audiences.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
- **Asynchronous Intake Workflow:** Terminology changes undergo an offline consolidation workflow—aggregating cross-WG definitions into unified review spreadsheets before formal submission as pull requests reviewed by domain editors.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]
- **Human Curation and Editorial Standards:** Definitions are governed by a terminology style guide and an AI usage policy mandating human editorial oversight.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]
- **Landscape Integration:** Ecosystem directory efforts integrate directly with landscape.aif.io, distinguishing between member-driven contributions and external industry entities.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]

Delegates from partner groups—including [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), Security and Privacy, and Workflows and Process Integration—participate in boundary resolution for complex concepts such as agent operational limits.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the workstream finalized its operating charter with multi-working-group endorsement, reset historical terminology into structured pull requests, and scheduled high-level agent boundary definitions as rolling technical deliverables.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90]

mutations.rationale: Update leadership, ratified charter status, SKOS-Lite and CNCF schemas, delegate onboarding, and review workflows based on merged meeting notes and June 2026 report.

proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic terminology with SKOS-Lite schemas and maintaining a CNCF-style ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF technical group chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) dedicated to harmonizing agentic artificial intelligence terminology and maintaining a unified ecosystem directory[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. The workstream establishes shared metadata structures to eliminate terminology fragmentation, align domain models across peer working groups, and prevent duplicate research across the foundation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates two core specifications and technical publishing systems:

- **Taxonomy Metadata Schema**: Implements a SKOS-Lite (Simple Knowledge Organization System) profile defining controlled vocabularies, broader and narrower semantic relationships, and term status attributes for agent concepts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0], [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **Ecosystem Landscape**: Follows a CNCF-style configuration format and interactive web portal mapping frameworks, protocols, and developer infrastructure across agentic domains[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0], [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **Decoupled Architecture**: Separates underlying data files from the web rendering interface, supported by an automated CI/CD static site generation pipeline[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0], [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

## Contribution and Governance Process

Contributions follow a pull-request-driven asynchronous workflow governed by designated domain editors[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]:

1. Participating working groups designate two official voting delegates to coordinate terminology intake[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
2. For initial onboarding, working groups contribute candidate batches of 10 to 20 core domain terms aggregated into a unified tracking matrix to identify and resolve overlaps prior to PR emission[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
3. Domain editors review proposed changes, enforcing definitions style guides, AI usage policies, and structural schema validation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0], [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

## Reporting Cadence

The workstream submits monthly progress updates to the Technical Committee by the final business day of each reporting period, adhering to a 7-day asynchronous review window before PR merge[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-21**: Inaugural meeting held; charter reviewed, SKOS-Lite and CNCF-style structures adopted, and weekly Monday sync cadence established[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].
- **2026-06-30**: Formal workstream charter ratified across participating working groups; CI/CD portal launched and initial seed terms cleared to enforce delegate review workflows[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing common telemetry conventions, cross-framework agent tracing models, and runtime observability architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog) that establishes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing conventions, and evaluation benchmarks for agentic systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]. The group analyzes runtime execution paths across model invocations, tool interactions, multi-agent coordination layers, and external service protocols to ensure verifiable auditability and diagnostic visibility.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group structures its operational agenda across focused domain tracks that investigate telemetry boundaries and publish formal gap analyses:

- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Formed by merging the previously distinct LLM Primitives and Protocol Observability focus groups to address attendance and deliverable overlap, organizing around unified problem spaces rather than fragmented architectural layers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]. Evaluates language model lifecycle signals, Model Context Protocol (MCP) telemetry, and agent-to-agent protocol boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Multi-Agentic Observability**: Investigates orchestration, inter-agent task delegation, swarm coordination, and distributed turn boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **Agentic State, Context & Reasoning**: Analyzes dynamic context injection, memory retention, step-level reasoning traces, and potential integration into combined observability workstreams[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2], [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Hardened Traceability Architecture**: Formulates normative criteria for tamper-evident, provable execution traces and cryptographic attestation across runtime boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

The working group coordinates with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) on standardizing terminology and actively assesses interoperability with specifications such as [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2], [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-29**: Submitted June 2026 report detailing kickoff of six-month deliverable sprint, formation of five initial focus groups, and migration of use case and gap analysis tracking to GitHub[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].
- **2026-07-09**: Formally consolidated the LLM Primitives and Protocol Observability focus groups into a single combined track meeting biweekly, reviewed landscape analysis tooling, and evaluated Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) integration points[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# References

- Agent Resource Discovery: [../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md)
- Agent Behavior Trace Model: [../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)

- Cross-Boundary Model: [../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Resource Discovery
proposed_concept.description: Decentralized discovery and verification specification enabling agents to resolve, verify, and bind AI resources via catalogs, registries, and trust manifests.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) is an open specification for discovering, querying, and cryptographically verifying AI tools, models, and agent capabilities in decentralized environments[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]. Presented by Junjie Bu in coordination with a consortium of ten industry participants, ARD enables autonomous agents to locate compatible external resources dynamically without relying on centralized single points of trust[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Architecture / Specification

The ARD architecture divides resource location and admission into two complementary planes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]:

- **Static Catalog**: A statically indexed, declarative publication format that exposes available tools, endpoints, and schemas for offline indexing or cold start discovery[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Dynamic Registry**: A runtime discovery service providing REST APIs and semantic query interfaces, allowing agents to execute natural language queries against operational tool offerings[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

## Trust and Verification

ARD incorporates verifiable identity and boundary validation mechanisms to mitigate supply-chain attacks such as tool poisoning:

- **Decentralized Trust Models**: Integrates with SPIFFE (Secure Production Identity Framework for Everyone) and Agent Network Standard (ANS) naming conventions to attest provider identity across administrative domains[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Trust Manifests**: Cryptographically signed attestations accompanying resource registrations that certify provenance, behavioral boundaries, and policy compliance prior to agent invocation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-09**: Presented to the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) as a joint specification authored with ten collaborating organizations, initiating review of identity standard overlaps and traceability telemetry requirements[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# References

- Identity and Trust WG: [../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- Observability and Traceability WG: [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Agent Network Protocol: [agent-network-protocol.md](agent-network-protocol.md)
- Agent Identity Primitives: [agent-identity-primitives.md](agent-identity-primitives.md)

# Overview

The Government, Risk and Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) is an AAIF technical body co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]. The working group evaluates international regulatory frameworks, existing AI guidance documents, and industry standards to formulate compliance baselines and operational risk governance models for autonomous agent deployments.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical and analytical outputs around structured lifecycle phases:

- **Policy Landscape Assessment**: Comprehensive survey and inventory mapping existing global agentic AI policy frameworks, regulatory mandates, formal standards, and governance best practices[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **Comparative Gap Analysis**: A comparative analysis benchmarking identified industry practices against emerging regulatory obligations to establish concrete baselines for agent compliance and assurance[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **Regulatory Harmonization**: Translating high-level regulatory mandates into concrete architectural patterns, verification checklists, and attestation obligations across AAIF technical workstreams.

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-01**: Submitted June 2026 report recording completion of its initial three-month landscape assessment deliverable and launching a three-month sprint for regulatory gap analysis[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group co-chaired by Alexander Frazer and Junjie Bu establishing threat models, runtime boundary controls, and security design patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) body co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google) focused on security architectures, runtime containment, threat modeling, and best practices for agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. The group transitioned from formation to execution following the public release of its repositories and operates five active workstreams coordinating with foundation initiatives and external security bodies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Workstreams and Technical Scope
The working group organizes technical activities across five specialized workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]:
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, reviewing eight agentic threat domains against established baselines including MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and the NIST AI RMF [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, authoring builder-focused operational guidelines for agent secrets management, guardrails, and execution sandboxing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, curating reusable, implementation-neutral design patterns for runtime boundary enforcement [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing operational intake criteria and baseline security checklists for technical deliverables across AAIF groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation**: Coordinated through delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman into the unified cross-WG taxonomy initiative led by Junjie Bu [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# External Coordination and Governance
The working group actively monitors and seeks strategic alignment with external organizations including OWASP, the Agentic AI Risk Model (AARM), the Model Context Protocol Architecture and Compliance Sandbox (MCP ACS), and the European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI TC SAI) regarding European AI Act compliance for AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. Monthly governance updates are submitted asynchronously to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) under the foundation's standard reporting workflow [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream led by Junjie Bu harmonizing agentic AI terminology across all working groups through a unified consensus tracking workflow.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative led by Junjie Bu chartered to standardize agentic AI terminology, define ontological boundaries, and coordinate vocabulary across foundation working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. The workstream operates an asynchronous, delegate-driven workflow where each participating working group contributes domain-specific terms alongside universal concepts targeting an initial v1.0 foundational release [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

# Execution and Terminology Review Workflow
The workstream maintains a central unified taxonomy working inventory comprising approximately 250 candidate terms contributed across AAIF working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]. Curation operates under several operational mechanisms:
- **Universal Terms Segregation**: Foundational concepts applying across all agentic architectures—such as identity, capability, model, context, and agent—are organized into a dedicated universal section at the top of the working inventory [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
- **Consensus and Cull Tracking**: A consensus-based evaluation column with conditional highlighting tracks member votes (LGTM, cull, debate) to prune generic or non-agent-specific vocabulary while protecting domain-critical terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
- **Cross-Working Group Delegates**: Working groups appoint official delegates (such as Jay White and Katherine Druckman for [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md)) to represent domain requirements and harmonize overlapping definitions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Pre-Debate Surfacing**: Highly contentious or debate-worthy terms are surfaced in cross-foundation discussion channels prior to being culled or redefined [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized monthly reporting template, delivery timeline rules, and pull request review workflow for AAIF working groups reporting to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Reporting Template defines the canonical structure, delivery cadence, and pull request review workflow for monthly updates submitted by AAIF working groups to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]. The process provides consistent visibility into charter success metrics, deliverable status, ecosystem engagements, risks, and explicit decision asks requiring committee intervention [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].

# Cadence and Deadlines
Working groups submit monthly reports subject to the following rules [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28]:
- **Submission Deadline**: Reports are due by the last business day of the reporting calendar month [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- **Review Window**: The Technical Committee review window closes seven calendar days following submission [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- **Merge Criteria**: The report pull request is merged once the Technical Committee signs off or when the seven-day review window closes without outstanding questions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
- **File Naming and Indexing**: Reports are saved as `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` and indexed at the top of the reporting `README.md` table in reverse chronological order [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].

# Specification and Required Sections
Monthly reports adhere to `reporting/TEMPLATE.md` and must include [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5]:
- **Metadata Header**: Working group name, reporting period (`Month YYYY`), active chairs, and submission date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
- **Summary**: A two-to-three sentence executive summary highlighting key progress and operational shifts during the period [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
- **Progress Against Objectives**: Deliverables committed or advanced, explicitly referenced against chartered objectives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
- **Ecosystem Highlights**: External engagement and activities with bodies such as OWASP, AARM, or MCP ACS, or marked "None this month" [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
- **Blockers and Risks**: Active capacity constraints, dependencies, or delivery risks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
- **Decisions Needed from the TC**: Explicit, actionable requests requiring formal committee guidance or approval [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
- **Next Month's Focus**: Top two to three technical and organizational priorities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].
- **Metrics / Links**: Status against charter KPIs—Adoption, Quality, Community, and Timeliness—with supporting PRs, meeting notes, and repository links [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Working group research deliverable evaluating baseline threat modeling frameworks—including MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF—against agentic risks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design deliverable is an ongoing research initiative produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, the project identifies architectural security gaps in classical threat models when applied to autonomous, tool-augmented AI agents and inter-agent workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Evaluated Baselines and Threat Domains
The gap analysis synthesizes research across eight designated agentic threat areas, assessing existing coverage across established cybersecurity frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]:
- **MITRE ATLAS**: Matrix of adversarial tactics and techniques across AI system lifecycles.
- **OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and Agentic Applications**: Behavioral risks including direct and indirect prompt injection, excessive agency, and unsafe tool invocation.
- **MAESTRO**: Threat model framework focusing on multi-agent orchestrations, delegation chains, and cross-agent execution boundaries.
- **NIST AI RMF**: Risk management framework outlining trustworthiness characteristics and governance controls.

The deliverable benchmarks these foundations to isolate agent-specific vulnerabilities—such as tool supply-chain poisoning, context exhaustion, and cross-client data leakage—providing the basis for custom mitigation frameworks within the AAIF ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating shared agentic AI terminology and maintaining the interactive open ecosystem map.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chartered to curate a unified glossary of agentic AI terms and maintain a consolidated, living ecosystem map[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream ensures all AAIF working groups share synchronized definitions and avoid duplicative market research[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Operating Model
The workstream operates on a federated curation model driven by nominated Domain Editors representing each technical working group[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]:
- **Consolidation over Creation:** Ingests, normalizes, and reconciles domain glossaries from working groups rather than creating domain-specific vocabulary in isolation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Iterative Consensus:** Conceptual partitions and category boundaries evolve dynamically through weekly cross-workgroup delegate review rather than rigid upfront definitions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **SKOS-Lite Schema:** Standardizes vocabulary using structured semantic fields (`prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, `contrastsWith`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Scope Guardrails:** Curates horizontal concepts while reserving vertical domain specifications (such as regulatory assessments in [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) or protocol execution in [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)) to specialized working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

## Portal Delivery Pipelines
The workstream maintains automated GitHub Actions pipelines to deploy static web distributions to GitHub Pages[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea]:
- Bundles the CNCF-style ecosystem map (`landscape.yml`) and static viewer into `/dist/landscape`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea].
- Bundles the interactive [Taxonomy Explorer](../resources/taxonomy-explorer.md) into `/dist/taxonomy`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea].
- Automates Los Angeles timestamp injection into the portal index during CI deployment[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea].

# Lifecycle History
Chartered on June 21, 2026, to eliminate siloed definitions across foundation groups and provide a unified architectural blueprint for industry stakeholders[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

- Taxonomy Alignment: Terminology curation transitioned to the cross-foundation [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].

## External Alignment
The working group engages with external security consortia, establishing formal coordination postures with OWASP, AARM, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) Advisory Committee for Security (ACS)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group defines vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing boundaries, and operational observability profiles for autonomous agent networks and runtime harnesses.

# Architecture / Specification

## Working Group Coordination
- **Focus Group Consolidation:** The Protocols and Primitives focus groups were unified to ensure coherent semantic definitions and operational alignment across work streams[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
- **Taxonomy Integration:** The group actively harmonizes domain concepts with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), reviewing terms alphabetically and proposing universal vocabulary candidates[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
- **Standards Alignment:** Focuses upstream contributions on [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) semantic conventions and reference SDKs based on runtime gap analysis[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].

## Multi-Agent Network Observability
Explores observability across peer-to-peer and decentralized networking stacks (such as libp2p), investigating telemetry standardization at application transport boundaries, OpenID identity binding, and Server-Sent Events (SSE) tracing for agent-to-agent interactions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining shared workflow models, execution semantics, and stateful lifecycle patterns across agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (W&PI) develops vendor-neutral agentic workflow execution models, standard terminology, and interoperability design patterns across agent frameworks and execution environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]. Established to solve orchestration fragmentation and state loss in non-deterministic systems, the working group standardizes workflow primitives, coordinates interactions between autonomous agents and external systems, and defines patterns for resilient, stateful task execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

The group operates under the governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and collaborates with domain workstreams such as the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to delineate workflow audit logs from low-level runtime telemetry [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's charter covers three primary technical domains [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]:

- **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics**: Establishing common [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md) (tasks, tool calls, branching, retries, and sub-agents), standard execution structures across frameworks, step-ordering rules, conditional paths, and agent-to-agent handoff semantics [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution**: Defining persistence models, idempotent retry patterns, and replayable failure recovery for agent tasks running across hours or days, alongside execution-level audit records [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Tool Invocation and External Coordination**: Specifying vendor-neutral workflow orchestration patterns between autonomous agents, external APIs, and human review gates [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was formally approved on 2026-05-13 and updated on 2026-07-23 [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]. Leadership is held by Chair Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Co-Chair Adam Seligman (Workato) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
