proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group harmonizes open specifications, architectural frameworks, and vocabulary for commercial transactions conducted by autonomous AI agents on behalf of human users, businesses, and software platforms [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]. Rather than authoring competing commerce protocols, the working group identifies common ground across existing and emerging specifications to provide neutral interoperability guidance and reference architectures [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

The group reports findings and convergence recommendations to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and aligns transactional concepts with foundation taxonomy such as [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md) and [delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group addresses full commercial interaction lifecycles across five operational phases [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]:

- **Discovery**: Standardizing product, service, and merchant discovery mechanisms accessible by autonomous agents [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].
- **Negotiation**: Evaluating interaction models for terms, pricing, and agent-to-agent contract exchange [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].
- **Checkout**: Formulating interoperable data flows for cart creation, identity resolution, and order validation [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].
- **Payment Orchestration**: Guiding tokenized and delegated payment execution through secure transaction rails [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].
- **Post-Purchase Support**: Defining cross-platform patterns for receipt verification, tracking, returns, and dispute handling [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

# Lifecycle History
The working group was established under chairs appointed by Platinum and Gold members: Chair Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Co-Chair Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), serving terms from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]. The group meets biweekly on Wednesdays at 9:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group establishes technical standards, evaluation benchmarks, and engineering methodologies required for AI agents to operate correctly and consistently in enterprise production environments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]. The group creates shared definitions for evaluating agent system properties such as [accuracy](../taxonomy/accuracy.md) and [reliability](../taxonomy/reliability.md), analyzing non-deterministic failure modes and establishing robust testing patterns [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].

Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group works in cross-functional coordination with workstreams across the foundation [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on core reliability pillars [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]:

- **Evaluation Standards**: Establishing shared criteria and standardized benchmark datasets to measure single-run task accuracy and multi-step execution consistency [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].
- **Failure Analysis**: Documenting recurring failure modes in agent reasoning, context processing, tool invocations, and environmental drift [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].
- **Enterprise Engineering Practices**: Developing operational guidelines for recovery loops, guardrails, and deterministic verification gates [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].

# Lifecycle History
The working group leadership was appointed by Platinum and Gold members for the term March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027, featuring Chair Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Co-Chair Casper Nielsen (Diagrid) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]. Meetings are held biweekly on Tuesdays at 9:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group serves as an operational bridge between international AI policy developments, regulatory compliance mandates, and practical technical architectures in agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]. The group analyzes emerging legal, safety, and risk management expectations across jurisdictions and translates them into actionable engineering standards and reference architectures for autonomous agent builders [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673].

The group collaborates across the foundation's technical working groups under the supervision of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on aligning agent system behaviors with regulatory governance structures [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]:

- **Policy Harmonization**: Mapping regional AI regulatory acts, safety benchmarks, and risk frameworks to technical control points [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673].
- **Auditability and Accountability**: Formulating technical models for agent audit trails, accountability chains, and regulatory reporting mechanisms [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673].
- **Risk Assessment**: Developing practical risk classification methodologies tailored to autonomous decision-making and cross-system agent tool executions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673].

# Lifecycle History
The working group is led by Chair Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Co-Chair Deborah Eng (JP Morgan Chase), appointed by Platinum and Gold members for a term spanning March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]. Meetings take place bi-weekly on Thursdays at 10:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes threat models, defensive design patterns, security best practices, and operational evaluation frameworks for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]. Co-chaired by Alexander Frazer and Junjie Bu, the group addresses vulnerabilities unique to agentic architectures, including prompt injection, model context protocol tool poisoning, data leakage, and unauthorized cross-system executions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].

The group maintains active deliverables aligned with external organizations such as OWASP, while collaborating internally with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define security-specific vocabulary including [guardrails](../taxonomy/guardrail.md) and [skills](../taxonomy/skill.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group executes its mission across five structured deliverable workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]:

- **Threat Modeling**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, producing the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Security Best Practices**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, drafting the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Design Patterns**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, building the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing the [Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinated by Junjie Bu alongside Security and Privacy delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman, reviewing security terminology within the foundation's unified landscape [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, the working group reviewed progress across all five deliverable tracks, established decentralized tooling policies permitting workstream leads to select suitable coordination environments, and affirmed ongoing informal collaboration with OWASP pending formal Technical Committee agreements [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Accuracy and Reliability
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining evaluation frameworks, failure mode taxonomies, and engineering practices for AI agent accuracy, robustness, and operational reliability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an AAIF technical working group chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. The group is chartered to define evaluation frameworks, failure mode taxonomies, and engineering practices addressing correctness, variance across runs, perturbation robustness, and operational recoverability in agentic deployments.

ARWG coordinates cross-workstream terminology alignment with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and maintains active liaison ties with peer groups including the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group structures its core technical agenda across distinct deliverable tracks[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]:

## D1: Terminology and Methodology Support
D1 establishes the formal literature grounding, methodological foundations, and core definitions for agentic evaluation[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. Executed across three planned milestones, D1 organizes terminology across distinct evaluation dimensions:
- **Outcome correctness**: Establishing precise boundaries for [accuracy](../taxonomy/accuracy.md).
- **Consistency across runs**: Quantifying variance and establishing criteria for [reliability](../taxonomy/reliability.md).
- **Robustness to perturbations**: Defining semantic and input stability via [robustness](../taxonomy/robustness.md).
- **Operational reliability**: Measuring real-world production fault tolerance and [recoverability](../taxonomy/recoverability.md).

Terminology development prioritizes terms directly owned and governed by the working group, staging review from central parent concepts down to leaf terms to manage review cognitive load across foundation participants[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

## D2: Enterprise Gap Analysis
Deliverable D2 analyzes the divergence between academic benchmarks and enterprise practitioner requirements[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. Rather than maintaining an academic benchmark catalog, D2 evaluates production personas, enterprise operational requirements, and actionable practitioner gaps. This effort drives the [Accuracy & Reliability Survey](../resources/accuracy-and-reliability-survey.md) to gather direct industry evidence on deployment failure modes and cost-reliability trade-offs[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

## Cross-Workgroup Liaisons (I1)
The group maintains structured liaison documentation (I1) to harmonize cross-cutting concerns, opening initial collaboration channels with the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

# Lifecycle History

In July 2026, ARWG completed the initial draft of D1 and transitioned it to an open repository pull request for collaborative review, contributing an initial 41-term milestone batch to the shared taxonomy sheet[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. Concurrently, D2 was reframed from a benchmark survey into an enterprise gap analysis backed by targeted practitioner survey collection[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

mutations.rationale: Update survey background and methodology reflecting ARWG's D2 deliverable re-scoping toward practitioner prioritization and pain-point ranking.

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral survey instrument gathering enterprise practitioner evidence on agent failure modes, deployment priorities, and reliability trade-offs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Survey is an empirical research instrument created by the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. Designed as part of the group's D2 enterprise gap-analysis deliverable, the survey gathers structured data directly from industry practitioners deploying autonomous and semi-autonomous AI systems in production environments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

The survey addresses a critical empirical gap where publicly available benchmarks do not align with practitioner realities or capture deployment-blocking failure modes[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

# Architecture / Specification

The survey instrument is structured to rank practical enterprise pain points and extract comparative data across diverse deployment tiers:

## Core Objectives
- **Practitioner Grounding**: Identifying target production personas, enterprise operational requirements, and actionable engineering gaps that prevent direct reuse of standard benchmarks[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].
- **Priority Ranking**: Evaluating how organizations trade off cost, execution latency, response quality, and [reliability](../taxonomy/reliability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].
- **Failure Mode Mapping**: Collecting real-world failure distributions across task domains, including hallucinations, tool call failures, and boundary violations.
- **Top-Priority Use Case Convergence**: Anchoring working group deliverable priorities on validated industry use cases rather than speculative agent architectures[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

## Methodology and Integration
The survey operates in conjunction with the working group's D1 terminology framework, linking practitioner responses directly to normalized dimensions of [accuracy](../taxonomy/accuracy.md), [robustness](../taxonomy/robustness.md), and [recoverability](../taxonomy/recoverability.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]. Results feed into gap analysis reports and guide standardization priorities submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).

# Lifecycle History

In July 2026, ARWG reframed deliverable D2 from an academic benchmark inventory into an enterprise-focused gap analysis, launching survey preparation as an explicit mitigation to address limited comparative practitioner data across early and advanced adopters[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Security and Privacy
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining threat models, privacy guidelines, and defensive design patterns for autonomous and semi-autonomous systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPWG) is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for defining threat models, privacy guidelines, and defensive architectural patterns for autonomous and semi-autonomous systems. The group maintains security baselines, vulnerability catalogs, and operational checklists designed to mitigate risks specific to agent runtimes, tool interfaces, and model memory.

SPWG coordinates cross-workgroup security reviews with peer groups across the foundation, conducting dedicated scope and overlap assessments with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12], the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-13], the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-14], and the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-15].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's technical deliverables span defensive engineering, risk assessment, and cross-workstream coordination:

## Threat Modeling and Vulnerability Analysis
The group analyzes failure modes unique to agent architectures, including prompt injection, context contamination, and tool manipulation. Key deliverables include:
- The [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), benchmarking agent risks against established frameworks like MITRE ATLAS and OWASP.
- The [Agentic Vulnerability Enumeration](../resources/agentic-vulnerability-enumeration.md), cataloging behavioral and supply-chain vulnerabilities such as [tool poisoning](../taxonomy/tool-poisoning.md) and [rug-pull attacks](../taxonomy/rug-pull.md).

## Architectural Design Patterns and Guidelines
SPWG formalizes reusable defensive patterns and practical developer guidance, including:
- The [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md), specifying patterns such as [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and [Inherited Security Floor](../patterns/inherited-security-floor.md).
- The [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), providing guidance for secrets management, tool invocation boundaries, and model evaluation.

## Cross-Workgroup Security Reviews
To prevent architectural siloing and identify security blind spots early in standard development, SPWG actively reviews the scopes of peer working groups to generate items for the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12]:
- **Identity & Trust**: Evaluating boundary overlaps in credential delegation, DID resolution, and attestation claims[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12].
- **Observability & Traceability**: Assessing trace data sanitization, sensitive context masking in telemetry, and audit provenance[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-13].
- **Workflows & Process Integration**: Reviewing runtime state machine isolation, branch execution boundaries, and human approval bypass risks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-14].
- **Agentic Commerce**: Investigating transaction authorization integrity, financial tool access controls, and payment delegation security[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-15].

# Lifecycle History

SPWG established its foundational security catalog and threat modeling resources while initiating structured cross-workgroup scope evaluations across Identity & Trust, Observability & Traceability, Workflows & Process Integration, and Agentic Commerce to formalize collaborative security checklist items[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-13][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-14][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-15].

mutations.rationale: Detail cross-workgroup intake and scope alignment activities assessing security boundaries across Identity & Trust, Observability, Workflows, and Commerce.

proposed_concept.title: Cross-WG Security Review Checklist
proposed_concept.description: Operational review checklist and intake framework guiding early identification of security and privacy risks across foundation working group deliverables.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Cross-Workgroup Security Review Checklist is an operational intake framework and evaluation instrument maintained by the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md). It guides early identification of security, privacy, and abuse risks within technical specifications, protocols, and reference architectures developed across the Agentic AI Foundation.

The checklist surfaces boundary-crossing security considerations by tracking domain overlaps with peer working groups, including Identity & Trust, Observability & Traceability, Workflows & Process Integration, and Agentic Commerce[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-13][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-14][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-15].

# Architecture / Specification

The checklist evaluates proposed foundation deliverables against critical security boundaries and interface handoffs:

## Working Group Scope Overlaps
Checklist items are continuously refined through targeted scope reviews across working group boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12]:
- **Identity & Trust**: Reviewing delegation tokens, key life-cycle management, decentralized identifiers, and [attestation primitives](../standards/agent-identity-primitives.md) to ensure credentials cannot be forged or replayed across agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12].
- **Observability & Traceability**: Verifying that trace collectors, span attributes, and [behavior trace models](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) enforce data redaction to prevent [cross-client data leakage](../taxonomy/cross-client-data-leakage.md) or secret exposure in telemetry streams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-13].
- **Workflows & Process Integration**: Ensuring execution state machines, approval checkpoints, and [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md) strictly enforce boundaries like [branch isolation](../patterns/branch-isolation.md) and prevent bypass of [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-14].
- **Agentic Commerce**: Inspecting transaction workflows such as [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md) and [delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md) for replay attacks, unauthorized spending authority expansion, and missing settlement verifications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-15].

## Review Gates and Intake Procedure
Working groups submit emerging specifications to the Security & Privacy Working Group during draft stages. The review checklist ensures that:
1. Threat assumptions and trust boundaries are explicitly declared.
2. Ingress prompts and egress tool arguments are subjected to input validation and schema enforcement.
3. Policy enforcement mechanisms cannot be bypassed through model hallucination or prompt injection.
4. Telemetry and audit trails maintain confidentiality while providing non-repudiation.

# Lifecycle History

The Security & Privacy Working Group initiated structured review tracks across the scopes of Identity & Trust, Observability & Traceability, Workflows & Process Integration, and Agentic Commerce to systematically expand checklist criteria across domain boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-13][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-14][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-15].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol alignments, and lifecycle interfaces across agentic discovery, checkout, payment, and post-purchase.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical committee workstream established to define vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol alignments, and interface standards for AI agents executing or facilitating commercial transactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]. Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group operates under an approved charter addressing fragmented commerce protocols, merchant integration burdens, and distributed trust boundaries [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

The working group focuses strictly on commerce-facing protocol interfaces and signaling rather than underlying provider internals, examining transaction lifecycles spanning product discovery, [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md), [delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md), fraud and trust signaling, and post-purchase fulfillment [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Architecture / Specification

### Lifecycle Model and Core Abstractions

The working group structures agentic commerce into a continuous, multi-stage user journey [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]:

1. **Product Discovery**: Evaluating differences between asynchronous product feeds and live query retrieval against merchant APIs, identifying source discovery, catalog normalization, freshness, and trust validation as distinct challenges [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
2. **Checkout and Negotiation**: Analyzing protocols such as ACP and UCP as stateful, merchant-authoritative negotiation processes, defining extension mechanisms, transport bindings, and human-handoff boundaries [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
3. **Payment Execution**: Modeling payment capabilities through three decoupled primitives—**handler**, **instrument**, and **credential** [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]. The group evaluates dynamic transaction eligibility, delegated tokenization, sensitive data boundaries, and composition with specialized payment protocols like Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) using challenge–credential–receipt flows [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
4. **Fraud and Trust Signaling**: Developing patterns to separate agent identity and risk from shopper identity and risk [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]. The group maps participant-specific signal visibility across shopper, agent platform, merchant, payment provider, and risk system boundaries without enabling indiscriminate cross-party data sharing [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
5. **Post-Purchase Operations**: Exploring operational boundaries for order tracking, cancellations, refunds, returns, and dispute management, distinguishing read-only order observation from authorized state changes [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

### Cross-Working Group Dependencies

The working group coordinates with related AAIF initiatives to resolve cross-cutting concerns [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]:
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) for delegated authority chains, credential issuance, and cryptographic binding between shopper, agent, intent, and transaction payload [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) for data boundary protection, tokenization scopes, and fraud prevention [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) for transaction lineage, intent evidence, and audit trails [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Lifecycle History

- **February 2026**: Working group launched; conducted initial ecosystem landscape inventory across consumers, agents, merchants, payment networks, and protocols (ACP, UCP, AP2, x402) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26].
- **March 2026**: Adopted a lifecycle-oriented framework (discovery, checkout, payment, post-purchase) and formulated neutral gap-analysis criteria [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
- **April 2026**: Conducted technical deep dives into product discovery and merchant-authoritative checkout negotiation across ACP and UCP; finalized draft charter [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **May 2026**: Charter formally approved; established the **Agentic Commerce Capability Map** as the primary deliverable; advanced the handler/instrument/credential payment taxonomy and MPP composition patterns [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **June 2026**: Analyzed distributed trust and fraud signals across organizational boundaries, formalizing distinctions between agent risk, shopper risk, and intent attestations [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol alignments, and lifecycle semantics for AI agent commercial transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group develops vendor-neutral capability models, protocol alignments, and architectural specifications for autonomous and semi-autonomous commercial interactions involving AI agents[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]. Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group coordinates lifecycle definitions spanning discovery, catalog interaction, negotiation, payment execution, and post-purchase settlement across both human-mediated and autonomous agent workflows[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

The group interfaces closely with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to define standard operational patterns for transactions such as [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md), [delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md), and [agent-initiated transactions](../taxonomy/agent-initiated-transaction.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Capability Mapping
The primary deliverable of the working group is the Agentic Commerce Capability Map, targeting delivery in late 2026[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]. The map structures agent transaction lifecycles into distinct stages:
- **Pre-Purchase and Discovery**: Semantic discovery, product negotiation, and policy exploration.
- **Transaction Execution**: Authorization, identity verification, and payment processing.
- **Post-Purchase Operations**: Order state observation, adjustment ledgers, eligibility checks, remedy negotiations, and state-changing mutations such as cancellations, returns, and refunds[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

In analyzing post-purchase workflows, the working group evaluated specifications such as the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) as concrete input for structured policies, order events, and adjustment mechanisms, emphasizing that read-only order visibility is distinct from authoritative mutation execution[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

## Wallet and Mandate Integration
The working group evaluates agent wallets and payment protocols within its gap analysis and reference architectures[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]. Wallets and protocol constructs—such as x402-style payment responses and AP2 payment mandates—are treated as specialized payment and credential capability providers rather than end-to-end commerce engines[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]. Key architectural integration challenges include:
- Binding bounded intent mandates to downstream payment executions.
- Merchant validation, cryptographic receipt generation, and transaction binding.
- Managing renewed buyer approvals when order adjustments or price renegotiations occur[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, the working group initiated detailed post-purchase capability reviews and wallet integration models, while identifying participant expertise shortages in post-purchase operations as a schedule risk for the September Capability Map target[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564]. Upcoming priorities include protocol deep-dives into x402 and the evaluation of fraud and risk telemetry[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating shared agentic AI terminology and maintaining the interactive ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream curates shared, vendor-neutral agentic AI terminology and maintains the public ecosystem map for the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream arbitrates conceptual boundaries across all AAIF working groups to establish normative vocabularies and publish verified terminology to the foundation's public portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

The workstream operates under standards and authoring conventions governed by the [Taxonomy Contribution Guide](../guidelines/taxonomy-contribution-guide.md) and collaborates with specialized groups including [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), and [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Review Methodology and Staged Ingestion
The workstream manages a unified backlog of 128 proposed terms using a staged admissions process[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]:
1. **Term Arbitration**: Terms are sequentially evaluated during weekly working syncs to determine whether they belong in the shared taxonomy.
2. **Admission Before Definition**: To unblock structural alignment, terms are admitted first into the taxonomy catalog, deferring field population for `definition`, `category`, and `broaderTerm` until broader consensus is reached[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
3. **Pull Request Publication**: Admitted terms are published via version-controlled pull requests directly to the open taxonomy site and explorer interface[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
4. **Git-Centric Debates**: Discussions are transitioned out of working spreadsheets into GitHub pull requests and issues to preserve transparent provenance alongside term records[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

## Landscape and External Intake
In addition to internal vocabulary reviews, the workstream manages external landscape contributions and tool catalog updates. External pull requests and issues are gated behind attendance at weekly review syncs to preserve evaluation consistency[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, the workstream expanded its weekly syncs to 60 minutes and transitioned from terminology collection to active arbitration[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. During the period, 46 terms were evaluated, yielding 13 admitted entries, 11 culled entries, and 21 terms held for debate. These 13 admitted terms formed the workstream's initial merged taxonomy deliverable (PR #33) on August 3, 2026, activating the public portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

Subsequent reviews brought the total reviewed terms to 67, with 21 admitted terms live in the repository (PR #35), 15 culled, and 25 held in debate. Contested universal terms, including the definition of `Agent`, form the primary tail risk governing the v1.0 release timeline[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing common telemetry conventions, cross-framework agent tracing models, and verifiable execution diagnostics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines standardized telemetry models, diagnostic protocols, and trace formats for monitoring, debugging, and auditing autonomous agent execution across heterogeneous runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]. The group establishes vendor-neutral conventions bridging peer-to-peer networks, application frameworks, and observability backends to deliver end-to-end auditability and verifiable agent accountability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

The working group coordinates technical initiatives with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and develops telemetry standards linked to [action records](../taxonomy/action-record.md) and the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Composable Trust Blueprint (VTO and AAC)
A core initiative is the development of a Composable Trust Blueprint uniting Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO) and Agent Action Capsules (AAC) for peer-to-peer agent systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]. The blueprint decouples telemetry semantics from cryptographic proofs, allowing portable execution records across varied transport layers. Key technical elements include:
- **Encoding**: Standardizing on CBOR42 encoding for structured, high-efficiency telemetry data supporting floating-point representations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Runtime Integration**: Implementing action capsule bindings in Go and Python implementations via libp2p networking layers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Standards Alignment**: Coordinating with IETF and IRTF working groups on standardized measurement formats, accountability drafts, and verifiable telemetry proofs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

## Focus Groups and Core Workstreams
The working group organizes its technical development into specialized focus tracks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]:
- **State and Context**: Investigating contextual telemetry, state transition traces, and agent capsule architectures.
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Designing modular observability maps and prototyping runtime engines, including Context Intelligence Graph Agentic Runtimes.
- **Application-Layer Interoperability**: Formulating the Agentic Trace Model proposal and drafting recommendations for the core OpenTelemetry specification.
- **Cross-Boundary Observability**: Specifying observation boundaries between local agent runtimes, peer-to-peer messaging layers (e.g., GossipSub), and external agent registries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the group demonstrated peer-to-peer observability stacks running over GossipSub and initiated joint integration efforts with libp2p and decentralized identity protocols[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]. The group also aligned taxonomy contributions with the universal terms workstream and scheduled upcoming submissions for the Agentic Trace Model and IETF telemetry drafts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group advances the mission of the Agentic AI Foundation by establishing a shared workflow model and standardized terminology for agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87] Operating under the governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group produces vendor-neutral interoperability guidelines, reference architectures, and design patterns that allow multi-step agent workflows to reliably execute across disparate runtime environments, execution frameworks, and external tools.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

# Architecture / Specification

### Governance and Operations
- **Chair:** Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Co-Chair:** Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

- **Public Channels:** `wg-workflows-process-integration@lists.aaif.io` mailing list and dedicated Discord channels.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

### Active Workstreams

2. **Reference Architectures:** Standardizes canonical workflow execution blueprints, including single-agent approval pipelines and parallel subagent orchestrations.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a]

# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry conventions, agent trace models, and cross-boundary visibility interfaces across foundation models, tool execution environments, and multi-agent coordination frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7] Led by co-chairs Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group develops reference specifications, correlation schemas, and gap analyses to ensure end-to-end auditability and performance monitoring for agentic systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

# Architecture / Specification

### Operational Structure and Active Tracks
In July 2026, the working group restructured its execution model by consolidating five initial focus groups into three active tracks to streamline participation and reduce domain overlap:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability:** Led by Zayne Turner, merging model primitives and protocol instrumentation. Current initiatives include tracing Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) workflows (skill discovery, provenance, governance, and pre-execution trust decisions), treating agent skills as first-class observable entities, and publishing a cross-boundary observability gap model.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- **Multi-Agentic Observability – Orchestration & Coordination:** Led by Ty Smith, addressing inter-agent handoffs, delegation graph tracing, and distributed task routing.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- **Agentic State & Context:** Led by Govindaraj, combining agent reasoning with persistent state and context window lifecycle observability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

### Key Deliverables
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** A standardized cross-framework recommendation led by Matthew Lee defining entity relationships and turn-level telemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]
- **Cross-Boundary Observability Model:** A structured framework analyzing visibility gaps between model harnesses, transport protocols, and tool processes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a practical engineering reference produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to provide builders with actionable controls against threats unique to autonomous and semi-autonomous systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9] The guide establishes implementation guidance across five core architectural domains using a repeatable failure-pattern, defensive control, and decision-framework structure.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Security Domains
The guideline addresses five foundational domains of agent deployment:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

1. **Secrets Management:** Protecting operational credentials, short-lived tokens, and API keys from prompt injection, unintentional reflection, and cross-session leakage.
2. **Secure Tool Invocation:** Mitigating supply-chain attacks, rug-pull vulnerabilities, and malicious payloads across Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and command-line execution boundaries.
3. **Guardrails:** Implementing pre-invocation and post-invocation behavioral filters, deterministic policy predicates, and structural payload validation.
4. **Evaluation Frameworks:** Benchmarking agent safety, tool boundary compliance, and resilience against adversarial prompt perturbations.
5. **Post-Incident Forensics:** Capturing tamper-evident audit trails, trace attestation, and event playback necessary for investigating compromised runs.

### Structural Methodology
Each domain section follows a three-part structure designed to balance tactical remediation with design rationale:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]
- **Failure Pattern:** Concrete description of how systems fail or are exploited in production.
- **Control:** Specific architectural pattern or technical configuration mitigating the vulnerability.
- **Decision Framework:** Trade-off analysis guiding engineering choices based on deployment risk and latency constraints.

### Scope Boundaries
Identity federation, token exchange (RFC 8693), and delegated authorization primitives (such as SPIFFE/SVID) are intentionally excluded from this guideline and are governed by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

# References
- [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)
- [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md)
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines vendor-neutral telemetry conventions, standardized trace formats, and evaluation harnesses across agent execution lifecycles. Operating under an open-source governance cadence, the working group maintains GitHub as its durable source of truth for all deliverables, coordination threads, decisions, and pull requests[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

# Operational Methods and Work Tracking
The working group organizes ongoing work through structured GitHub work items and defined review windows to ensure project status is discoverable without requiring synchronous meeting presence[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

Work items follow a standardized lifecycle across six explicit states[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50]:
- `needs owner`: The deliverable or task is approved and validated, but no driver has been assigned.
- `scoping`: Working group members are actively defining boundaries, expected outcomes, and necessary inputs.
- `in progress`: Active research, drafting, or cross-workstream coordination is underway.
- `ready for review`: The drafted artifact is staged and awaiting community feedback.
- `blocked`: Execution is suspended pending an explicit decision, missing external dependency, or input.
- `done`: The deliverable has merged, closed intentionally, or transitioned to long-term maintenance.

Every substantive work item requires an explicit owner, defined outcome, acceptance criteria, and linked dependencies prior to closure[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50]. Pull requests require linked tracking issues, explicit reviewer focus areas, and status markers for living documents[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b2496e80299b-e136231b].

# Operating Cadence
The group executes on a structured rhythm aligned with regular technical sessions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]:
1. **Pre-meeting triage:** Maintainers scan open issues and pull requests for stale steps or blocked deliverables to set meeting agendas.
2. **In-meeting recording:** Decisions and action items are captured directly into minutes with cross-references to repository artifacts.
3. **Post-meeting synchronization:** Issue assignees and statuses are updated immediately so asynchronous contributors can follow progress.
4. **Monthly reporting:** Aggregated issue closures, merged pull requests, and recorded minutes form the authoritative evidence base for Technical Committee reporting.

# Related Concepts

- `../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md`
- `../governance/technical-committee.md`

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining threat models, privacy guidelines, and defensive design patterns for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes threat models, defensive architectures, mitigation guidelines, and privacy-preserving design patterns for agentic artificial intelligence systems. Chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group tracks deliverables across threat modeling, practitioner security guidelines, design pattern catalogs, and cross-working group security review frameworks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Active Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group coordinates active execution across five principal workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10]:
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, assessing agentic vulnerabilities against frameworks including MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF across eight domain areas. Initial drafts have been opened as pull requests for community review[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing actionable security controls, secrets management, and invocation safety guidance for agent implementers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, defining reusable architectural patterns and coordinating coverage boundaries with general reference architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist:** Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing operational security checklists and intake gates for deliverables produced across the foundation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Taxonomy Alignment:** Delegated to Jay White and Katherine Druckman, aligning security and privacy terms within the shared cross-working group landscape catalog[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# External Liaisons and Industry Context
The working group maintains active engagement with external standards bodies and ecosystem initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]:
- Formal and informal collaboration with OWASP around the State of Agentic AI Security and Governance report[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].
- Coordination with ETSI TC SAI regarding European AI Act standardization and AI agent requirements[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- Tracking protocol changes in the Model Context Protocol (MCP), specifically stateless execution and cryptographic attestations to mitigate tool rug-pull vulnerabilities[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- Identifying coordination opportunities with FINOS AI governance and reference architecture initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining threat models, privacy guidelines, and defensive design patterns for secure and privacy-preserving agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. The group produces open threat models, shared taxonomy contributions, defensive design patterns, and security best practice guidelines that agent creators, enterprise consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to maintain trustworthy agentic deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Leadership
The working group is led by two appointed chairs serving a term from March 1, 2026, through January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]:
- **Chair:** Alex Frazer (Runlayer)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]
- **Co-Chair:** Junjie Bu (Google)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]

Working group pull requests can be reviewed and merged directly by the working group once peer consensus is reached, provided deliverables stay within the approved charter, without requiring explicit pre-approval from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Merged work is formally communicated to the TC through monthly status reporting[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Meeting records and summaries are maintained openly across public repositories and LFX tooling[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

## Core Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes its deliverables into five primary tracks:
1. **Threat Modeling:** Developing the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md) mapping existing frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF, STRIDE, and PASTA) to agentic architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
2. **Best Practices Guide:** Authoring the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), addressing human-in-the-loop accountability, runtime boundaries, and tool invocation safety[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
3. **Design Patterns Catalog:** Curating the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md), including patterns such as the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
4. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist:** Operating the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) to audit specifications and avoid domain overlap with groups such as the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
5. **Taxonomy Alignment:** Contributing security and privacy terminology into the unified cross-working group vocabulary managed alongside the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History
The working group held its orientation on February 17, 2026, and elected Alex Frazer as chair on March 3, 2026[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]. Following charter approval in May 2026, the group made all GitHub repositories, Discord channels, and meeting recordings publicly accessible, establishing biweekly Tuesday meetings[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Technical Committee governance policy defining project intake requirements, four progression stages (Sandbox, Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and annual review criteria.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy sets forth the criteria, processes, and expectations for open technical projects seeking to join or progress within the foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. Effective March 18, 2026, this policy provides a transparent governance framework across four maturity stages: Sandbox, Growth, Impact, and Emeritus, under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Proposal Requirements
All proposed projects must submit a formal proposal to the AAIF project proposals repository specifying[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:
- Project name, description, origin, and history[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Statements of alignment with the AAIF mission and integration with existing AAIF projects[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Adoption evidence and example use cases[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Designated Technical Committee sponsor, if identified[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Licensing under an OSI-approved permissive license[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Public repository location, automated CI/CD release mechanics, specification contribution process, and public issue tracking[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Core maintainers, governance documentation (`GOVERNANCE.md`), official communication channels, and external dependencies[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

## Progression Stages
The lifecycle categorizes projects into four stages[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:
1. **Sandbox Stage:** The initial entry point for early-stage, experimental, or emerging projects exploring novel agentic technologies and building initial community adoption[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
2. **Growth Stage:** Reserved for active projects with sustained contributor growth, expanding production adoption, and solid governance practices demonstrating cross-organizational collaboration[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
3. **Impact Stage:** Flagship projects demonstrating broad industry adoption, high operational maturity, stable release engineering, and substantial ecosystem utility[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
4. **Emeritus Stage:** Projects that have reached end-of-life, completed their original technical objectives, or retired active development, maintained in a stable archival state[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

## Annual Review Process
Every active project undergoes an annual review conducted by the Technical Committee to assess project health, community diversity, maintenance activity, and progression eligibility against stage acceptance criteria[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Lifecycle History
The Technical Committee approved and adopted the Project Lifecycle Policy on March 18, 2026, establishing standardized project entry and graduation procedures for the foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security pattern isolating the policy decision point and evidence signing within a hardware-attested environment while keeping the agent outside the trust boundary.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attested Isolated Runtime is an architectural security pattern that isolates policy decision points and evidence signing within a hardware-isolated environment while leaving the AI agent outside the trust boundary[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. Designed for operational deployments where infrastructure operators or hosting layers reside within the threat model, the pattern protects governance rules, tool execution authorizers, and audit proof generation from compromise by unmeasured or adversarial execution environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Architecture / Specification

## Architectural Invariants
The pattern establishes four mandatory requirements to prevent governance and measurement failures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:
1. **Enforcement Isolation (Agent Outside):** The policy decision point (PDP) and enforcement logic run strictly inside an isolated runtime, while agent logic remains external[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. Because agent code routinely executes untrusted and attacker-influenced input (such as prompt injections), enclosing the agent inside the trusted computing base (TCB) would expose the secure enclave to subversion[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
2. **Internal Key Generation:** Signing keys must be generated inside the isolated boundary and bound directly to cryptographic attestation claims, ensuring evidence cannot be forged by host infrastructure[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
3. **Measured Policy Sealing:** Policy bundles, system prompts, and tool schemas are sealed to enclave measurements and only released upon successful hardware appraisal[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
4. **Independent Verifier Appraisal:** An independent external verifier appraises per-unit-of-work attestation evidence before releasing sensitive resources or executing downstream actions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

## Attestation Targets and Neutrality
The pattern is vendor-neutral and maps to multiple confidential computing architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:
- AMD SEV-SNP[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
- Intel TDX[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
- ARM CCA[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
- NVIDIA GPU Confidential Computing[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
- TPM 2.0 and software-only emulation modes for local testing and conformance[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]

## Standards Alignment and Workstream Questions
The pattern references standard attestation protocols including IETF RATS (RFC 9334), CBOR Web Token (RFC 8747), COSE (RFC 9711), IETF SCITT, and SLSA[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. Key design questions under evaluation by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) include defining the exact artifact measurement set (such as prompt definitions versus dynamic memory states) and coordinating assurance vocabulary with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Working group research deliverable evaluating existing threat modeling frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF, STRIDE, PASTA) against agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a research deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) evaluating existing cybersecurity and AI threat modeling frameworks against agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. The analysis identifies where traditional software and AI security baselines fall short in addressing autonomous goal decomposition, tool execution boundaries, and human accountability[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Framework Coverage and Evaluation
The gap analysis evaluates agentic threat vectors across industry frameworks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]:
- **OWASP:** Assessing LLM Top 10 vulnerabilities, supply-chain risks, and prompt injection vectors in autonomous agent runtimes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **MITRE ATLAS:** Evaluating matrix tactics against agent multi-hop execution, persistence, and lateral tool invocation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **MAESTRO and NIST AI RMF:** Benchmarking risk management categories and governance controls against dynamic agent environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **STRIDE and PASTA:** Investigating classic threat-modeling taxonomies to assess spoofing, tampering, elevation of privilege, and risk-centric threat paths unique to tool-augmented agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

## Human Accountability and Protocol Considerations
The deliverable incorporates operational considerations surrounding Human-User-Agent (HUA) interaction models, ensuring that while agents execute actions autonomously, humans retain legal, ethical, and operational accountability[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. It also analyzes security boundaries introduced by interoperability specifications such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent plugin standards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History
Authored by Fernando Lucktemberg, initial drafts of the gap analysis were introduced in July 2026, followed by formal pull request submission (PR #8) in August 2026 to support dedicated threat modeling sub-workstream sessions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Structured triage skill formatting maintainer-oriented issue reviews, containing prompt injections via nonce delimiters, and formulating testable root-cause hypotheses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `issue-analysis` skill produces structured, first-pass technical assessments of filed GitHub issues to assist maintainers in issue triage, prioritization, and root-cause identification [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Maintained within the `aaif/submission-analyser` repository, the skill ingests issue bodies encapsulated within nonce-delimited data containers, treating all user-supplied text strictly as passive evidence rather than executable instructions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill defines a four-step analysis pipeline governing issue ingestion, codebase inspection, historical comparison, and structured reporting:

- **Untrusted Input Ingestion & Injection Handling**: Incoming issue text is delivered inside a nonce-delimited boundary. The skill treats all text within that block as data [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. When an issue contains prompt injection attempts—such as directives to disregard instructions, execute unauthorized commands, call tools, expose secrets, or broadcast mass social mentions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60]—the agent sets `injectionSuspected = true`, documents the attempt within `injectionNotes`, and evaluates the remaining technical merits objectively [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Read-Only Codebase Grounding**: Prior to formulating hypotheses, the skill inspects the repository working tree to locate concrete component paths (e.g., `src/queue/consumer.ts` or `src/http/client.ts`) and assess reported failure plausibility [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-20fc496a9225-9e278b3d]. Modifying repository files, dispatching network calls, and executing build tasks are prohibited during analysis [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Past Review Consultation**: The skill scans existing hand-written evaluations in `references/`, comparing frontmatter tags (`tags`, `issue-type`, `severity`, `components`) to identify 3–5 high-relevance cases [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Precedent reviews—such as buffered queue acknowledgement drops during shutdown [^evt-submission-analyser-file-20fc496a9225-9e278b3d] or debug serializer bypasses exposing authorization headers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4754a1b8e47b-9ed9890b]—are cited in `relatedPastIssues` only when they directly substantiate severity judgments or failure mechanisms [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Structured Template Conformance**: Analyses conform to a standardized maintainer reporting template [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]:
  1. *Summary*: Single-paragraph maintainer-level description of reported behavior.
  2. *Classification*: Explicit enumeration of type (`bug`, `feature-request`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, or `ambiguous`), severity rating (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, or `informational`), and reproducibility with impact rationale [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
  3. *Affected Components*: Concrete file paths or module boundaries [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
  4. *Root-Cause Hypotheses*: Concrete physical failure mechanisms paired with clear confirmation and refutation criteria [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
  5. *Suggested Actions*: Prioritized diagnostic checks, file inspection seams, and regression tests (excluding unverified code patches) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
  6. *Open Questions*: Concrete operational ambiguities to clarify with the reporter [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
  7. *Related Past Reviews*: Citations to precedent analyses justifying the analytical conclusion [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

# References
- `../resources/submission-analyser.md`
- `../standards/agent-skills.md`

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless triage runner executing issue analysis skills against GitHub submissions using nonce data boundaries, prompt injection telemetry, and read-only repository sandboxing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`submission-analyser` is a headless triage agent and sandboxed GitHub Actions runner developed within the AAIF ecosystem to execute automated first-pass evaluations of newly filed issues [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Operating in CI environments, it mounts repository codebases alongside triage skills like `issue-analysis` while enforcing strict boundary controls against untrusted input [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

# Architecture / Specification
`submission-analyser` couples skill orchestration with defensive execution controls:

- **Nonce-Delimited Untrusted Ingestion**: Submissions from external contributors are wrapped within uniquely generated nonce-delimited text blocks [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. The runner instructs downstream models that all delimited content is passive data, neutralizing embedded prompt injection attempts such as unauthorized mention flooding, role hijacking, or diagnostic overrides [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60].
- **Structured Injection Telemetry**: Adversarial instructions contained within issue text are identified and extracted as metadata findings rather than executed [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. The runner records security findings in dedicated fields (`injectionSuspected` and `injectionNotes`), allowing maintainers to inspect injection attempts out-of-band [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Read-Only Sandboxed Execution**: Harness runs are restricted to non-destructive inspection of checked-out repositories [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Agents may locate and read files but are denied permissions to run builds, mutate local disk state, or initiate outbound network calls during analysis [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Defensive Regression Test Fixtures**: The runner suite maintains synthetic injection vectors (such as `@everyone` mass ping payloads) under `tests/fixtures/injections/` to benchmark and verify model resilience against prompt manipulation [^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60].

# References
- `../skills/issue-analysis.md`
- `../standards/agent-skills.md`

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless triage runner executing issue analysis skills against GitHub submissions with regression test fixtures for indirect prompt injection defenses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Submission Analyser is a headless triage runner executing automated analysis skills against GitHub issues and community submissions while maintaining boundary defenses against prompt injection [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6]. Operating alongside ../skills/issue-analysis.md, it isolates untrusted input streams to prevent untrusted payload execution during triage evaluations.

# Architecture / Specification

The test suite maintains regression fixtures assessing system resilience across diverse adversarial injection techniques:

- **Direct Instruction Override**: Fixtures commanding the agent to disregard system instructions, alter output formats, or dump runtime prompts [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].
- **Hidden Comments**: Payload injection concealed within HTML comment blocks intended to alter severity scores or suppress injection indicators [^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe].
- **Synthetic Tool Invocations**: Structured XML and JSON blocks mimicking `<tool_call>` or `<invoke>` schemas to trick the model into triggering unauthorized tool runs [^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f].
- **Attacker URLs**: External diff and script links designed to induce secondary retrieval and arbitrary payload execution [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd].
- **Obfuscation and Homoglyphs**: Directives encoded in Base64, ROT13, or Cyrillic homoglyphs targeting keyword filtering mechanisms [^evt-submission-analyser-file-0f27825af60d-1d3aca33].
- **Role-Play and Unicode Controls**: Bidirectional control characters and unconstrained persona adoption attempts designed to bypass system prompt constraints [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca].

These fixtures support the testing of isolation boundaries defined in ../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md.

proposed_concept.title: Linux Driver Tracing
proposed_concept.description: Layered kernel observability and debugging reference architecture defining structured logging, dynamic debug, tracepoints, and bus tracers for Linux device drivers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Linux Driver Tracing defines the kernel and subsystem-level instrumentation mechanisms used by device driver developers and system administrators to observe, trace, and debug driver behavior within the Linux operating system.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321] Maintained as a reference architecture by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), this document connects generalized kernel tracing facilities such as [ftrace](../resources/ftrace.md), [Linux perf](../resources/linux-perf.md), and [LTTng](../resources/lttng-kernel.md) to driver-specific instrumentation points and hardware bus monitors.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]

# Architecture / Specification
The driver tracing architecture spans five primary instrumentation layers targeting modern Linux kernels (version 6.x recommended, baseline ≥ 4.19) with `CONFIG_DYNAMIC_DEBUG`, `CONFIG_DEBUG_FS`, and `CONFIG_TRACEPOINTS` enabled:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]

- **Structured Device Logging**: Drivers record operational state and anomalies through standardized logging macros (`dev_dbg`, `dev_info`, `dev_warn`, `dev_err`) defined in `<linux/device.h>`. Messages include device identity prefixes and are routed through `printk` to the kernel ring buffer.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]
- **Dynamic Debug (`dyndbg`)**: Controls debug call sites at runtime without driver recompilation. Administrators query and toggle individual call sites by module, file, function, or line number via `/sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control` or kernel boot parameters.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]
- **Driver Tracepoints (`TRACE_EVENT`)**: Low-overhead structured tracepoints declared through the kernel `TRACE_EVENT` macro system expose binary data through `tracefs` (`/sys/kernel/tracing/`). Tracepoints can be filtered and consumed concurrently by tools such as `perf` or `trace-cmd`.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]
- **Bus and Subsystem Monitors**: Domain-specific tap interfaces capture I/O transactions directly from hardware subsystems, such as `usbmon` capturing USB Request Blocks (URBs) for packet analysis and `blktrace` capturing block queue request timelines.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]
- **Diagnostic Dumps and Debugfs Interfaces**: Drivers export non-standard diagnostic counters, hardware state tables, and crash memory dumps via `/sys/kernel/debug/` mounts and the `devcoredump` framework.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]
