proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless triage runner executing issue analysis skills against incoming submissions with regression suites evaluating prompt injection defenses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Submission Analyser is an automated headless triage runner that applies the [Issue Analysis](../skills/issue-analysis.md) skill to incoming GitHub issues and pull requests, generating structured technical summaries while enforcing strict boundaries against adversarial prompt injections.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61] To ensure resilience when parsing untrusted community inputs, the project maintains an automated regression test suite containing realistic attack fixtures targeting agent workflows.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea]

# Architecture / Specification
The analyser's test suite validates parsing, sandboxing, and classification boundaries against distinct classes of indirect prompt injection:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61]

- **Environment and Secret Exfiltration**: Fixtures evaluate whether malicious instructions can coerce the agent into disclosing environment variables (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, service account keys) or base64-encoding secrets into unexpected metadata fields.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61]
- **Delimiter and Nonce Forging**: Test inputs construct fake closing boundary tags (such as `</untrusted-issue>`) and forge privileged system wrappers (e.g. `<system nonce="trusted">`) to trick the runner into treating untrusted text as operator directives.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61]
- **Obfuscated and Embedded Payloads**: Injections are hidden within HTML comments, collapsed markdown disclosure elements (`<details>`), image error handlers (`onerror` fetch calls), and group mentions to test sanitization robustness.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea]
- **Authority Impersonation and Urgency**: Scenarios simulate high-priority directives claiming authorization from repository owners, model vendor safety teams, or Linux Foundation security staff to demand suppression of injection warning banners or override egress policies.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-fdb9d913d85d-8ad69d31]

proposed_concept.title: Goose Agent Framework and Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Open-source general-purpose agent framework and Rust runtime coordinating multi-turn tool calling, ACP and MCP extension interfaces, and OpenTelemetry and Langfuse telemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Goose is an open-source general-purpose AI agent framework and runtime providing an autonomous execution loop for LLM-driven tool calling, security scanning, and multi-protocol extensibility [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]. Implemented in Rust, Goose operates as a local server daemon (`goosed`) and command-line interface (`goose`) that connects desktop clients, IDEs, and terminal environments to foundational model providers and external tools [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

# Architecture / Specification
Goose operates at the system runtime layer, coordinating the complete agent execution lifecycle across several core subsystems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]:

- **Server and API Tier (`goose-server` / `goosed`)**: Built on the Axum web framework, exposing endpoints for inference replies (`/reply`), session management (`/session`), streaming event notifications (`/session_events` via Server-Sent Events), configuration, scheduling, and proxy interfaces (`/mcp_app_proxy`, `/mcp_ui_proxy`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **Client Interfaces**: Supports multiple interaction surfaces including the `goose-cli` terminal client, an Electron desktop application, and third-party code editors (such as JetBrains and Zed) communicating over the [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md) via `stdio` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **Agent Core and Execution Loop**: Coordinates multi-turn conversation context, context compaction, and subagent delegation. It integrates provider chat integrations supporting over 15 LLM backends, alongside a Permission Inspector and a Security Manager that pairs pattern matching with ML scanners [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **Extension Protocols**: Connects to tool extensions using the Model Context Protocol ([MCP](../standards/agent-plugins.md)) over `stdio` and SSE transports [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **State Storage**: Persists local conversation histories and session checkpoints in an embedded SQLite database using `sqlx` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **Observability and Telemetry**: Emits structured traces via dual telemetry channels: an [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) collector exporter (HTTP/protobuf on port 4318) capturing `agent_reply`, `provider_chat`, and `tool_execution` spans, and direct generation observation traces exported to [Langfuse](../resources/langfuse.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

# Lifecycle History
The AAIF Observability and Traceability Working Group documented the reference architecture for Goose v1.39.0 on 2026-06-29 under the AI agent observability landscape [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless issue triage runner executing Flue agent skills within GitHub Actions, isolating untrusted inputs across cross-repo dispatch boundaries and restricting write access.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Submission Analyser is a headless triage automation runner that analyses incoming GitHub issues and publishes structured evaluations to maintainers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. Running on Flue 2.0 within GitHub Actions workflows, the system evaluates untrusted issue text across a cross-repository trust boundary while containing prompt injection risks through token privilege boundaries and external egress publishing [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].

# Architecture / Specification
The runner architecture enforces defense-in-depth isolation controls for untrusted, attacker-controlled inputs in an agent execution loop [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]:

- **Cross-Repository Dispatch Boundary**: Target repositories host a lightweight trigger workflow (`request-issue-analysis.yml`) invoking the analyst workflow via `workflow_dispatch` with a fine-grained token (`ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN`) restricted to `Actions: read and write` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]. `repository_dispatch` is deliberately excluded because it requires `Contents: write`, which would permit push access and modification of the analyst workflow [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
- **Least-Privilege GitHub Actions Tokens**: The analysis workflow limits permissions to `contents: read` and `copilot-requests: write` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]. It omits `issues: write` and never writes back to repository files or issue threads, preventing injected models from modifying repository assets [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].
- **External Publishing Channels**: Analysis reports publish exclusively to human-facing destinations: a Google Doc in a maintainer Drive folder and an announcement in a Discord channel [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].
- **Supply-Chain Action Pinning**: Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to full 40-character commit SHAs rather than mutable git tags, preventing supply-chain tag re-pointing attacks [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].
- **Offline Faux Verification in CI**: Continuous integration runs credential-free tests with `FLUE_FAUX=1 flue run ... --json` using in-memory mock providers and egress, validating mounted skill frontmatter schemas and exit codes at load time [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].

# References
- Executes the [Issue Analysis](../skills/issue-analysis.md) skill [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- Implements controls aligned with [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and the [Inherited Security Floor](../patterns/inherited-security-floor.md).

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Maintainer-focused triage skill that evaluates incoming issues against historical reference analyses retrieved by component and tag metadata.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Issue Analysis is an automated agent skill executing structured triage, categorization, and severity evaluation on incoming issues filed against open-source repositories [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]. Deployed via the [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md) runner, the skill combines project context retrieval with strict threat modeling to prevent untrusted issue text from executing prompt injection attacks or leaking credentials [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill operates via standardized prompt evaluation and indexed reference retrieval [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]:

- **Reference Corpus Retrieval**: The skill scans a local corpus of historical handwritten analyses, reading YAML frontmatter to match incoming issue properties against `tags` and `components` fields. It selects the 3 to 5 most relevant past analyses to load in full [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- **Precedent Grounding**: Synthetic bootstrap examples carry `example: true` in their frontmatter, instructing the agent to exercise the retrieval pipeline without citing fabricated examples as factual precedent [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- **Auditing and Redaction Rules**: Because corpus conclusions are cited directly in published Google Docs and Discord announcements, corpus entries are audited to exclude customer names, internal hostnames, secrets, unannounced roadmap items, or private security embargoes [^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].
- **Untrusted Input Handling**: Issue titles, descriptions, labels, author metadata, and comments are classified as untrusted input and evaluated without granting repository write privileges [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].

# References
- Packaged and executed by [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].
- Adheres to the [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) specification.

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless issue triage runner executing Flue agent skills within GitHub Actions, isolating untrusted inputs while routing model calls exclusively through GitHub Copilot via token exchanges.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Submission Analyser is a headless triage runner executing [Flue](../../skills/issue-analysis.md) agent skills inside GitHub Actions workflows to evaluate project proposals and community issues [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]. It enforces strict credential boundaries, operates without write access to monitored issue repositories, and routes all LLM invocations exclusively through GitHub Copilot [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c].

# Architecture / Specification

### Model Access and Credential Isolation

All model inference routes strictly through GitHub Copilot using model specifiers formatted as `<provider-id>/<model-id>` with dotted versioning (such as `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7` and fallback `github-copilot/gpt-5.4`) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c]. The runtime rejects non-Copilot providers at startup to prevent unintended data routing [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c].

In CI environments, the agent does not maintain a static third-party API key; instead, it relies on workflow-scoped authorization via the `copilot-requests: write` GitHub Actions permission [^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73]. Copilot inference endpoints reject direct GitHub PAT tokens with HTTP 400 bad request responses, requiring an upstream token exchange against `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` using editor client headers to mint short-lived Copilot bearer tokens (`tid=...;exp=...;proxy-ep=...`) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c].

### Repository Permissions and Cross-Repo Isolation

Submission Analyser adheres to least privilege by enforcing `contents: read` permissions on GitHub tokens without repository write or issue modification rights [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]. When running cross-repository triage, the target repository is explicitly declared via `TARGET_REPOSITORY` and verified in workflow assertions to prevent unintentional evaluation of the runner's local issues [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]. Output publication is isolated to external channels via Google Drive service account integration and Discord webhooks [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

# Lifecycle History

- Detailed model routing rules, Copilot internal token exchange behaviors, and GitHub Actions `copilot-requests: write` permissions documented in repository specifications [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation body responsible for developing open telemetry standards, behavioral tracing specifications, and reference architectures across agent runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]. The group analyzes telemetry gaps in application-layer tools such as OpenTelemetry and evaluates multi-layer observability models spanning application logic down through kernel and accelerator hardware [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# Architecture / Specification

### Focus Areas and Layered Model

The group operates focus workstreams addressing core agent telemetry challenges [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]:
- **Protocols and Primitives**: Focuses on wire protocols, boundary envelopes, and interchange representations.
- **State, Context, and Reasoning**: Focuses on context session tracking, memory replay mechanisms, and agent decision correlation.

The group investigates a five-layer observability stack, evaluating gaps where application-level frameworks (Layer 5) fail to observe execution states in lower layers (including kernel scheduling, network paths, and hardware accelerators) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]. Associated initiatives include semantic conventions for [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), dynamic verification architectures, cross-layer field-level encryption, and Merkle link graphs for verifiable security records [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# Lifecycle History

- August 2026: Working group advanced term submissions to the AAIF taxonomy, reviewed five-layer observability stack gaps beyond OpenTelemetry, and structured open focus groups on protocols and state context [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

proposed_concept.title: Session
proposed_concept.description: A bounded span of agent activity that shares one accumulated working state, beginning when that state is created and ending when it is discarded or handed off.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

A session is a bounded span of agent activity that shares one accumulated working state, beginning when that state is created and ending when it is discarded or handed off [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-45].

# Scope and Semantics

The boundary of a session is determined by the lifecycle of its working state rather than by wall-clock time, transport connection stability, or user-visible conversation intervals [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-45]. A single ongoing conversation can span several consecutive sessions when working state is summarized, compressed, and reloaded into a fresh execution context [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-45]. Conversely, a single session can serve several distinct user interactions or subtasks as long as they share the active working state [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-45].

The physical storage location of the accumulated working state—whether maintained directly within model context windows, agent harness memory structures, or external temporary caches—is an implementation choice that does not alter whether an execution window constitutes a session [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-45]. Durable artifacts that intentionally survive the session boundary, such as persistent databases or saved file artifacts, represent outputs left behind by the session rather than active session state [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-45]. Similarly, a long-running background process that performs stateless polling or accumulates no state constitutes a process rather than a session [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History

The definition for Session was submitted as a universal taxonomy term to the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream in August 2026 to resolve an unpopulated placeholder [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-45].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Structured catalog categorizing agent observability requirements across operational domains, evidence integrity, and compliance use cases.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog documents functional, operational, and regulatory requirements that guide telemetry conventions and trace formats within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. It structures enterprise and builder needs into distinct operational clusters, establishing benchmark scenarios for agent execution tracing, debugging, and auditability.

# Specification and Categorization

The catalog structures use cases across operational domains, runtime monitoring, and safety and compliance clusters [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

## Safety and Compliance Cluster

The safety and compliance cluster addresses the verification, governance, and forensic analysis of autonomous agent actions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]:

- **E1–E3**: Focus on policy enforcement monitoring, safety boundary assertions, and internal compliance recording.
- **E4 - Tamper-Evident Evidence for Audit and Dispute Resolution**: Addresses the requirement for regulated organizations to prove to external auditors, regulatory authorities, or judicial proceedings what an agent actually executed [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

### Integrity and Cryptographic Requirements (E4)

Use Case E4 establishes concrete integrity requirements extending standard distributed tracing into verifiable audit trails [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]:
- **Merkle-Chained Records**: Cryptographically signed event journals that prevent retroactive modification, truncation, or reordering of agent trace sequences [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **WORM Storage**: Immutable write-once-read-many log sinks ensuring audit trail persistence [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **RFC 3161 Timestamps**: Trusted third-party timestamp tokens verifying the exact timing of agent tool invocation and human approvals [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Declared vs. Observed Linkage**: Strict cryptographic correlation binding an agent's declared intent to observed execution telemetry captured at protocol boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Evidence-Grade Ladder**: Standardized grading of audit trail defensibility against hierarchical evidence models, such as the WitnessOS progression ranging from E0 (Declared) to E4 (Anchored) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

# Lifecycle History

Use Case E4 and corresponding priority matrix ratings from industry participants were contributed to the working catalog through pull request review in the Observability and Traceability Working Group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to standardize telemetry conventions, cross-framework trace correlation models, and verifiable execution records for autonomous agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].

# Charter and Coordination Scope

The working group positions itself as a coordination forum rather than a competing standards organization, aligning industry efforts across agent telemetry and tracing frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11]. Its formal charter was approved internally by the working group on April 15, 2026, and submitted for AAIF Technical Committee review on April 21, 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].

## Liaison Roster and Cross-WG Tracking

To prevent duplication and maintain alignment across standards bodies, the working group maintains an active liaison roster and cross-group intake tracker [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11]:
- **External Standards Bodies**: Active coordination with OpenTelemetry GenAI, OWASP Agentic Open Schema (AOS), W3C Trace Context, Model Context Protocol (MCP), AGNTCY, and Monocle [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].
- **Internal Foundation Coordination**: Regular bidirectional coordination with the central [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and related AAIF technical working groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].
- **Intake and Follow-up**: Dedicated tracking of inbound requests, assigned liaison owners, recurring synchronization cadences, and outbound proposals [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Observability Prior Work Survey is a comparative landscape analysis maintained by the Observability and Traceability Working Group evaluating existing industry specifications, telemetry platforms, and action accountability mechanisms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23].

# Landscape Evaluation

The survey evaluates existing observability approaches to ensure AAIF initiatives adhere to an "interoperability over invention" approach without duplicating established work [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23].

## Evaluated Standards and Accountability Primitives

The survey maps complementary layers across the agent observability ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23]:
- **Session and Trace Telemetry**: OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions, OWASP AOS, and related frameworks answering what an agent did and documenting its structural execution trace [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23].
- **Post-Hoc Action Verification**: Emerging primitives such as `action_ref` / Mycelium Trails [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23]. While structural trace models capture workflow steps, `action_ref` addresses the orthogonal question of whether a particular recorded action can be independently verified by a third party who does not trust the reporting entity [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23]. Anchored in production systems (Arbitrum) and explored within IETF individual draft contributions, it operates beneath session telemetry to provide action accountability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23].

# Lifecycle History

In 2026, a contribution proposing the integration of `action_ref` / Mycelium Trails as entry #18 in the prior-work catalog was submitted for working group consideration [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining the six-step review workflow, engagement bar, and onboarding gates for AAIF project proposals.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process is the operating procedure governing how open-source projects are submitted, evaluated, approved, and onboarded into the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. It implements the intake, review, and progression criteria defined by the [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

The procedure is designed to default to asynchronous, offline execution via GitHub and LFX Vote, recognizing the geographically distributed nature of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and reducing live meeting overhead[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. Rather than requiring an upfront individual champion for every project, the process mandates an engagement bar: a minimum threshold of Technical Committee members must actively engage with a proposal before it can proceed to a formal vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Workflow Stages
The onboarding workflow consists of six sequential steps, an asynchronous parallel compliance track, and an optional on-demand presentation[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]:

1. **Step 1 - Initial Intake**: The CTO screens submissions for completeness and executes smoke tests assisted by an automated intake agent. TC chairs review the proposal via GitHub issue comments, and the CTO compiles the TC brief[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
2. **Step 2 - TC Q&A Window**: An asynchronous inspection period where TC members evaluate the submission and raise technical questions. If the mandatory engagement bar is not met, TC chairs initiate a search for an on-demand TC supporter; submissions lacking engagement or a supporter are rejected[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. An optional live presentation may be scheduled if requested by TC members[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
- **Contributor Paperwork (Parallel Track)**: Project submitters coordinate with the PMO to complete contributor agreements, trademark transfers, and technical charter drafting[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
3. **Step 3 - TC Vote**: The Technical Committee conducts an asynchronous vote on project admission and initial lifecycle stage assignment via LFX Vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
4. **Step 4 - GB Approval**: The Governing Board evaluates resource requirements and organizational alignment, voting on admission via LFX Vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
5. **Step 5 - LF Legal Formation**: Linux Foundation Legal finalizes the contribution agreement, technical charter, and asset transfers via DocuSign[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
6. **Step 6 - Technical Onboarding**: Project submitters and Linux Foundation IT execute technical repository migration, access control configuration, and infrastructure integration[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

## Roles and Responsibilities
- **Project Submitter**: Files proposals, responds to inquiries during the Q&A window, delivers presentations if requested, executes contributor paperwork, and performs technical onboarding[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
- **CTO**: Screens Step 1 submissions, conducts smoke tests with the intake agent, approves Q&A window extensions, and triggers the on-demand supporter mechanism[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
- **Intake Agent**: Automated agent executing public technical compliance checks on GitHub issues and private advisory reviews delivered to TC-only channels[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
- **TC Chairs**: Provide intake feedback in Step 1 and recruit a TC supporter if the engagement bar is unmet in Step 2[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
- **TC Supporter (On-Demand)**: A Technical Committee member designated when a submission fails to reach the organic engagement bar, shepherding the project through a restarted Q&A window[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
- **Technical Committee**: Evaluates proposals during Q&A and votes on admission and lifecycle stages[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
- **Governing Board, LF PMO, LF Legal, and LF IT**: Manage organizational readiness, legal execution, meeting coordination, and technical infrastructure onboarding[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Lifecycle History
- **Version 0.3 (August 28, 2026)**: Defined the six-step onboarding lifecycle, established the engagement bar to replace individual project champion requirements, integrated the automated intake agent, and formalized the on-demand supporter fallback mechanism[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Deterministic Acceptance Gate is an architectural pattern that decides whether a candidate agent output or state change may advance using explicit, repeatable checks rather than model self-assessment[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]. In autonomous or bounded workflows, allowing a generating model to evaluate its own result leaves the system vulnerable to confident yet ungrounded self-assessment[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

The pattern decouples evaluation from generation by testing candidates against predefined criteria such as automated test suites, JSON Schema validations, contracts, or explicit policy rules[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]. It forms a core verification component of [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) alongside [Bounded Convergence Loop](bounded-convergence-loop.md) and [Proposal/Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

# Architecture / Specification

## Mechanism
When an agent produces a candidate result with a declared operational scope, the deterministic gate performs two-factor verification[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]:
1. **Technical Criteria & Scope Validation**: Checks evaluate whether technical conditions are satisfied and ensure the action remains within task-level boundaries—including affected systems, allowed change classes, accessed data, and permitted tools[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
2. **Evidence Recording**: If acceptance criteria and scope validations pass, tamper-evident verification records are persisted and bound to the candidate's exact version or content digest[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
3. **Workflow Control**: If evaluation fails or evidence is insufficient, the gate returns the result to workflow orchestration. The enclosing workflow decides whether to iterate within budget limits, escalate, or halt[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

## Required Capabilities
- **Deterministic Evaluator**: Repeatable test runner, contract verifier, or schema validator independent of model reasoning[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Policy/Scope Validator**: Boundary checking component verifying that candidate outputs comply with permitted operational targets and action limits[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Evidence Store**: Storage repository retaining signed or verifiable evaluation records bound directly to candidate artifact digests[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

## Invariants
Implementations must uphold seven invariant guarantees[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]:
- Acceptance criteria are declared before evaluating candidate results[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- The gate operates independently of the model or agent producing the candidate output[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- Acceptance evidence is cryptographically or structurally bound to the evaluated candidate version or digest[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- Passing functional checks is insufficient if policy or scope verification fails[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- Failed, ambiguous, or unavailable gate evaluations never default to an accepted state[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- Workflows record all evaluation inputs, outcomes, and resulting decisions in an audit log[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- Gate authority is strictly limited to its declared contract; broader downstream modifications require independent authorization[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

## Failure Modes
- **Agent Self-Evaluation**: Allowing generating agents to assess output correctness converts hallucinated confidence into workflow truth[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Detached Evidence**: Failing to bind acceptance evidence to candidate digests permits stale evidence to authorize altered payloads[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Permissive Failure Defaults**: Treating gate evaluation outages or missing checks as acceptable advances unvalidated changes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Omitted Scope Boundary Validation**: Validating technical correctness without enforcing target constraints allows actions to exceed granted organizational authority[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural framework organizing agent reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than agent topology.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Job-Oriented Architecture Model is an architectural structuring principle defined by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group that organizes reference architectures around the job a practitioner needs an agentic system to perform[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424]. While topological metrics such as agent count ("single-agent" versus "multi-agent") provide structural context, they do not communicate the operational objective, behavioral guarantees, or failure boundaries of a workflow[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].

Under this framework, reference architectures function as practitioner routing checklists: builders evaluate whether an architecture fits their target use case, whether an adjacent variant applies, or whether individual reusable patterns provide sufficient control[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].

# Architecture / Specification

## Structural Taxonomy
The framework establishes explicit definitions distinguishing architectures, patterns, and scenarios[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424]:
- **Reference Architecture**: A complete composition defining reusable patterns, required capabilities, system boundaries, component relationships, guarantees, and exit states for a recognizable practitioner job[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424]. The architecture's name completes the sentence: *"We're building a ___"*[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].
- **Pattern**: A self-contained solution addressing a single recurring sub-problem that can be adopted independently or composed into multiple reference architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424]. Each pattern owns its own invariants and failure modes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].
- **Scenario**: Validation material demonstrating how an architecture behaves under a concrete, real-world use case[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424]. Scenarios serve strictly as test harnesses and validation benchmarks, not separate architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].

## Baseline Reference Architectures
The catalog establishes contrasting reference architectures addressing distinct practitioner jobs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424]:
- [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md): An agent drafts a proposal, an authorized human reviews and approves, and an isolated execution engine performs the protected modification[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424]. Composes [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), and [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].
- [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md): An agent iterates within a fenced problem boundary, an independent deterministic acceptance gate checks convergence, and bounded effects are committed[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424]. Composes [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md), and [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].

## Architectural Boundary Rules
Reference architectures must delineate deterministic and model-driven activities, identifying where conventional workflow logic provides repeatable, testable execution versus where open-ended reasoning requires generative models[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424]. Inside agent boundaries, deterministic code and ReAct-style iterative reasoning loops are treated as equivalent implementation choices[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].

mutations.rationale: Updates the bounded convergence loop pattern with authoritative invariants, evaluation boundaries, and architectural relationships from the merged specification.

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Convergence Loop
proposed_concept.description: Iterative workflow pattern safely executing agent attempts within strict budget, scope, and deterministic acceptance gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Bounded Convergence Loop is a workflow orchestration pattern that enables an agent to iterate on a bounded task until an external deterministic acceptance condition is met, or until declared resource limits terminate execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]. It addresses tasks that cannot reliably be resolved in a single step—such as lint errors, type corrections, dependency upgrades, or documentation fixes—without granting the probabilistic model open-ended authority or self-certification privileges[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].

This pattern is primarily utilized in [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) and relies on close composition with the [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](deterministic-acceptance-gate.md), [Proposal/Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md), and [Durable Wait](durable-wait.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].

# Architecture / Specification
The workflow engine orchestrates candidate generation while strictly isolating the evaluation and effect boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]:
1. **Task Admission:** An explicitly bounded task with pre-declared scope and capabilities is admitted.
2. **Agent Attempt:** The agent attempts work using only granted tools and constrained context.
3. **Deterministic Evaluation:** A deterministic acceptance gate independently tests candidate output against explicit criteria and scope boundaries.
4. **Retry Arbitration:** If the gate rejects the candidate, the workflow verifies configured retry budgets (iteration counts, wall-clock time, or cost caps). If budgets remain, another attempt is permitted; otherwise, the loop halts, fails, or escalates.
5. **Controlled Effect:** Once accepted, execution exits to apply the change through controlled mechanisms.

## Invariants
Implementations must enforce seven core invariants[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]:
- Scope, allowed capabilities, and acceptance criteria must be fixed before loop initiation.
- Agents cannot declare convergence; deterministic verification must evaluate every attempt.
- Every retry is bound by declared budgets (mandatory iteration limit, plus time or cost limits).
- Attempt counts, gate evaluation payloads, and terminal reasons must be logged in an audit trail.
- A gate failure can only lead to bounded retries, escalation, abstention, or recorded failure.
- Passing changes that violate declared task scope must not proceed to protected effects.
- Restarts must resume from persisted state without resetting iteration counters or budgets.

# Lifecycle History
Introduced and merged into `wg-workflows-and-process-integration` as part of the bounded autonomous remediation reference architecture pull request[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Architectural governance pattern separating intent proposal, authorization decisions, and workflow execution into distinct roles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Proposal/Execution Split is a foundational workflow governance pattern that separates intent generation, authorization, and execution into distinct, independently recorded roles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]. Because probabilistic models cannot provide deterministic compliance, legal attribution, or auditability, an agent must only propose immutable data payloads rather than directly triggering protected effects[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

Used within both [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md), this pattern coordinates with [Human Approval Gate](human-approval-gate.md) and [Durable Wait](durable-wait.md) to guarantee that actions match exact authorizations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern establishes three distinct roles and systems of record[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]:
- **Proposer (Agent):** Formulates candidate changes as immutable data payloads, lacking runtime privileges to execute protected effects.
- **Authorization Authority (Human or Policy):** Evaluates the exact immutable proposal against policy or human oversight, issuing signed or recorded decision evidence.
- **Executor (System):** A deterministic workflow engine component invoked only upon valid authorization to enact the exact approved payload.

## Invariants
- The proposal is immutable data; the agent cannot directly invoke the executor.
- Authorization applies strictly to the exact proposal payload without drift or modification.
- The authorization gate fails closed on missing, expired, or invalid decisions.
- Proposals, authorization records, and executed effects are recorded in an auditable system of record.
- Workflow retries must not execute duplicate effects for an authorized proposal.

# Lifecycle History
Authored and maintained under the `wg-workflows-and-process-integration` reference architectures repository, standardizing execution boundaries across autonomous and human-supervised workflows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution through declared budgets, deterministic gates, and escalation paths.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is a job-oriented reference architecture designed for scoped, automated issue resolution where an agent may safely iterate on solutions without human intervention before every effect[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26]. In contrast to human-gated architectures, an independent deterministic gate evaluates every candidate output, involving humans only when the workflow fails to converge or hits declared safety boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

This architecture composes the [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md), and [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture governs single-problem remediation runs through strict architectural requirements[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26]:
- **Pre-qualified Bounded Problem:** Each execution run handles exactly one fenced issue (such as a dependency bump or lint fix) with pre-declared scope and tool access.
- **Resource Boundaries:** Hard boundaries govern allowed execution iterations, wall-clock time, and cost expenditure.
- **Independent Acceptance Evidence:** Acceptance is determined solely by deterministic testing and static policy checks, prohibiting model self-certification.
- **Constrained Effect Execution:** Execution of the accepted outcome is limited strictly to the verified payload.
- **Terminal Escalation:** If convergence fails or scope is violated, execution transitions cleanly to recorded non-success, abstention, or human escalation.

## Use Case Validation
The architecture was validated against the AAIF Critical Use Cases inventory[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26]:
- **Autonomous Maintenance Run ("Night Shift"):** Candidate fit for executing recurring, bounded repository maintenance tasks autonomously.
- **Fleet-Wide Dependency & CVE Remediation:** Partial fit, serving as the per-repository execution unit while fleet-level discovery and fan-out require orchestration layers.

# Lifecycle History
Merged into the `wg-workflows-and-process-integration` repository via PR #26 as a contrasting reference model to single-agent human approval architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

proposed_concept.title: Activity
proposed_concept.description: A single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
An Activity is a single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. It serves as the atomic building block of structured workflows across agentic and automated processes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

Activities are composed to form workflows, where control flow logic governs their ordering, branching, synchronization, and durability[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

# Architecture / Specification
In the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group taxonomy, an Activity is formally distinguished from higher-level orchestration constructs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]:
- **Atomic Execution:** Represents a discrete unit of execution with observable completion criteria.
- **Defined Boundaries:** Operates over explicit input parameters and returns concrete output payloads or failure states.
- **Trackability:** Provides lifecycle checkpoints enabling state stores and workflow engines to monitor durability and progress.

# Lifecycle History
Adopted by the `wg-workflows-and-process-integration` workstream in PR #31 to replace earlier terminology ("Workflow Step" / "Workflow Task"), establishing an independent definition that avoids circular dependencies with the concept of a Workflow[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining evaluation frameworks, failure mode taxonomies, and engineering practices for agent reliability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group establishes standardized methodologies, taxonomies, and testing benchmarks to evaluate and enhance the operational correctness, robustness, and safety of agentic systems[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]. Co-chaired by Jordan Auge (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group produces failure mode classifications and empirical surveys for enterprise practitioners[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

Its key deliverables include Deliverable 1 (D1: Terminology and Taxonomy) contributing to cross-working-group landscape efforts, and Deliverable 2 (D2: Gap Analysis and Survey Support) addressing real-world agent failure modes[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its primary initiatives across structured workstreams[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]:
- **D1 Terminology & Taxonomy:** Developing shared definitions for accuracy dimensions, failure states, and verification metrics in PR #8 for integration into the AAIF shared taxonomy.
- **D2 Enterprise Survey & Gap Analysis:** Designing survey instruments (PR #9) targeting enterprise practitioners to gather empirical failure rate and prioritization data.
- **Phase 2 Coordination:** Preparing cross-working-group collaboration mechanisms and recruitment for advanced benchmarking efforts.

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group maintained active PR review cycles for D1 (PR #8) and finalized review on the D2 survey instrument (PR #9), while requesting [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) assistance for survey distribution across AAIF channels[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating shared agentic AI terminology, classification schemas, and the ecosystem landscape catalog.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation body tasked with defining standard agentic vocabulary, reconciling terminology across working groups, and curating the interactive Agentic AI Landscape [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream coordinates domain editors from horizontal technical groups to maintain consensus definitions and prevent taxonomic drift [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Architecture / Specification

### Term Review Process and Domain Coverage

The workstream operates regular terminology-review syncs and definition pull request cycles [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]:

- **Triage and Cull Ratio**: Candidate terms submitted by member groups undergo triage to evaluate domain necessity, universal applicability, or overlap with existing concepts. During August 2026, 53 candidate terms were evaluated: 37 were retained, 15 culled, and terms such as `Multi-agent misdirection` reserved for extended technical debate [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Contributing Domains**: Terms span [Governance, Risk & Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md), [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), [Workflows & Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), and [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Universal Terms**: Broad foundational primitives—such as `Agent`—are debated and anchored as universal baseline entries across all foundation deliverables [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

### Relational Modeling and Landscape Tracking

Definitions developed in the workstream model explicit structural boundaries and relationships between adjacent operational constructs [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]:

- [`Skill`](../taxonomy/skill.md) and [`Tool`](../taxonomy/tool.md)
- [`Kill switch`](../patterns/kill-switch.md) and `Reversibility`
- `Harness` and `Meta-harness`
- `Delegation` and `Handoff`

In addition to vocabulary terms, the workstream tracks industry solutions across landscape classifications, including Attestation & Verifiable Evidence and Agentic Vulnerability Enumeration [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08**: Reviewed 53 terms across three domain syncs; merged the canonical `Harness` definition (PR #37); opened definition proposals for `Human in the loop`, `Meta-harness`, [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) primitives, and workflow primitives; Leonardo Galesky joined to represent Agentic Commerce [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification standardizing agent execution entities, turn boundaries, session continuity, and provider interactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40]. It standardizes how agent harnesses and orchestration engines record execution turns, conversation sessions, tool invocations, and model interactions into vendor-neutral telemetry compatible with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].

# Architecture / Specification

### Baseline Telemetry and Gap Classification

The model establishes reproducible test workflows across reference implementations—including [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and independent multi-agent SDKs—to capture baseline telemetry and systematically classify behavioral discrepancies into four categories [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40]:

1. **Unsupported Behavior**: Scenarios where an agent runtime does not implement a given interaction pattern.
2. **Instrumentation Gaps**: Runtime states where semantic context (such as conversation or thread identifiers) is known internally but omitted from trace spans or metrics emission [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].
3. **Guidance Gaps**: Areas where telemetry conventions lack sufficient clarity for implementers.
4. **Semantic Gaps**: Abstract execution concepts requiring new telemetry attributes, events, or span semantics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].

### Cross-Trace Session and Turn Continuity

To trace long-running, asynchronous, or multi-day agent tasks, the specification avoids monolithic session-spanning trace spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]:

- **Turn and Session Linking**: Individual turns represent distinct execution traces, linked together across time via persistent session, conversation, or thread correlation IDs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].
- **Process Restarts and Reconnection**: When an agent session resumes following an idle timeout, process restart, or durable wait, subsequent turns join the original conversation record without requiring an open trace context [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].
- **Caller Context Preservation**: Supports child turns executed inside preexisting caller traces while retaining native agent identity and conversation bindings [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].

### Provider API and Tool Call Semantics

The specification decouples model provider protocol traces from downstream execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46]:

- **Tool Call Requests vs. Tool Execution**: Telemetry emitted during model provider API interactions capturing a tool call request (such as structured arguments) must not report that the [tool](../taxonomy/tool.md) executed until confirmed by an actual execution runtime [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].
- **Native Identifier Mapping**: Accommodates vendor SDK naming variations (such as threads versus sessions) by mapping native runtime scopes into unified standard attributes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08**: Formulated a nine-task execution plan defining baseline captures in Goose, turn continuity validation, and provider API conformance scenarios [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate post-purchase capability map structure (P1-P7) and bounded verdict envelope specification proposed for Deliverable 1 and Deliverable 2.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol alignments, and lifecycle standards for commercial agent transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group develops vendor-neutral architecture maps, protocols, and governance standards for AI agents executing commercial transactions on behalf of users and merchants [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]. Its charter covers the end-to-end commerce lifecycle, spanning product discovery, delegated negotiation, checkout, and automated post-purchase dispute resolution [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

# Architecture / Specification

### Capability Map: Post-Purchase Operations (P1–P7)

As part of Deliverable 1 (Capability Map), the group defines normative capability boundaries for post-purchase operations [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]:

- **P1: Eligibility Inquiry**: Autonomous discovery and validation of merchant return, exchange, or refund policies applicable to an order.
- **P2: Remedy Offer and Negotiation**: Multi-turn dialogue between customer and merchant agents negotiating restitution, store credit, or replacement terms.
- **P3: Buyer Authorization and Consent Evidence**: Cryptographic capture of explicit user sign-off for financial adjustments or returns.
- **P4: State-Change Execution Signals**: Emitted intent and dispatch signals informing order management and logistics engines of status updates.
- **P5: Evidence Binding**: Irreversible attachment of interaction transcripts, receipt records, and shipping carrier proofs to the transaction lifecycle.
- **P6: Dispute and Claims Initiation**: Structured escalation to payment networks or third-party mediation mechanisms when automated negotiation fails.
- **P7: Adjustment Ledger**: Verifiable ledger tracking debit, credit, refund, and balance restatements resulting from concluded post-purchase actions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

### Bounded Verdict Envelope

To facilitate interoperable auditability across merchant and buyer systems, post-purchase decisions are formalized into an 8-field machine-readable contract [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]:

1. `verdict`: The outcome determination (e.g., approved, rejected, escalated).
2. `verifier`: Identity reference of the verifying agent or policy system.
3. `verifier_signature`: Cryptographic signature over the verdict payload.
4. `evidence_refs`: URI or CID pointers to associated evidentiary artifacts.
5. `evidence_fingerprints`: Content digests validating evidence integrity.
6. `verification_basis`: Specific rule, contract clause, or policy cited for the verdict.
7. `witness_scope`: Verification boundary or custodial authority label (aligning with [Witness Scope](../taxonomy/witness-scope.md)).
8. `timestamp`: Standard UTC execution timestamp [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

### Protocol and Workgroup Alignment

The capability map cross-evaluates emerging commerce protocols—including Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP), AP2, and x402—while aligning evidence structures with the [Evidence Record Spec](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md) from the [Attestation & Evidence](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md) and [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) groups [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08**: Proposed post-purchase capabilities P1–P7 and bounded verdict envelope structure for Deliverables 1 and 2 (PR #6) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture enforcing explicit human authorization gates before an agent executes protected, high-impact, or published actions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture defines a reference pattern and execution boundary where an autonomous agent prepares action proposals but requires explicit, verifiable human authorization before applying state changes or publishing content [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]. By decoupling proposal generation from execution, the architecture ensures deterministic control over high-impact, irreversible, or externally visible operations.

This architecture instantiates the [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) patterns, binding proposals directly to validation and review boundaries documented in the [agentic-use-case-inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Architecture / Specification

The reference architecture organizes agent execution across three discrete operational boundaries:

1. **Proposal Generation Boundary**: The agent operates within a restricted workspace to analyze input, gather context, and synthesize proposed changes or assets without mutating live target state [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
2. **Review and Authorization Boundary**: The candidate proposal is submitted to a review queue where human operators evaluate proposed diffs, check guardrail adherence, and register authenticated approvals [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
3. **Execution and Publication Boundary**: Upon receipt of verified human approval, an isolated runner executes the approved payload against production endpoints or live stores [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

## Validated Content Use Cases

The architecture specifies concrete validation boundaries across several public and operational content publication scenarios [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]:

- **FAQ and Knowledge Base Updates**: The agent proposes content updates from resolved tickets or updated documentation; changes remain staged until technical support leads approve knowledge base release [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Release Notes Drafting**: The agent aggregates commits, pull requests, and issue discussions into customer-facing release notes, presenting a draft for product manager approval before changelog deployment [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
- **Catalog and Listing Descriptions**: The agent generates or revises product descriptions against structured product attributes, routing copy to brand or compliance reviewers prior to storefront publication [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Lifecycle History
- Validated against content publication scenarios (FAQ, knowledge bases, release notes, catalog listings) linking proposal, human approval, and publication boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol alignments, and dispute standards for agent-mediated transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group defines open capability models, interoperability baselines, and post-transaction governance for autonomous and agent-mediated commercial transactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]. The working group evaluates protocol alignment across checkout, payment rails, and delegation flows, ensuring trust and dispute accountability when human cardholders are absent from execution loops [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

Collaborating with related initiatives across the Agentic AI Foundation, the working group standardizes transactional primitives such as [agent-initiated-transaction](../taxonomy/agent-initiated-transaction.md), [agent-in-the-loop-transaction](../taxonomy/agent-in-the-loop-transaction.md), and [delegated-payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md).

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's technical agenda spans several foundational commerce layers:

## Payment Protocol and Rail Integration
The group analyzes low-level payment protocols including x402, an independent Linux Foundation project standardizing discrete value movement across HTTP, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) transports [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]. Key architectural dimensions include:
- **Rail Decomposition**: Decomposing payments into scheme, network, asset, and settlement mechanisms, coupled with narrow verify/settle facilitator contracts [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- **Capability Boundaries**: Distinguishing agent-layer intent and policy enforcement from discovery, reputation, and final settlement rail extensions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- **Micropayment Mechanisms**: Enabling pay-per-use micropayments for automated API consumption, content access, and context retrieval beyond standard cart checkout flows [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

## Post-Transaction Disputes and Accountability
In delegated agent transactions where the human cardholder was never directly present, traditional fraud evidence (such as click trails, browser fingerprints, and physical session telemetry) is absent [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]. The working group addresses this gap through:
- **Verifiable-Intent Records**: Cryptographically attested records establishing delegation scope, spending limits, and authorization parameters [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- **Know-Your-Agent (KYA) and Provenance**: Standardized agent identifiers, platform signatures, and model version metadata embedded in transaction payloads to support dispute reconstruction and buyer receipts [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- **Consent Surfaces**: Formalized structured representations of merchant terms and condition acceptances that agents currently bypass or implicitly acknowledge [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026**: Conducted deep dive on the x402 payment protocol, analyzing rail composition across AP2, UCP, and ACP, and convened PSP-led sessions on post-transaction dispute resolution and verifiable intent records [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- Scheduled forward evaluations of the Order Network eXchange (OnX) standard and Machine Payment Protocol (MPP) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining threat models, privacy guidelines, and defensive design patterns for secure agent execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes defensive architectures, threat modeling frameworks, and security best practices for autonomous agent deployments across the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]. Its scope includes runtime policy enforcement, tool sandboxing, supply-chain defense, and privacy-preserving execution models [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

The group maintains operational connections with the [identity-and-trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [observability-and-traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) working groups, standardizing patterns like the [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) and actionable guidelines such as [agentic-ai-security-best-practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group coordinates four primary technical workstreams:

1. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices**: A practitioner-focused guide detailing secrets management, tool invocation controls, guardrails, and runtime defenses. The first version freezes in September 2026 as the group's inaugural release deliverable [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]. In addition, the guide is being codified into machine-enforceable rules for static analysis tools across major vendor SDKs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
2. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: A catalog of reusable defensive architectures. Core patterns include multiple variants of containment kill switches, with memory isolation and state sanitation patterns expanding the catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
3. **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: An operational evaluation framework and review intake process designed to assess security assumptions across Foundation working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
4. **Taxonomy and Terminology**: Formalizing standardized security terms—such as privacy-preserving execution—into the AAIF common taxonomy in alignment with the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Lifecycle History
- **September 2026**: Decided to freeze and merge version 1 of the Security Best Practices Guide as an official WG release deliverable while excluding out-of-scope identity topics; initiated conversion of best practices into static analysis rules; integrated kill-switch patterns into the design pattern catalog; initiated cross-group outreach for the review checklist [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing common telemetry conventions, cross-framework agent tracing models, and verifiable action provenance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines interoperable telemetry models, execution tracing standards, and audit provenance architectures for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]. Its mandate covers application-level interactions, protocol transitions across Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) gateways, and lower-level infrastructure observability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

The group maintains active initiatives linking open telemetry specifications, including [agent-behavior-trace-model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) and cryptographic audit structures like [action-record](../taxonomy/action-record.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's roadmap encompasses multiple telemetry planes and focus groups:

## Primitives and Protocol Observability
The Primitives and Protocol Observability focus group coordinates stack-wide tracing and provenance across heterogeneous agent environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]:
- **Lower-Layer Observability**: Expanding scope below Layer 7 to capture system-level provenance, including kernel syscall tracing, cgroup throttling, and network events [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
- **Protocol Mediation**: Standardizing execution tracing across MCP applications, extensions, and Agent Gateway traffic proxies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

## Action Provenance and Verification
The group evaluates tamper-evident recording mechanisms, such as Agent Action Capsules, which operate as an intermediary verification layer between regulatory constraints and runtime agent actions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]. Using cryptographic proofs and ledger reconstruction, these mechanisms capture what actions were dispatched, what occurred during execution, and whether policy permitted the operation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

## Governance and Community Standards
The working group participates in cross-foundation efforts to formalize policies for AI-assisted contributions and establishes taxonomy pull request guidelines for observability terms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Lifecycle History
- **September 2026**: Formed consensus to incorporate lower-layer (below L7 syscall) observability into the Primitives and Protocol focus group; reviewed Agent Action Capsule implementation using MeshLLM for cryptographic dispatch verification; initiated foundation policy drafting for AI-assisted contributions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group serving as a bridge between international AI policy developments and technical standards across AAIF architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group bridges global AI legal frameworks, international regulatory standards, and practical engineering architectures within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]. The group translates statutory compliance, risk management guidelines, and auditability requirements into testable engineering invariants for agent systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

It collaborates with technical workstreams to ensure regulatory requirements inform core patterns such as [hard-constraint-gate](../patterns/hard-constraint-gate.md) and [attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).

# Architecture / Specification

The working group executes its deliverables across three distinct sequential phases [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]:

1. **Phase 1: Policy Instrument and Theme Identification**: Cataloging global legislative acts, regulatory rules, and governance frameworks, structuring them across approximately a dozen foundational themes (such as accountability, transparency, systemic risk, and human oversight) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
2. **Phase 2: Gap Analysis and Mapping**: Mapping identified governance themes against existing technical specifications, agent architectures, and execution protocols using standardized information extraction prompts to highlight unaddressed technical and compliance gaps [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
3. **Phase 3: Final Synthesis Deliverable**: Consolidating findings into a comprehensive regulatory alignment guide for autonomous systems, publishing technical guidance for compliance engineering [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

# Lifecycle History
- **July 2026**: Achieved working group consensus on the initial set of policy instruments and core thematic mappings; concluded Phase 1 landscape analysis and initiated Phase 2 gap analysis using automated extraction prompts [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].
