proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral specifications, attestation models, and authority delegation frameworks for AI agent identity and authorization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and reference viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3] The group ensures agents can be discovered across organizational perimeters, verify their operational identities, prove delegated authority, and present auditable human approval trails across administrative domains.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Leadership

The working group operates under leadership appointed by Platinum and Gold member representatives, serving an initial term from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

- **Chair**: Grant Miller (IBM)
- **Co-Chair**: Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE)

## Operations and Working Cadence

Working group activities run on a weekly cadence with alternating meeting slots to facilitate global participation:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

- **Meeting Schedule**: Every Thursday, alternating between 6:30 AM and 9:00 AM USA Pacific Time via LFX Zoom.
- **Meeting Records**: Running notes are maintained via public collaborative agendas, while session recordings and AI-assisted summaries are archived on LFX.
- **Communication**: Public discussions occur through the dedicated mailing list (`wg-identity-trust@lists.aaif.io`) and the official AAIF Discord community server.

## Strategic Focus and Invariant Principles

The group focuses on foundational trust models that interface with peer AAIF initiatives:

- Developing agent attestation profiles in coordination with [Attestation and Evidence](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md).
- Defining authorization and credential delegation frameworks connecting to [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) and [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).
- Advancing baseline identity primitives codified in [Agent Identity Primitives](../standards/agent-identity-primitives.md).

Participants contribute as individuals under the AAIF Commitment to Neutrality rather than as corporate delegates, ensuring balanced evaluation of open specifications.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]

# References

- [Agent Identity Primitives](../standards/agent-identity-primitives.md)
- [Attestation and Evidence Working Group](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md)
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Deep Dive
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference matrix and telemetry propagation model analyzing direct agent subprocess invocations across semantic and process-launch boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Deep Dive defines the observable propagation mechanics between an agent runtime and directly invoked local CLI child processes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] While an agent interacts with a tool at an abstract semantic level, local CLI realization concurrently crosses an operational operating-system process boundary where trace context, resource attribution, and causal relationships must cross during process creation rather than post-execution transcript ingestion.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]

# Architecture / Specification

## Boundary Decomposition

The reference execution hierarchy delineates agent decision context from local process execution:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]

```text
optional upstream caller
  └── agent turn / invocation
      └── tool execution span              ← Agent → Tool semantic boundary
          └── [optional CLI caller span]
              └── local CLI execution span ← Agent Runtime → Local Process boundary
                  └── CLI sub-operations and downstream calls
```

The interaction spans two distinct operational surfaces:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]
1. **Agent Execution Surface**: The model selects a tool, generating a call ID and sanitized arguments; the runtime checks authorizations and schedules execution.
2. **Operating-System Process Surface**: The runtime resolves binary paths, configures child process environment variables, spawns the child PID, monitors exit codes, and surfaces output back to the agent session.

## Filled Matrix Pass

| Observable Dimension | Telemetry Requirements | Standard Coverage | Identified Portability Gaps |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Identity** | Agent, principal, session/turn, tool call ID, executable path, process ID, telemetry service resource.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | OpenTelemetry GenAI (`gen_ai.tool.name`, `gen_ai.tool.call.id`) and OpenTelemetry CLI conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | Missing cross-runtime identity binding the agent call, child executable digest, and initiating principal.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] |
| **Context** | Active trace parent, invocation baggage, sanitized arguments, working directory, budgets, policy constraints.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | W3C Trace Context and OpenTelemetry normalized environment-variable carrier specifications.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | Runtimes filter child environments; no shared profile for passing turn deadline, execution budget, or security constraints.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] |
| **Relationship** | Turn-level causal ownership spanning launch spans, synchronous execution children, and detached links.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | OpenTelemetry GenAI `execute_tool` spans and CLI caller/callee conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | Late transcript instrumentation breaks child-visible causality; detached runs require standard span link conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] |
| **Lifecycle** | Selection, authorization, context preparation, process spawn, execution, exit/timeout/cancellation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | GenAI tool execution duration and OS exit codes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | Lack of standardized lifecycle representations joining agent policy approval delays, spawn failures, and background jobs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] |
| **Outcome** | Structured tool results, exit status, error classifications, side-effect manifestations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | CLI `process.exit.code` and `error.type`.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | Standard exit codes do not convey mutated files, downstream API calls, compensation actions, or sensitive payload masks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] |
| **Provenance** | Tool schema source, launching skill, binary hash, instrumentation scope, observer evidence class.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | OpenTelemetry Resource attributes and tool metadata.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] | Shell expansion and wrapper scripts obscure binaries; binary integrity hashes are rarely propagated into trace context.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b] |

## Implementation Patterns

Reference implementations (such as LoongSuite Pilot) validate that causal integrity requires pre-execution reservation: injecting `TRACEPARENT` into the process environment variables before child invocation, rather than reconciling spans asynchronously from completed session logs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]

# References

- [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md)
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand and Design System Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity rules, typography tokens, surface constraints, and trademark policies governing Agentic AI Foundation digital assets and reports.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Brand and Design System Guidelines establish normative visual standards, CSS design token extractions, typography hierarchies, and surface rules across all human-facing assets, Slack audits, presentation decks, and web reports.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] The system is engineered to prevent visual drift, enforce uncompromised aesthetic discipline, and maintain strict consistency between automated artifact generators and official Foundation identity.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

# Architecture / Specification

## Source of Truth and Token Pipeline

The brand architecture relies on a strict single source of truth and automated token synchronization:[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

- **Bundle Source**: `design/aaif-design-system.html` serves as the authoritative, self-extracting design system bundle containing tokens, component specifications, and responsive layouts.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Generated Tokens**: `design/aaif-tokens.css` is generated mechanically via `scripts/extract_design_tokens.py` to extract root variables; hand-editing is strictly prohibited and guarded by automated CI freshness checks.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Core Assets**: Vector mark lockups (`assets/aaif-mark.svg`, `assets/aaif-mark-square.svg`, and `assets/aaif-logo-white.svg`) must be consumed verbatim without manual redraws or stroke modifications.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

## Core Invariants

The design system enforces key constraints that counter common styling misconceptions:[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

1. **Primary Accent is Black**: The primary UI accent is strictly black (`--accent: var(--ink)`). The ten spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) serve exclusively as internal accents with a single leading hue per surface. Coral (`--spec-8`) is an accent token, not the brand primary color.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
2. **Typeface Discipline**: The entire system uses exactly one typeface—**Instrument Sans** (weights 400, 500, 600, 700)—for both display and interface copy. System monospace is restricted to metadata tags, eyebrow labels, and terminal outputs.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
3. **Medium-Weight Headings**: Headings must be set at weight 500 with tight tracking (`-0.02em`) and line-heights between 1.05 and 1.15, avoiding bold weights (with exceptions only for h5/h6 levels at weight 600).[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
4. **Flat Aesthetic and Hairline Depth**: Drop shadows are prohibited. Structural depth is conveyed through 1px hairlines, surface tint transitions (`--paper` → `--paper-2` → `--paper-3`), and inset borders. Cards, tables, and metric tiles remain square (`border-radius: 0`); pill radii are reserved strictly for standalone badges and buttons.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
5. **Surfaces and Dark Mode Prohibition**: The system recognizes two explicit surfaces: white editorial and black plate. There is no automated dark mode and no `prefers-color-scheme` media query; components are intentionally designed for specific contrast grounds.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
6. **Agent Motif Restrictions**: The modular agent avatar built from mark primitives is authorized for empty states, loading indicators, event badges, and section dividers; it is strictly forbidden in formal governance, board, regulatory, or press documents.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

# References

- [AAIF Brand Guidelines Skill](../skills/aaif-brand-guidelines.md)
- [Blog Guidelines](../guidelines/blog-guidelines.md)
- [Social Media Guidelines](../guidelines/social-media-guidelines.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing common telemetry conventions, cross-framework agent tracing models, and external standards liaison coordination.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines telemetry models, cross-framework event schemas, execution boundaries, and evaluation metrics for monitoring autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33] The group bridges foundational runtime execution events with distributed tracing platforms to ensure that multi-agent interactions, subagent delegations, tool calls, and human approvals are auditable and reproducible.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33]

# Architecture / Specification

## External and Cross-WG Coordination Tracking

Per charter coordination mandates, the group maintains a structured liaison roster and cross-working-group intake tracker to monitor aligned specifications and technical dependencies:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33]

### External Standards Liaisons
The group tracks formal relationships with six key external initiatives:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33]
- **OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG**: Harmonization of semantic conventions for generative AI agent invocations and tool execution spans.
- **OWASP AOS**: Alignment on agentic security logging and observability standards.
- **W3C Trace Context**: Standardization of distributed tracing carriers across local and distributed agent execution perimeters.
- **Agent Trace**: Tracking line-level attribution standards and code provenance frameworks.
- **Monocle**: Evaluation of open-source agent pipeline tracing tools.
- **AGNTCY**: Telemetry conventions for decentralized agent directories and interoperability protocols.

### Internal Foundation Coordination
Within the Agentic AI Foundation, the group synchronizes across several internal focal points:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-33]
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) for architectural approvals.
- Projects including Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Goose runtime implementations.
- Coordination with [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) regarding sanitized telemetry capture.
- Coordination with [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) on joint terms such as execution handoffs.
- Bi-weekly intake syncs with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).

# References

- [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md)
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)
- [Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Deep Dive](../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md)
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral specifications, attestation models, and authority delegation frameworks for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group (I&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to develop vendor-neutral, interoperable specifications, guidance, and reference architectures for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, authorization, discovery, consent, and trust[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]. Traditional identity infrastructures target human-to-application authentication or static workload-to-workload authorization, leaving open critical architectural questions regarding agent provenance, transitive delegation depth, human approval attestation, and cross-boundary auditability[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

The working group collaborates across foundation initiatives, aligning vocabulary with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and developing foundational frameworks including the [Agent Identity Primitives](../standards/agent-identity-primitives.md) draft specification[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f][^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-8].

# Architecture / Specification

To translate overarching problem statements into concrete specifications, the working group organizes work across three specialized breakout streams[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:

- **Use Cases Breakout**: Elicits identity and trust requirements from realistic enterprise and consumer deployment scenarios, establishing functional constraints for delegation and consent. Coordinated by Wei Chen[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Reference Architecture Breakout**: Identifies core architectural components, actor roles, trust boundaries, and interoperability gaps needed to support scalable agent identity and authority propagation. Coordinated by Brian Malone[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Taxonomy Coordination**: Formalizes domain-specific identity and trust terminology and harmonizes definitions across working groups via the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md). Liaison roles are led by Julianna Mealin and Leonardo Galesky[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

## Referenced Frameworks and Industry Inputs

The group evaluates leading external architectures and standards to distinguish settled baseline protocols from unsolved agent identity gaps[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:

- **[Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD)**: Decentralized capability publication, discovery, and federation protocol presented by Junjie Bu[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Uber Agent Identity Architecture**: Research by Matt Mathew and the Uber Engineering Security team detailing SPIFFE/SPIRE workload attestation, actor chains, per-hop token exchange, and policy enforcement[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **SPIFFE/SPIRE**: Foundational workload identity framework evaluated to assess its boundaries regarding human delegation context, autonomous agent identities, and cross-trust-domain portability[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **NVIDIA Secure Agent Workspace Reference Design**: Layered defense-in-depth model structuring identity isolation, delegated authorization, and runtime policy enforcement[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **IETF AI Agent Authentication and Authorization**: Internet-Draft (`draft-klrc-aiagent-auth`) establishing protocol boundaries and informing gaps in token exchange and delegation flows[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Lifecycle History

The working group meets bi-weekly on alternating Thursdays at 6:30 AM and 9:00 AM Pacific Time, archiving all meeting minutes, recordings, transcripts, and AI-generated summaries within the Linux Foundation LFX platform[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]. Work items evolve through collaborative working documents before formal review and submission to the repository as authoritative specifications[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]. Candidate implementations and open testing testbeds for live primitives are scheduled through the group's presentation agenda queue[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-c743b929b22e-3767aad0][^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-8].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Inventory is a curated AAIF reference catalog classifying production agent deployments across industry sectors, execution structures, coordination models, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] Maintained by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, the inventory maps real-world operational systems to the formal dimensions specified in the agentic use case classification schema.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

# Architecture / Specification
The inventory tracks enterprise agent deployments against structural architectural criteria, demanding primary source verification for every classification.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

### Production Deployments and Verifications
Key evaluated production systems and their verified structural topologies include:
- **Lead Research & Enrichment**: Classified as a `Sequential pipeline` based on documented multi-provider waterfall enrichment workflows where each provider query executes sequentially on prior lookup misses.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]
- **On-Call Incident Summary**: Classified as a [Parallel Fan-Out](../patterns/parallel-fan-out-and-join.md), `Inherently multi-agent`, and `AI-coordinated, planning` workflow based on SRE agent architectures that dynamically partition investigation context across concurrent sub-agents to avoid context window degradation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]
- **Contract Review & Red-Lining**: Mapped to `AI-coordinated, planning` based on legal review workflows that plan red-line reviews across distinct clause categories.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]
- **Autonomous Maintenance Run**: Mapped to autonomous code maintenance workflows citing research across vibe-coding SDLC models, dynamic agent CLI sessions, and issue tracker automations.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

### Citation and Integrity Criteria
Under working group classification guidance, rows without definitive implementation documentation indicating execution timing or dependency are preserved as `Unspecified: insufficient source detail` rather than speculatively classified.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] Candidate classifications for incident post-mortem drafting, network anomaly detection, and tax compliance tracking were reverted to unspecified status when cited vendor materials lacked evidence for deterministic gates or sequential execution order.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

# Lifecycle History
The inventory underwent source verification in pull request #39, establishing strict evidence requirements that resolved missing citations, repaired broken documentation references, and audited existing classifications against primary engineering documentation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] Ongoing reconciliation addresses lingering ambiguities between concurrency and dependency definitions across remaining unspecified cells.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]

# References
- [AAIF Workflows and Process Integration Working Group PR #39](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/pull/39)
- [Agentic Use Case Classification Schema](agentic-use-case-classification.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Schema
proposed_concept.description: Multi-dimensional taxonomy and classification schema characterizing agentic AI production deployments across execution topology, coordination, and autonomy.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification Schema defines the normative dimensional taxonomy used by the AAIF to characterize production agent deployments. Maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), the schema provides explicit criteria for categorizing agent implementations by execution structure, agent topology, coordination mechanism, and human oversight level.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]

# Architecture / Specification
The schema structures agent deployments across multiple orthogonal axes, including execution topology, coordination model, and autonomy levels.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]

### Execution Topology Dimensions
Deployments are categorized by primary workflow execution structure:
- **Sequential Pipeline**: Workflows characterized by ordered, dependent activities where the output of each discrete step feeds directly into the subsequent phase.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]
- **Parallel Fan-Out**: Workflows characterized by concurrent subtask dispatch across independent workers or tools.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]
- **Convergence Loop**: Iterative workflows evaluated against deterministic exit gates.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

### Definitional Open Questions
The working group identified a structural orthogonality conflict in the schema between `Parallel fan-out` (defined strictly by execution timing as concurrent subtasks) and `Sequential pipeline` (defined strictly by data dependency as sequential feeding).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47] Because timing and dependency are non-exclusive axes, workflows may exhibit attributes of both or neither, leading to unresolvable classifications in the [Use Case Inventory](agentic-use-case-inventory.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47] The working group is evaluating three conceptual models to reconcile this boundary:
1. **Timing as observed**: Categorizing strictly by concurrent vs. sequential execution time.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]
2. **Agent count**: Distinguishing single-agent sequential executions from multi-agent worker delegations.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]
3. **Dependency topology**: Categorizing primarily by data-flow dependency graphs regardless of concurrency.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]

# Lifecycle History
The classification schema was formally updated via pull request #47 to document the fan-out versus pipeline definitional conflict as an open governance question, informing active use case categorization in the inventory.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]

# References
- [AAIF Workflows and Process Integration Working Group PR #47](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/pull/47)
- [Agentic Use Case Inventory](agentic-use-case-inventory.md)

proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification standardizing agent execution entities, turn boundaries, and cross-framework semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification standardizing the structural entities, span hierarchies, and runtime state representations of agentic AI execution. Governed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model provides a vendor-neutral schema for instrumenting agent turns, conversation boundaries, and multi-agent delegation events.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

# Architecture / Specification
The specification establishes standard spans, contextual attributes, and cross-cutting correlation IDs across agent frameworks, ensuring telemetry can be ingested seamlessly by OpenTelemetry-compatible collectors and observability backends.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

### Upstream Contribution Strategy
The working group implements a structured nine-task execution plan designed to translate trace model findings into upstream industry standards.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47] Key integration vectors include:
- **OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions**: Contributing upstream telemetry guidance and schema changes to `semantic-conventions-genai`, specifically resolving turn-entry span identification and conversation lifecycle semantics.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]
- **AAIF Taxonomy & Landscape Alignment**: Proposing shared vocabulary terms and crosswalk definitions to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]
- **Runtime Instrumentation**: Directly contributing fixes to open-source agent frameworks that omit standard attributes such as conversation identifiers or turn-entry spans from emitted telemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

# Lifecycle History
Following working group discussions, the WG established a formal nine-task execution plan for the Agent Behavior Trace Model.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47] Task 9 tracks the upstream transfer of empirical trace model findings into OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and agent runtime repositories.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

- [OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions Repository](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation gates, and workload identity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide provides practical engineering recommendations for securing autonomous agent runtimes, tool integrations, and operational infrastructure. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the document outlines defense-in-depth controls spanning credential handling, role scoping, model guardrails, and runtime attestation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline defines security baselines across key agent architectural components:

### Secrets and Workload Identity
Agent runtimes require scoped, ephemeral credentials rather than static API keys or long-lived tokens.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
- **Baseline Single-Cloud Identity**: Standard workload identity configurations prescribe a 1-hour default token lifetime (configurable lower) with permissions bounded strictly by IAM role scope.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
- **Multi-Cloud and Hybrid Identity Workstreams**: Under active cross-group development with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), guidance is expanding to formalize federated workload identity for multi-cloud and hybrid environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23] Key architectural focus areas include:
  - OIDC-based workload identity federation across disparate cloud IAM providers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
  - Cross-cloud role assumption and least-privilege scoping across trust boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
  - Token lifetime limits and dynamic rotation patterns tailored for autonomous agent loops.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
  - Blast-radius containment and privilege escalation prevention when identity chains cross cloud boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
  - Cloud-to-on-premises federation patterns where native cloud workload identity is unavailable.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]

### Secure Tool Invocation and Guardrails
Architectures must separate intent proposal from tool execution, isolate subprocesses, and enforce strict parameter validation before external API invocation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]

# Lifecycle History
The guide's workload identity baseline was reviewed in WG Issue #23, initiating joint work with the Identity & Trust Working Group to standardize federated cross-cloud IAM patterns and hybrid trust boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]

# References
- [AAIF Security and Privacy WG Issue #23](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/issues/23)
- [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture resolving bounded problems iteratively using isolated work areas, independent deterministic acceptance gates, and constrained effect execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Bounded Autonomous Remediation reference architecture governs workflows that resolve small, bounded problems autonomously without requiring human authorization for every intermediate attempt [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. It contrasts with human-approved operations (such as [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)) by delegating repetitive problem-solving to an agent while maintaining strict invariants: declared execution budgets, independent deterministic validation gates, and strictly constrained effect executors [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture composes three core workflow patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Limits agent retry loops by enforcing finite execution budgets, resource ceilings, and termination predicates.
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Ensures an external deterministic validator—not the agent itself—evaluates candidate outcomes against schema, test, contract, or policy criteria before any side effect occurs.
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Separates proposal generation within an isolated workspace from the downstream executor applying changes.

### Required Logical Capabilities
The architecture requires eight distinct logical roles [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
1. **Execution Engine**: Admits tasks, sequences workflow steps, monitors retry counters, and triggers stop conditions.
2. **Bounded Agent/Tool Environment**: Constrains interpretation and operations to declared scopes and allowed tools.
3. **Isolated or Non-Authoritative Work Area**: Sandboxes scratchpads and draft artifacts away from production estates.
4. **Deterministic Acceptance Gate**: Executes multi-criteria tests, contract checks, and policy evaluations.
5. **State/Context Store**: Preserves checkpointed execution state and iteration context.
6. **Constrained Effect Executor**: Executes only the exact, validated proposal against external systems.
7. **Audit Log**: Captures an immutable trail of candidate outputs, evaluation decisions, and execution events.
8. **Escalation Surface**: Dispatches failures, budget exhaustion, or out-of-scope conditions to human operators.

### Validation Scenarios
The architecture incorporates concrete scenario evaluations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37]:
- **Autonomous Maintenance Run ("Night Shift")**: Validated against automated dependency upgrades and build remediation where candidate patches must satisfy a multi-criteria acceptance gate before opening pull requests [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].
- **Weekly Staff Schedule Generation**: Illustrative candidate scenario validating shift scheduling against labor rules before publishing roster drafts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

# Lifecycle History
- Proposed and drafted in the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- Updated with formal validation notes and multi-criteria acceptance gate rules in PR #37 [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

# Overview
The AAIF Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]. Established under the Foundation's Technical Charter, the TC oversees technical vision, open-source project lifecycles, cross-working-group architecture, and common best practices across Foundation initiatives [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

# Architecture / Specification
### Membership and Terms
Founding TC members were appointed by the AAIF Governing Board, serving an initial term from March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]:
- **David Soria Parra** (Chair) — Anthropic

- **Bradley Axen** — Block
- **James Ward** — Amazon Web Services
- **Nick Cooper** — OpenAI
- **Sambhav Kothari** — Bloomberg

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Validation Guide
proposed_concept.description: Operational framework and evaluation taxonomy classifying reference architecture candidate fit into Validated, Partial, No fit, and Candidate statuses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Reference Architecture Validation Guide provides contributors and working group members with a standardized process to evaluate candidate reference architectures against concrete enterprise use cases [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35]. Governed by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), this framework prevents speculative architectures by requiring documented evidence from real-world practitioner deployments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

# Architecture / Specification
### Classification Tiers
Validation evaluations assign one of four structured status labels to a reference architecture against a specific use case [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35]:
- **Validated**: The reference architecture completely satisfies the operational, boundary, and capability requirements of the use case without architectural modification.
- **Partial**: The architecture satisfies substantial portions of the job but exhibits minor gaps, unmodeled steps, or auxiliary constraints.
- **No fit**: Fundamental mismatches exist in the authority model, autonomy boundary, or effect reversibility (e.g., applying autonomous loops to irreversible high-impact actions).
- **Candidate**: A promising deployment scenario proposed for review that is still awaiting complete operational evidence or inventory verification.

### Contribution Rules
In accordance with contributor instructions and working group guidelines [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30]:
- Scenarios validate architectures; domain-specific examples must not be mistaken for the generic architecture name.
- Evaluations must rely strictly on supplied empirical evidence rather than hypothetical agent capabilities.
- Validation records are submitted as structured pull requests or issues adhering to standard templates.

# Lifecycle History
- Formulated during RA Workstream Sync #6 and adopted via PR #35 in the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification standardizing conversation scopes, turn lifecycles, proposed actions, and cross-framework OTel mappings.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and semantic convention specification being developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]. It standardizes how agent execution entities, multi-turn conversation boundaries, proposed tool actions, external observation results, and human-in-the-loop approval waits are represented across heterogeneous runtimes and mapped into OpenTelemetry (OTel) traces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Architecture / Specification
### Identity and Relationship Crosswalk
The specification establishes a versioned relationship contract defining the structural hierarchy of agent traces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]:
- **Conversation / Session Scope**: Encapsulates cumulative conversational state spanning multiple turns; individual turns within a conversation may be tracked across distinct trace identifiers while maintaining contextual session lineage.
- **Turns and Calls**: Delineates discrete agent reasoning and execution cycles, accommodating standalone turn traces while preserving inbound caller trace context.
- **Proposed Actions vs. Observations**: Decouples an agent's intent (e.g., proposed action `P1`) from downstream execution. If approval for `P1` is denied, trace context retains the reference to `P1` without requiring a synthetic tool execution span.
- **Approval Waits and Incomplete Observations**: Explicitly represents asynchronous pauses, human authorization gates, resumed execution contexts, and missing observational targets.
- **OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions**: Crosswalks AAIF behavioral primitives with upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.

# Lifecycle History
- Prioritized as Task 3 in the nine-task Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan emerging from the August 2026 Observability Working Group meetings [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Survey Specification
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question survey instrument gathering empirical practitioner evidence on enterprise agent deployment stages, failure modes, human oversight, and testing priorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Accuracy & Reliability Survey is a platform-neutral survey instrument authored by the Accuracy & Reliability Working Group to collect firsthand empirical data from practitioners deploying AI systems in production and pilot environments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. Comprising 16 core questions, the instrument evaluates real-world deployment maturity, practitioner activities, system architectures, accuracy barriers, operational failure consequences, and industry standardization priorities without imposing vendor-specific tooling[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

# Architecture / Specification

The survey specification establishes standard response structures and strict qualification gating across five structural sections[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]:

- **Response Formats**: Defines four standardized input paradigms: single select, multi-select, single-response Likert matrix, and conditional inline text entries[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Eligibility and Screening (Q1)**: Restricts detailed responses to practitioners with hands-on experience on systems reaching serious pilots, limited deployments, broad deployments, or recently paused/retired initiatives within the past six months[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. Respondents with generic prototype exposure or secondhand knowledge are routed to an early-exit closure[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Focal-System Framing (Q2–Q5)**: Enforces that subsequent answers evaluate a single specific "focal system" across direct practitioner activities (design, quality evaluation, runtime monitoring, approval oversight, usage, or management), operating domains, structural composition, and organization scale[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Benefits and Operational Challenges (Q6–Q8)**: Documents organizational constraints, human checking cadences, and principal business value realized[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Accuracy and Reliability Telemetry (Q9–Q13)**: Captures the frequency of unacceptable outputs, causal reliability factors, failure detection latency prior to business impact, most severe operational consequences, and primary verification evidence relied upon[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **Future Priorities (Q14–Q16)**: Elicits industry priorities for shared open benchmarks, failure catalogs, and technical guidelines[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

# Lifecycle History

The survey specification was published as an authoritative deliverable by the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to anchor research benchmarks in observable production conditions[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream curating a shared agentic vocabulary and ecosystem map through nominated Domain Editors across all vertical technical working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream serves as the horizontal architectural bridge across all seven top-level vertical Technical Working Groups in the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream operates not as a standalone working group, but as an intake, harmonization, and disambiguation forum that standardizes vocabularies and maintains the ecosystem landscape without encroaching on domain sovereignty[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Architecture / Specification

### Domain Editor Representation

Governance and cross-group alignment are maintained through nominated Domain Editors representing each vertical working group[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:

- [Accuracy & Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md): Casper Nielsen and Matthew Khouzam[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md): Leonardo Galesky[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md): Amithash Kankanallu Jagadish[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md): Julianna Mealin[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md): Pavan Sudheendra and Matt Lee[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md): Jautau White and Katherine Druckman[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Workflows & Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md): Sumanth Sathyanarayana[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]

### Architectural Guardrails

The workstream operates under strict structural boundaries[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]:

- **Horizontal Index Principle**: The workstream prioritizes consolidation over creation, harmonizing cross-cutting definitions that span two or more working groups while leaving deep domain-specific payloads (such as whitepapers and wire protocols) in vertical working group repositories[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Paired Contrast Disambiguation**: Adjacent or look-alike concepts (for example, Tool vs. Skill) must be explicitly contrasted rather than collapsed into ambiguous definitions, linking concepts via `relatedTerms` and `contrastsWith`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Anti-Erasure Guardrail**: Concepts cannot be deleted or folded into aliases without written sign-off from the owning working group's Domain Editor[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Operational Scope**: Contribution is currently restricted to the taxonomy; landscape contributions remain deferred pending formal process adoption[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Lifecycle History

Originally chartered to coordinate cross-cutting terminology, the workstream adopted an agile curation posture to evolve category buckets progressively rather than front-loading rigid taxonomy hierarchies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. Tracking metrics enforce cross-group citation utility, vendor diversity balance, and conflict resolution responsiveness[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contribution and Schema Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Authoring standards, SKOS-Lite data schema requirements, intake lifecycle stages, and local validation workflows for AAIF taxonomy contributions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Taxonomy Contribution Guide outlines the process, schema constraints, and technical workflows required to propose, review, and validate terms for the shared AAIF taxonomy[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]. Maintained by the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), these standards govern additions to the SKOS-Lite machine-readable vocabulary stored in `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

# Architecture / Specification

### Term Lifecycle

Proposals progress through five formal lifecycle gates[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:

1. **Candidate Identification**: A working group identifies a candidate term, articulating its agentic relevance, differentiation from general software definitions, and owning working group[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. Terms relevant to three or more groups may be marked Universal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
2. **Intake Spreadsheet Triage**: The term is logged in the Taxonomy Working Spreadsheet with one of three statuses: `Debate` (under review), `Keep` (accepted for definition work), or `Cull` (rejected as established generic software or security terminology)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
3. **Qualification Decision**: Candidate terms must demonstrate unique agentic AI meaning; generic concepts (e.g., "Red teaming") are culled[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
4. **Socialization**: Definitions are drafted with cross-working-group input[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
5. **Pull Request Submission**: Changes are submitted as Git branches tagging designated Domain Editors[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713].

### SKOS-Lite Data Schema and Field Rules

Entries in `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` adhere to explicit schema requirements[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]:

- `term` (String, Required): Unique display term in sentence case[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `category` (String, Required): **Deferred** for initial check-in; set to `""` pending cross-group categorization alignment[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `aliases` (Array of Strings, Required): Synonyms and legacy terms; empty array if none[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `broaderTerm` (String or null, Required): **Deferred**; set to `null` while hierarchical boundaries are settled[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `definition` (String, Required): **Deferred**; uses placeholder `"Definition pending — term accepted; definition under working group discussion."` until formal consensus[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `scopeNote` (String, Optional): Records historical context and working group boundary agreements[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `relatedTerms` / `contrastsWith` (Array of Strings, Optional): Implements explicit paired contrast linkages for adjacent concepts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `workgroups` (Array of Strings, Required): Owning or collaborating working groups; `"Universal"` is explicitly disallowed and must instead be denoted by an empty array `[]`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

### Local Validation and Git Workflow

Contributors validate changes using a zero-dependency local preview server (`python3 -m http.server 8000` or `npx serve -l 8000`) before opening a pull request[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713]. Pre-submission verification mandates checking Developer Tools console for JavaScript errors and ensuring link health with HTTPS endpoints[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713]. Landscape modifications are excluded from review until further notice[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining evaluation frameworks, failure mode taxonomies, survey instruments, and test reporting standards for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group establishes standardized evaluation methods, failure mode classifications, and measurement practices to assess the correctness, predictability, and operational resilience of agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. Represented on the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) by Casper Nielsen and Matthew Khouzam, the working group develops empirical surveys, test inventories, and benchmark reporting criteria to support rigorous evaluation across diverse enterprise deployments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11].

# Architecture / Specification

### Key Deliverables and Activities

- **Empirical Industry Survey**: Authored the platform-neutral [Accuracy & Reliability Survey](../resources/accuracy-and-reliability-survey.md), establishing a 16-question practitioner assessment evaluating deployment maturity, failure consequences, and testing needs across production environments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
- **D1 Deliverable Framework**: Under active development, the D1 workstream specifies testing vocabulary, benchmark inventories, and execution reporting standards[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11].
- **Coverage and Defect-Detection Reporting**: Proposed guidelines for D1 §9.4 mandate clear separation in coverage and mutation testing claims between declared inventories, selected evaluation subsets, fully exercised units, and uncompleted or excluded tests[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11]. For mutation analyses, the proposal mandates disaggregating detected, exercised-undetected, and unexercised seeded defects, rather than collapsing errors and timeouts into a single composite metric[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11].

# Lifecycle History

The working group operates under the Technical Committee governance, regularly reviewing community feedback on deliverable drafts and coordinating cross-cutting terminology through designated Domain Editors[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream serves as a horizontal architectural bridge across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), curating a standardized glossary of agentic AI terminology and maintaining an ecosystem map[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. The workstream eliminates siloed terminology across specialized foundation working groups, prevents redundant conceptual research, and provides enterprise stakeholders with a cohesive blueprint of the agentic AI technology stack[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Leadership
The workstream operates under appointed leadership nominated by working group chairs across the foundation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]:
- **Chair**: Junjie Bu (Google)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]
- **Co-Chair**: Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]

## Operational Cadence and Communication
- **Meetings**: Weekly on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT via LFX Meetings[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].
- **Mailing List**: `ws-taxonomy-landscape@lists.aaif.io`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].
- **Chat**: Discord channel `#ws-taxonomy-landscape`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

## Repository Structure and Contribution Boundary
The workstream repository is organized into distinct subdirectories governed by phased acceptance policies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]:
- `charter/`: Workstream charter and governance specifications.
- `taxonomy/`: Interactive shared taxonomy web explorer and SKOS-Lite vocabulary definitions.
- `landscape/`: Future-roadmap ecosystem architecture map.

The workstream enforces an explicit scope restriction: current contributions are limited exclusively to the shared **Taxonomy**[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. Pull requests proposing additions or changes to the **Landscape** are closed until a formalized landscape review and contribution process is formally ratified[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline and shared infrastructure managing chapter provisioning, estate lifecycle automation, identity resolution, and asset generation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations pipeline provides shared infrastructure, administrative automation, and directory synchronization across Google Workspace, Slack, and community event trackers[^evt-community-events-pr-44]. It standardizes chapter asset provisioning, enforces identity reconciliation between disparate platform identifiers, and automates design-system badge and document generation under strict safety invariants[^evt-community-events-pr-34][^evt-community-events-pr-39][^evt-community-events-pr-42].

# Architecture / Specification

## Multi-Platform Identity Reconciliation
Estate users frequently interact across distinct email addresses and handles[^evt-community-events-pr-44]. The pipeline resolves identities into three distinct columns on intake sheets without overwriting user-submitted intake email addresses[^evt-community-events-pr-44]:
- `Slack ID`: Immutable `U…` user identifier resolved via email lookup, avoiding mutable `@handles`[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- `Slack Email`: Account email address associated with the Slack profile[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- `Drive Email`: Email address holding active access on the chapter folder access control list (ACL), using visible `(no grant)` sentinels rather than blanks when unassigned[^evt-community-events-pr-44].

### Normalization and Safety Guards
- **Consumer Gmail Folding**: Lookup services fold dots and `+tags` strictly for consumer `gmail.com` and `googlemail.com` domains; custom Google Workspace domains enforce exact dot sensitivity to prevent cross-account collisions[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- **Name Match Guardrails**: Automatic write routines accept verified email lookups only. Name matching produces advisory suggestions requiring explicit `--apply` flags to prevent accidental assignment across identical names[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- **Whitespace Sanitization**: Inputs containing non-breaking spaces or empty variants are cleanly discarded to avoid inheriting previous iteration payload identifiers[^evt-community-events-pr-44].

## Asset and Document Generation Rules
- **Badge Hierarchies**: Chapter badges are stored in dedicated per-chapter `Badges/` subfolders within each chapter's Google Drive parent folder rather than a shared flat directory[^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Design System Badges**: Badges are generated via headless Chrome using Instrument Sans, live tokens from `design/aaif-tokens.css`, and deterministic per-chapter mascot scene palettes, with all display names XML-escaped to neutralize injection attempts[^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Font Embedding Policy**: In OOXML (`.docx`) document generation, `ox.NEVER_EMBED` mandates that fonts such as JetBrains Mono and Instrument Sans must be declared but never embedded, leveraging native Google Docs font availability to reduce file weight by ~210KB per document while retaining embedded Manrope metric fallbacks[^evt-community-events-pr-34].

- [Estate Sync Skill](../skills/aaif-sync.md)
- [Brand Guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Slack Audit Skill inspects community workspace structures, validating channel configurations, organizer membership rosters, and operational access boundaries against configured estate records[^evt-community-events-pr-44]. It identifies unreviewed participants in private channels, audits chapter organizer rooms, and verifies administrative hygiene across community spaces[^evt-community-events-pr-44].

# Architecture / Specification

## Staff Identification and Roster Scoping
To prevent false-positive alerts reporting authorized operations personnel as unvetted strangers in private rooms, the audit engine reconciles staff status across multiple configuration dimensions[^evt-community-events-pr-44]:
- **Ops Staff Allowlisting**: Evaluates members against both per-person `Ops staff email` entries and explicit `Ops staff domain` allowlists retrieved from estate configuration tabs[^evt-community-events-pr-44]. Missing configuration entries trigger explicit warnings rather than failing open[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- **Shared Organizer Rooms**: Handles scenarios where multiple chapters share a single operational channel (e.g., `#bay-area-organizers` shared by San Francisco and Silicon Valley chapters)[^evt-community-events-pr-44]. Roster verification reports cross-chapter members under an explicit `shared` key instead of flagging the room as unstaffed[^evt-community-events-pr-44].

## Identity Resolution Resilience
- **Strict Email Lookup**: Resolves member identities via Slack API email queries, accounting for consumer Gmail dot folding while preserving dot significance for custom Google Workspace domains[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- **Hydration Error Handling**: Differentiates between API token/network failures and genuine missing Slack accounts, preventing transient errors from classifying active organizers as absent[^evt-community-events-pr-44].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Estate Sync Skill synchronizes community channel states, permissions, and cloud storage mappings across Slack and Google Drive[^evt-community-events-pr-42][^evt-community-events-pr-43]. It provisions chapter spaces, manages controlled channel renames, seeds operational personnel, and posts administrative drive resources while enforcing least-privilege token boundaries[^evt-community-events-pr-42][^evt-community-events-pr-43].

# Architecture / Specification

## Channel Provisioning and Operational Seeding
When provisioning new or missing chapter spaces, the synchronization pipeline automates final workspace readiness[^evt-community-events-pr-42]:
- **Ops Account Seeding**: Automatically resolves ops staff emails via Slack lookups and invites them into private organizer channels, avoiding gaps in room administration[^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Organizer Drive Folder Links**: Posts chapter Google Drive folder links strictly into private organizer channels, preventing unauthorized access requests from public members[^evt-community-events-pr-42]. Folder URLs are rebuilt from validated IDs to prevent hyperlink anchor injections[^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Message Idempotency**: Post guards query channel message history directly rather than relying solely on pin status, preventing duplicate notification loops during retries[^evt-community-events-pr-42].

## Controlled Renaming and Permission Constraints
- **Explicit Rename Mapping**: Channel renames are mediated through an explicit `CHANNEL_RENAMES` map in configuration rather than arbitrary ad-hoc renaming scripts[^evt-community-events-pr-43]. Execution requires explicit `--write --i-have-approval` invocation[^evt-community-events-pr-43].
- **Scoped API Permissions**: Required OAuth scopes are restricted to `channels:write`, `groups:write`, and `chat:write`[^evt-community-events-pr-42]. Scopes such as `chat:delete` and `pins.remove` are deliberately withheld to prevent automated deletion of channel history or human unpinning decisions[^evt-community-events-pr-42][^evt-community-events-pr-43].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational provisioning and rebranding skill that creates and renames AAIF city chapters, generates Google Drive assets, and synchronizes presentation decks across the community estate.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` skill manages the lifecycle and asset provisioning of regional AAIF city chapters, handling template cloning, name transforms, presentation deck sweeps, and Drive resource setup.[^evt-community-events-pr-45]

The skill provides automated synchronization mechanisms for updating chapter slide decks and Google Workspace resources, ensuring consistency with foundation branding and project rosters across all global chapters.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]

# Architecture / Specification

### Chapter Renaming Pipeline

Chapter identity updates operate via `rename_chapter.py`, which executes in-place text transformations across four core surfaces: Drive folder hierarchies, chapter CRM workbooks, About documents, and design assets.[^evt-community-events-pr-45]

- **Slug and Token Isolation**: City name transformations are explicitly isolated from Luma event slugs and `aaif-<slug>` identifiers to prevent invalidating public chapter URLs or breaking existing links.[^evt-community-events-pr-45]
- **Verification Read-Back**: Asset changes are verified by re-reading metadata and content directly from Google Drive after modification.[^evt-community-events-pr-45]

### Estate Sweeps and Project Portfolio

The chapter deck maintenance tooling is structured around `deck_estate.py`, providing a modular estate-walking and verification pipeline for presentation templates.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]

- **Hosted Project Roster**: The `backfill_projects.py` script synchronizes the six official AAIF hosted projects across the About slide in chapter templates: `MCP`, `goose`, `AGENTS.md`, `agentgateway`, `A2A`, and `Agent Router`.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]
- **Matching and Overflow Invariants**: Slide inspection detects the roster via the `THE PROJECTS` section eyebrow rather than string matching, preserving custom chapter phrasing.[^evt-community-events-pr-46] Geometry and font sizes adapt dynamically to fit six entries, reporting explicit overflow errors if bounding boxes collide rather than silently corrupting slide layouts.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]
- **Execution Contracts**: Deck processing defines distinct download, sweep, and upload phases, verifying Drive storage state using the Google Workspace CLI before marking files as clean.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]

# Lifecycle History

Originally written to handle one-time chapter cloning, `aaif-create-chapter` evolved to support bidirectional renames and continuous template updates as part of [community-event-operations](./community-event-operations.md).[^evt-community-events-pr-45] In PR #46, shared sweep routines were consolidated into `deck_estate.py` and the About slide template was expanded to accommodate all six hosted foundation initiatives.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-sync` skill automates bidirectional synchronization between AAIF central intake systems, chapter Customer Relationship Management (CRM) sheets, Slack workspaces, and Google Drive access permissions.[^evt-community-events-pr-28][^evt-community-events-pr-36]

It enforces strict data validation, non-destructive messaging, and safe permission management to ensure organizers and attendees are routed accurately without overwriting manual community contributions.[^evt-community-events-pr-36][^evt-community-events-pr-45]

# Architecture / Specification

### CRM Pipeline and Status Decoupling

Chapter CRM spreadsheets decouple candidate application roles from workflow decision states:[^evt-community-events-pr-28]

- **Status vs. Interested In**: The `Status` column captures lifecycle decisions (`Prospect`, `In progress`, `Interviewing`, `Tentative`, `Accepted`, `Attended`, `Regular`, `Volunteer`, `Declined`), while the `Interested in` column (Column L) records application roles (`Organizer`, `Speaker`, `Host`).[^evt-community-events-pr-28]
- **Detail Field Population**: Merges and populates candidate profile data including `LinkedIn URL`, `Company`, `Role / title`, and `Technical expertise`, reserving the `Signal` column exclusively for human notes.[^evt-community-events-pr-28]
- **Schema Drift Protection**: `sync_crm` detects sheet schema discrepancies and halts execution against unmigrated workbooks rather than performing misaligned column writes.[^evt-community-events-pr-28]

### Google Drive Access Control

Organizer permissions are granted via `sync_access.py` using functional Google account matching:[^evt-community-events-pr-45]

- **Drive Email Routing**: A dedicated `Drive Email` column supplies the operational Google account target for Drive write access while keeping original intake contact emails immutable.[^evt-community-events-pr-45]
- **Safety Invariants**: Access grants require valid email overrides; contradictory rows or `(no grant)` sentinels drop automated grants loudly to prevent unauthorized permission sprawl.[^evt-community-events-pr-45]

### Slack Country Channels and Directory Sync

Slack channel synchronization reconciles local chapters with shared national or regional hubs:[^evt-community-events-pr-36]

- **Scoped Invites**: `invite_organizers.py` provides `--scope {organizer,country,both}` to invite chapter organizers to public country channels, deduplicating rosters by resolved Slack accounts across multiple chapters sharing a channel.[^evt-community-events-pr-36]
- **Country Channel Resolution**: Reconciles non-standard country room names (`#deutschland`, `#nordics`, `#korea`, `#brasil`) against a centralized `COUNTRY_CHANNELS` mapping table.[^evt-community-events-pr-36]
- **Additive Directory Posts**: `post_country_directory.py` publishes and appends chapter directory information to country channels without modifying or replacing custom messages written by human organizers.[^evt-community-events-pr-36]

### Luma Feed Integration

Chapter feed processing decouples row creation from external event publication:[^evt-community-events-pr-45]

- **Opt-In Luma Requirement**: Row generation supports `--require-luma` as an optional constraint rather than a hard block on initial registration.[^evt-community-events-pr-45]
- **Estate-Wide Luma Audit**: The `--audit-luma` flag audits all existing rows in the feed for missing or broken (HTTP 404) `Chapter Luma Link` targets.[^evt-community-events-pr-45]

# Lifecycle History

Initially developed for 1:1 chapter folder and channel provisioning, `aaif-sync` was overhauled across PRs #28, #36, and #45 to address edge cases in regional channel sharing, CRM data flattening, and Google Workspace account mismatches.[^evt-community-events-pr-28][^evt-community-events-pr-36][^evt-community-events-pr-45]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-audit-slack` skill inspects AAIF Slack workspace channels and memberships to detect orphaned rooms, missing organizer assignments, permission drift, and message compliance issues.[^evt-community-events-pr-36]

It provides detailed reporting to workspace administrators and estate sync engines, identifying actionable onboarding tasks and data discrepancies.[^evt-community-events-pr-36]

# Architecture / Specification

### Organizer Gap Classification

The `summarize_audits.py` tool categorizes missing chapter organizer memberships into distinct operational queues:[^evt-community-events-pr-36]

- **Invite Gaps (`gaps`)**: Organizers who possess an active Slack account matching their intake email but have not been invited to their respective private organizer or country channels.[^evt-community-events-pr-36]
- **Missing Accounts (`no_account`)**: Intake records where no registered Slack account exists under the provided email address, categorized as an intake data-quality issue rather than a Slack routing failure.[^evt-community-events-pr-36]
- **Channel Decoupling**: Finding classification operates independently of whether a chapter's private organizer channel has already been provisioned, ensuring newly created chapters surface intake discrepancies immediately.[^evt-community-events-pr-36]

# Lifecycle History

Prior to PR #36, `summarize_audits.py` conflated missing Slack accounts with uninvited members, artificially inflating actionable channel backlog metrics.[^evt-community-events-pr-36] PR #36 split these buckets, introduced dedicated test suites, and aligned findings with [aaif-sync](./aaif-sync.md).[^evt-community-events-pr-36]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `community-event-operations` suite provides the shared automation infrastructure, design conformance checks, and operational orchestration supporting the global AAIF community chapter network.[^evt-community-events-pr-32][^evt-community-events-pr-45]

It underpins specialized community skills—such as [aaif-create-chapter](./aaif-create-chapter.md), [aaif-sync](./aaif-sync.md), and [aaif-audit-slack](./aaif-audit-slack.md)—by providing common libraries, data schemas, and design token enforcement across Google Workspace and Office Open XML (OOXML) documents.[^evt-community-events-pr-32][^evt-community-events-pr-46]

# Architecture / Specification

### OOXML Design System Conformance

Document formatting and brand identity across spreadsheets, slide decks, and Word files are governed by `lib/aaif_events/ooxml_style.py` and `contrast.py`:[^evt-community-events-pr-32]

- **Typography and Tokens**: Standardizes presentation and document typography on Instrument Sans, replacing legacy faces (Space Grotesk, Manrope, Arial, Calibri) and applying AAIF color tokens across DrawingML and SpreadsheetML formats.[^evt-community-events-pr-32]
- **Minimal-Diff Rewrites**: XML updates modify only font typeface and color attributes while preserving `AlternateContent` blocks and relationship identifiers.[^evt-community-events-pr-32]
- **Automated Contrast Verification**: Resolves effective foreground and background luminance hierarchies (shape fill → slide background → layout → master) to prevent unreadable pairings such as black text on dark plates.[^evt-community-events-pr-32]

### Shared Estate Sweeps

Common estate-wide maintenance sweeps are centralized in `deck_estate.py`:[^evt-community-events-pr-46]

- **Estate Walk Contracts**: Implements structured per-file download, parse, rewrite, and upload verification patterns across chapter templates and series decks.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]
- **Non-Destructive Invariants**: Scripts target semantic structure (such as section eyebrows) rather than hardcoded text, skipping human-customized copy and raising explicit warnings on layout overflows.[^evt-community-events-pr-46]

### Identity and Access Architecture

The operational estate separates individual user identity across intake, authentication, and communication surfaces:[^evt-community-events-pr-28][^evt-community-events-pr-45]

- **Decoupled Application Decisions**: Chapter CRM sheets isolate applied roles from organizational decisions via split `Interested in` and `Status` columns.[^evt-community-events-pr-28]
- **Drive ACL Delegation**: Grants write access to verified Google account addresses via `Drive Email` overrides without rewriting primary applicant contact information.[^evt-community-events-pr-45]
- **Communication Routing**: Deduplicates multi-chapter organizer rosters and routes announcements to country-level channels while preserving localized room names.[^evt-community-events-pr-36]

# Lifecycle History

The community operations engine expanded iteratively through several infrastructure milestones: schema normalization in PR #28, full OOXML design system conformance in PR #32, country-channel routing in PR #36, resilient Drive ACL routing and chapter renaming in PR #45, and modular estate sweeps for six hosted foundation projects in PR #46.[^evt-community-events-pr-28][^evt-community-events-pr-32][^evt-community-events-pr-36][^evt-community-events-pr-45][^evt-community-events-pr-46]
