proposed_concept.title: Prior Work in Agent Observability
proposed_concept.description: Comparative landscape survey analyzing open specifications, industry standards, protocols, and platforms across agent observability and telemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Prior Work in Agent Observability is a living landscape survey maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]. It surveys existing specifications, data formats, open-source platforms, and academic research relevant to agentic telemetry, providing a common foundation for AAIF standards like the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

# Architecture / Specification

### Landscape Refresh Highlights (June–August 2026)

The landscape reflects significant specification maturation and protocol consolidation across industry bodies[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]:

- **OpenTelemetry GenAI Standards Repository**: OpenTelemetry established a dedicated repository (`open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai`) for GenAI semantic conventions, standardizing explicit spans for `create-agent`, `invoke-agent`, `invoke-workflow`, `execute-tool`, and `plan`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF)**: OCSF Schema 1.9 introduced an agent-specific profile defining AI Operation, AI Agent, Delegation, and Record Integrity classes, enabling normalized security event logging for agent actions and delegated authority[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **OWASP Agent Observability Standard (AOS)**: AOS separated its specification surface into distinct Instrument, Trace, and Inspect specifications, establishing mappings for OpenTelemetry, OCSF, and AgBOM software supply-chain standards (CycloneDX/SPDX/SWID)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **AGNTCY Observe**: The AGNTCY Observe SDK (`v1.0.43`) provides protocol-level telemetry interception across A2A, SLIM, and MCP with distributed trace recomposition over multi-agent boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Protocol**: Following its accession to AAIF in August 2026, A2A v1.0 standardizes signed agent cards, cross-vendor task delegation, and nested step trace extensions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Environment-Derived Instrumentation**: OTel eBPF instrumentation (including OBI) provides kernel-level, unforgeable network and execution signals that complement framework-emitted telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Focused Attribution Formats**: Specialized formats like Cursor Agent Trace (v0.1.0) remain focused on narrow AI code attribution within developer tools[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

### Comparative Matrix

| Initiative | Scope | Maturity | Format / License | Primary Focus |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OTel GenAI SemConv** | LLM, agent, workflow, tool, MCP spans/events | Active Development | Open (Apache 2.0) | Broad multi-vendor runtime telemetry |
| **OWASP AOS** | Security, auditing, AgBOM mapping | Draft / Active | Open | Compliance, guardrail violation auditing |
| **OCSF (v1.9)** | AI agent identity, delegation, integrity | Production Schema | Open | Security incident and audit evidence |
| **AGNTCY Observe** | Multi-agent context propagation | SDK v1.0.43 | Open (Apache 2.0) | Cross-agent protocol boundary reconstruction |
| **Agent Trace (Cursor)** | Source code attribution | RFC v0.1.0 | Open (CC BY 4.0) | Line-level IDE code generation provenance |
| **Monocle (LF AI & Data)**| GenAI framework auto-instrumentation | v0.8.4 | Open (Apache 2.0) | Non-intrusive trace wrapper generation |

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-15**: Initial landscape survey drafted by the AAIF Observability Working Group[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **2026-08-13**: Comprehensive refresh capturing dedicated OTel GenAI repository separation, OCSF 1.9 AI Agent profile, A2A AAIF accession, and AOS multi-part specifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

# References

- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)
- [Agent-MCP Server Boundary](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md)
- [Agntcy](../resources/agntcy.md)

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining threat models, privacy guidelines, review checklists, and defensive design patterns for autonomous agent deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an active AAIF technical body focused on hardening agentic architectures against autonomous security failures, data leakage, and supply chain attacks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6]. Co-chaired by Alex Frazer and Junjie Bu, the group develops threat modeling frameworks, defensive design patterns, security review checklists, and operational best practices guides[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# Architecture / Specification

### Primary Workstreams and Status

1. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices**: A practitioner guide detailing secure credential isolation, static code smell checks, tool invocation permissions, and guardrail controls (led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Erin Farr)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6]. Version 1 completed extensive community review (~88 review comments resolved) before final merge[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
2. **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: A comparative assessment contrasting OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Systems and MITRE ATLAS against production agent vulnerabilities[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6]. The first draft PR was posted in August 2026, resuming active iteration following the best practices publication[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
3. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: An intake framework led by Govindaraj Palanisamy to audit overlapping security, privacy, and identity requirements across AAIF groups (notably [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), and [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
4. **Taxonomy & Landscape Alignment**: Active term intake curating security definitions using a dedicated taxonomy browser tool that logs model provenance and human edit distance for generated drafts[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
5. **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural security patterns including isolated runtimes, policy boundaries, and hardware-enforced checkpoints[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

### External Standards and Ecosystem Coordination

- **ETSI TC SAI**: Tracking the European Norm cybersecurity work item extending AI service requirements to autonomous agents with potential bidirectional liaison[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **MicroVM Isolation**: Assessing hypervisor and microVM sandbox architectures (such as Eclipse Enclave) as stronger isolation boundaries than standard container environments for preventing agent escapes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **FINOS Labs**: Monitoring the Open Enterprise Agent Governance and Orchestration project for compliance overlap with AAIF protocol gateways[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08-18**: Evaluated cross-boundary observability frameworks, local chapter activations, and protocol workstream consolidation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].
- **2026-09-15**: Closed comment period on Best Practices v1, integrated taxonomy provenance tracking tooling, instituted quiet-period PR merge norms, and reviewed ETSI liaison proposals[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# References

- [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)
- [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)
- [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Structured catalog detailing operational agent observability use cases, cross-cutting telemetry requirements, and evaluation priorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog is an inventory document maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) defining visibility requirements across agent engineering, operations, security, and governance[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]. It standardizes how practitioners evaluate observability gaps across debugging, cost control, code attribution, evaluation, safety, multi-agent systems, operational monitoring, research, and identity resolution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

# Architecture / Specification

Each catalog entry defines a practitioner task, target role personas, required telemetry fields, and current state gaps in existing tooling[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

### Cross-Cutting Telemetry Requirements

All use cases assume five foundational telemetry guarantees[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]:

- **Source and Trust:** Telemetry must declare its producer and observation point, distinguishing agent [self-reported](../taxonomy/self-reported.md) claims from framework, gateway, sandbox, OS, or security sensor evidence, noting available cryptographic attestation or tamper-evidence mechanisms[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Privacy and Governance:** Context, identity, and correlation fields must carry policy metadata sufficient to enforce minimization, data classification, redaction, consent, residency, and credential exclusion[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Completeness and Sampling:** Telemetry streams must declare sampling decisions, collection gaps, and dropped counts, separating discardable telemetry from audit-mandated records[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Schema Evolution:** Records must capture schema, semantic convention, agent, model, tool, and configuration versions to enable historical comparison[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Correlation and Causality:** Telemetry requires stable identifiers and causal links across sessions, tasks, delegations, and tools rather than relying solely on wall-clock order or single parent-child span hierarchies[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

### Operational Categories

The catalog organizes requirements into nine domains[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]:

1. **A. Debugging and Root Cause Analysis:** Explaining rationale (A1), detecting execution bottlenecks and retry loops (A2), and reproducing agent runs (A3)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
2. **B. Cost Management and Optimization:** Session costs (B1), outcome cost efficiency (B2), and token waste identification (B3)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
3. **C. Code Attribution and Provenance:** AI code attribution (C1) and security review of generated artifacts (C2)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
4. **D. Evaluation and Quality Assurance:** Capability evaluations (D1), regression detection (D2), and configuration benchmarking (D3)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
5. **E. Safety and Compliance:** Real-world action logs (E1), scope enforcement (E2), regulated environment audit trails (E3), and tamper-evident evidence for dispute resolution (E4)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].
6. **F. Multi-Agent Systems:** Cross-boundary tracing (F1) and agent-to-agent protocol telemetry (F2)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
7. **G. Operational Monitoring:** Health monitoring (G1) and fleet capacity planning (G2)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
8. **H. Research and Improvement:** Failure mode discovery (H1), fine-tuning data extraction (H2), and cross-implementation benchmarking (H3)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
9. **I. Identity and Ownership:** Cross-surface identity resolution (I1)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].

# Lifecycle History

First compiled in March 2026, the use cases catalog was updated in August 2026 with additions including E4 (tamper-evident evidence) and I1 (cross-surface identity resolution)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53]. Alignment efforts with the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) address notation overlaps between use case IDs and evidence-grade classifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification standardizing conversation scopes, turn lifecycles, and independent trace interpretation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and event correlation specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to standardize agent execution records across frameworks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. It establishes normative representations for conversational turns, tool interactions, approval checkpoints, and external actions, enabling consistent behavioral analysis across heterogeneous agent runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Architecture / Specification

The specification requires that trace representations be interpretable by independent consumers without reliance on producer runtime context[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

### Independent Interpretation Constraints

To establish portable interoperability, the model defines verification criteria for independent telemetry readers and query engines[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]:

- **No Hidden Runtime State:** Independent consumers must reconstruct execution lifecycles without accessing producer memory, private fixture mappings, or proprietary helper libraries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Arrival Order Robustness:** Query paths must derive identical state conclusions regardless of record arrival order, accurately linking proposals, approvals, tool invocations, and environmental outcomes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Partial and Conflicting Evidence Handling:** Readers must explicitly detect missing receipts or conflicting reports (e.g., classifying an external effect as unconfirmed when an execution record exists without a corresponding service receipt)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Explicit Causal Linkages:** Operations must link explicitly across multi-turn and asynchronous execution boundaries rather than assuming monotonic wall-clock ordering[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History

During August 2026 working group meetings, the workstream adopted a nine-task execution plan[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. Task 7 specifies testing requirements for independent telemetry interpretation to verify that third-party tooling produces consistent semantic graphs across varied trace topologies[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG Workflows & Process Integration) develops vendor-neutral workflow primitives, execution models, and reference architectures for enterprise agentic systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7] Chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the group focuses on standardizing how agents decompose goals, execute activities, coordinate across organizational boundaries, and interface with human approval processes.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group is organized into three collaborative work streams:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **Reference Architectures:** Authors end-to-end operational models and design patterns. Core assets include the architectural principles guideline, contribution guide, and pattern architectures such as [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) ("human-approved operation") and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7] Candidate architectures are assessed against a four-outcome validation matrix (`validated`, `partial`, `candidate`, `no fit`) based on job and boundary alignment.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **Taxonomy:** Formulates core workflow vocabulary. In August 2026, the work stream delivered the Phase One Core Terms draft—the first shipped asset across the AAIF—defining decoupled baseline primitives like [Activity](../taxonomy/activity.md) while scoping out gate/evaluation mechanics to partner working groups.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **Critical Use Cases:** Maintains an empirical catalog of enterprise workflow deployments, aligning field operational patterns with standardized terminology.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, WG Workflows & Process Integration completed the Phase One Core Terms vote at the foundation plenary, becoming the first AAIF working group to ship an official deliverable.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7] The group also merged core architecture principles, advanced reference architecture implementations, and instituted operational repository policies, including a standing pull-request size ceiling (~10 files) following oversized PR deferrals.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry models, execution trace formats, and cross-boundary correlation for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG Observability & Traceability) establishes vendor-neutral telemetry conventions, correlation models, and tracing standards for agentic architectures.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the working group defines cross-runtime observability to capture agent reasoning trajectories, tool invocations, and multi-agent interactions across heterogeneous infrastructure.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

# Architecture / Specification
The group's technical initiatives span several key architectural domains:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** Developing an open standard led by Matthew Lee to preserve causal execution context across SDKs, gateways, and backends via portable telemetry context, complementing OpenTelemetry GenAI semantics.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]
- **Cross-Boundary Observability:** Establishing interaction mappings across agent-to-skill, skill-to-tool, agent-to-agent, and agent-to-MCP protocol boundaries, including integration with [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) and local subprocess CLI boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) Pipeline Observability:** Creating trace instrumentation spanning discovery, identity verification, decision metadata, and skill execution lifecycles in collaboration with [WG Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Shared Taxonomy:** Contributing foundational observability terms to the AAIF catalog, including Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Memory Access, Context Assembly, Retrieval, and Traceability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Cross-WG and External Liaisons:** Tracking engagement with OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, W3C Trace Context, OWASP AOS, and AAIF internal working groups.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18]

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group confirmed the technical scope of the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) and approved seven taxonomy definitions at the cross-WG review.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] Additionally, the working group folded the Multi-Agentic Observability Orchestration & Coordination focus group into the primary WG plenum to streamline participation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

mutations.rationale: Update the specification concept with confirmed scope details from August 2026, clarifying its relationship with OpenTelemetry GenAI and outlining the reference validation strategy.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry standard defining portable context propagation, causal execution tracing, and decision-to-outcome correlation for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and trace correlation specification that standardizes how execution context and causal relationships are preserved across agents, SDKs, mediation gateways, and telemetry backends.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b] Developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model uses portable telemetry context to correlate plans, decisions, and outcomes without requiring the transmission of raw chain-of-thought data.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model is designed to support and extend upstream telemetry specifications—specifically OpenTelemetry GenAI—rather than replace them:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Portable Telemetry Context:** Maintains end-to-end execution context across distributed agent runs, tool invocations, and subagent delegations without tying instrumentation to a single vendor's telemetry backend.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Causal Linking:** Connects high-level planning, intermediate decisions, and execution side effects while preserving user and organizational privacy by avoiding mandatory raw thought capture.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Canonical Identifiers & Long-Running Tasks:** Standardizes identifier propagation across multi-agent handoffs, conversational turn lifecycles, and asynchronous agent tasks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]
- **Validation & Conformance Plan:** Implemented via a reference library, synthetic agent workload examples, and conformance test suites designed to identify concrete gaps warranting upstream contributions to OpenTelemetry GenAI.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, WG Observability & Traceability finalized the trace model recommendation planning and confirmed its initial scope, prioritizing reference library construction and cross-boundary validation across September 2026.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]

proposed_concept.title: Activity
proposed_concept.description: A single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion within an agent workflow.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
An activity is a single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7] Within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) vocabulary, an activity represents the fundamental atomic unit of agent execution, serving as the building block from which larger agentic workflows are composed.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

# Architecture / Specification
In the AAIF workflow taxonomy, activity was explicitly selected over alternative terms such as "step" or "workflow step" to prevent circular semantic definitions:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **Decoupled Definition:** The term is defined independently without circular references to a containing workflow structure.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **Compositional Hierarchy:** A workflow is subsequently modeled as an orchestration or composition of one or more activities.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]
- **Scope Boundaries:** Gate, check, and evaluation semantics are explicitly scoped out of the activity primitive, remaining under the custody of security, observability, and accuracy working groups.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

# Lifecycle History
Adopted as part of the Phase One Core Terms draft by WG Workflows & Process Integration and formally voted through at the August 2026 plenary meeting, making it part of the first official deliverable shipped across the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining threat models, defensive architecture patterns, review checklists, and security best practices for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing threat models, privacy guidelines, defensive design patterns, and cross-cutting review checklists for agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. The working group is co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables across five primary workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]:

- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating industry frameworks including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF, with active extensions examining STRIDE and PASTA alignment, Model Context Protocol (MCP) surfaces, and Human-in-the-Loop/User-Interface (HUA) considerations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. See [threat modeling gap analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing defensive guidance across secrets management, tool invocation, and execution guardrails [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Identity and authorization boundaries interface directly with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. See [best practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, curating reusable, implementation-neutral design patterns and contribution templates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. See [design patterns catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md).
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing operational intake frameworks and security/privacy review checklists across foundation working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. See [review checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Alignment**: Coordinated via delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman, reviewing candidate terms alongside the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group transitioned past meeting recordings to be public by default [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22]. The group also submitted a request to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) seeking formal clarification on how incoming protocol donations (such as A2A) demarcate security work boundaries across working groups and projects like [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows & Process Integration Working Group (WG Workflows & Process Integration) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing reusable agentic workflow models, execution primitives, and reference architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The working group is co-chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its deliverables across three coordinated workstreams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]:

- **Reference Architectures**: Led by Mario and Zayne, developing architectural archetypes, structural design principles, and a specification-driven design flow that transforms machine-readable YAML specs into documentation and execution diagrams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The workstream established seven execution profiles ranging from 1 (fully deterministic) to 7 (fully agentic), operating under a proposed "least agentic default" architectural principle [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Led by Kevin Ng (Telus) and Jodee Varney (Cisco) with contributor Rocky Zhang (SAP), cataloging 89 production use cases categorized against structural primitives—including trigger types, human-in-the-loop patterns, agent count, coordination models, and workflow patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The workstream converged on a shortlist of under 10 reusable patterns, including the [bounded convergence loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Led by Gala, coordinating universal workflow terms and primitive definitions in direct collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to prevent cross-group terminology drift [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, the working group validated its specification-driven design pipeline against invoice processing and autonomous maintenance use cases across both default and elevated autonomy profiles [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. Workstream syncs were established bi-weekly alongside the regular plenary to finalize foundation PRs and reconcile primitive vocabularies prior to formal membership votes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Working group deliverable evaluating OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF against agentic architectures, STRIDE, PASTA, and MCP boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a research and framework evaluation deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, the deliverable benchmarks existing cybersecurity and AI threat modeling frameworks against agent-native vulnerability vectors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Architecture / Specification
The gap analysis evaluates several industry methodologies and frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]:

- **Baseline Threat Models**: Assesses OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and Agentic Systems, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) to identify gaps specific to autonomous execution, multi-agent swarms, and asynchronous tool delegation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Methodology Alignments**: Investigates how traditional threat modeling methodologies, specifically STRIDE and PASTA (Process for Attack Simulation and Threat Analysis), adapt to multi-turn agentic environments and dynamic tool invocation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Protocol and Interface Surfaces**: Incorporates boundary analyses covering Model Context Protocol (MCP) server connections, UI and Human-User/Agent (HUA) interaction channels, and agent-to-agent communication links [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Lifecycle History
Initiated as a core objective of the Security and Privacy Working Group, PR #8 reached active review in August 2026, incorporating review feedback from community members and Google contributors regarding protocol and interface risks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Catalog of reusable, vendor-neutral security and privacy design patterns for autonomous agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is an architectural resource curated by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, the catalog establishes implementation-independent design patterns addressing security, privacy, and safety boundaries across agent execution lifecycles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog defines common structural patterns to mitigate agent-specific risks, including prompt injection, unauthorized tool execution, memory corruption, and data exfiltration [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Patterns follow a standardized submission template outlining:

- **Context and Problem**: Specific runtime constraints, threat models, and operational hazards encountered in agent deployments.
- **Pattern Solution**: Architectural layout, trust boundaries, policy checkpoints, and isolation mechanisms mitigating the identified hazard.
- **Related Patterns**: Cross-references to runtime guardrails such as the [attested isolated runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and [inherited security floor](../patterns/inherited-security-floor.md).

# Lifecycle History
An initial catalog draft and pattern contribution template were completed in August 2026, preparing for intake and review as a pull request in the official AAIF repository [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist
proposed_concept.description: Operational review checklist and intake framework guiding early identification of security and privacy considerations across AAIF deliverables.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist is an operational intake framework maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, the checklist establishes structured criteria to ensure early identification and remediation of security and privacy concerns across AAIF technical deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Architecture / Specification
The framework provides an overlap analysis checklist designed to evaluate cross-cutting specifications and reference architectures across working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Key review criteria include:

- **Surface Exposure**: Identification of external protocol boundaries, tool calling capabilities, and network communication channels.
- **Identity and Delegation**: Verification that agent authorization, credential scoping, and user delegation align with standards defined by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Auditability and Evidence**: Assessment of event logging and attestation records compatible with [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) telemetry models.

# Lifecycle History
The review checklist workstream convened its initial cross-group syncs in August 2026 with four AAIF working group leads to build the overlap matrix and clarify deliverable scopes across repository workspaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Architectural catalog defining vendor-neutral, reusable design patterns addressing recurring security and privacy challenges in agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is a working deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) defining vendor-neutral, reusable architectural mechanisms for recurring security and privacy challenges in autonomous agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]. It provides implementation-independent patterns capturing the problem context, architectural mechanism, and associated trade-offs across diverse platforms, deployment models, and execution runtimes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

The catalog forms the architectural foundation for the complementary [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8]. While the catalog specifies reusable structural mechanisms, the best practices guide provides implementation and operational guidance for realizing them[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog establishes eight architectural pattern domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8]:
- Runtime security and governance
- Agent control and containment
- Secure tool invocation
- Agent memory protection and lifecycle management
- Privacy-preserving execution
- Secure multi-agent collaboration
- Security monitoring and intervention
- Auditability and recovery

The catalog assumes foundational identity, authentication, and credential management are established by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and treats those capabilities as inputs to security policy and runtime enforcement[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

Individual draft patterns published under the catalog include:
- [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md): Binds approval records to the action executed and logs execution impact[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50].
- [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md): Enforces attested, isolated execution environments for agent workloads[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50].
- [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md): Establishes independent control plane mechanisms to halt execution and trigger containment and recovery[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream is led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase), with contributions from IBM, TELUS, Global Payments, Huawei, Bluerock, Ericsson, and independent contributors[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]. Draft 0.1 was established as a working draft deliverable within the Security and Privacy Working Group repository[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing security and privacy as shared disciplines across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]. Appointed by Platinum and Gold members, the group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) for the term running from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56].

The working group convenes biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT, with additional alternate-week APAC trial sessions scheduled to support contributors across Asia-Pacific time zones[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables across five primary workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]:
- **Security Best Practices Guide**: Living practitioner guidance covering secure tool calling, prompt injection mitigations, secrets handling, and containment ([Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural patterns addressing recurring security and privacy challenges ([Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Threat Modeling**: Agentic AI threat modeling gap analyses and evaluation frameworks against existing industry standards ([Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Operational review criteria aligning security assessments across peer working groups ([Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape**: Domain vocabulary harmonization in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Lifecycle History
The group operates under repository governance guidelines mandating that pull requests merged into the published `deliverables/` folder cannot be self-merged by their authors, while workstream leads retain delegated operational control over their respective active drafting directories[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]. Reporting adheres to foundation operational standards, providing monthly status reports to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral telemetry models, execution trace specifications, and observability boundaries across autonomous agent runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59]. The group coordinates cross-cutting instrumentation across protocol layers, tool invocations, and agent-to-agent interactions.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group produces specifications and architectural analyses, including trace correlation models, context propagation protocols, and reference architectures evaluating runtime tracing frameworks across userspace, kernel, and hardware instrumentation.

# Lifecycle History
To satisfy [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) reporting guidelines and track monthly repository completion metrics, the working group maintains an automated GitHub Actions workflow (`monthly-metrics.yml`)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9373ed8bd5e2-54fdeb4c][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59]. The scheduled workflow counts monthly issue and pull request activity, measuring open and closed throughput as well as resolution timings to generate standardized monthly report issues labeled for committee review[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9373ed8bd5e2-54fdeb4c][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, defensive architecture patterns, builder best practices, and cross-working-group security review checklists for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body chartered to define threat models, defensive architecture patterns, implementation best practices, and cross-cutting security evaluation checklists for autonomous agent systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] Led by chair Alex Frazer, the group focuses on agent-specific risks including tool invocation integrity, memory and context poisoning, excessive agency, and multi-agent interaction failures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical output across five foundational deliverables, coordinating with neighboring AAIF working groups for domain-specific handoffs:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]

- **D1: Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions:** Shared vocabulary for agentic-AI-specific threats and security boundaries. Originally developed within the working group, D1 was transitioned in June 2026 to the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157]
- **D2: Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Comprehensive evaluation of existing AI threat frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF) determining coverage across eight agentic threat categories, led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Alon Mazor.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308] See [../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
- **D3: Design Patterns Catalog:** Architectural security and containment patterns addressing identified agentic voids, including isolated runtimes and kill switches, led by Sagar.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308] See [../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md).
- **D4: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Practical operational guidance for builders covering secrets management, secure Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool invocation, guardrails, evaluations, and post-incident forensics, led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] See [../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **D5: Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Operational review framework and intake gates guiding security reviews across AAIF specifications, led by Govindaraj Palanisamy.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308] See [../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).

Identity, delegation chains, and decentralized attestation architectures are explicitly scoped outside this working group and handed off to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](./identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]

# Lifecycle History

The working group commenced orientation in February 2026, approved its charter in May 2026, and opened its public GitHub repositories in June 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] In September 2026, the group instituted alternate-week APAC meetings to accommodate global participation, established policy requiring peer maintainer review for deliverable pull requests, and prepared the merge of the Best Practices Guide (PR #9).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]

# References

- Deliverables Index: [aaif/wg-security-and-privacy deliverables](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/deliverables/README.md)
- Threat Modeling Workstream: [aaif/wg-security-and-privacy threat-modeling](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/workstreams/threat-modeling/README.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, Model Context Protocol security, skill verification, guardrails, eval frameworks, and post-incident forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is an authoritative deliverable of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) (Deliverable 4) providing operational, implementable security controls for engineers deploying agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] Authored by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, the guide addresses real-world failure patterns through architectural controls across five core operational areas: secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]

Agent identity primitives, SPIFFE/SVID workload attestation, RFC 8693 delegation chains, and UCAN capability token architectures are explicitly out of scope, having been transferred to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and surfaced via the [Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist](./cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]

# Architecture / Specification

The guide outlines failure patterns, mitigation architectures, and concrete control requirements across core agent interaction boundaries:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]

- **Secrets Management:** Mandates transitioning from static, long-lived API keys in environment variables (which expose systems to deserialization leaks like CVE-2025-68664) to ephemeral attestation credentials.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] Controls prioritize platform-native workload identities (AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity), dynamic request-scoped secrets engines (HashiCorp Vault), network-layer proxy credential injection for legacy systems, and hardware-protected confidential computing enclaves (Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) for high-sensitivity multi-tenant environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP) Security:** Mitigates tool poisoning (including Unicode tag character injection U+E0000–U+E007F), tool definition rug pulls, cross-server shadowing, and conversation hijacking.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] Enforces mandatory pre-connection server vetting (source repository checks, ≥90-day activity verification, public tracker lookups, and static scanning via Cisco MCP Scanner), strict OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and RFC 8707 audience binding for HTTP transports, sandbox isolation for stdio transports, tool definition hash verification at session start, and traffic consolidation through mediation proxies like [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Supply Chain and Skill Verification:** Establishes a multi-tier verification process for skills, MCP packages, and agent cards.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] Tier 1 requires automated static pattern matching and dataflow scanning (Cisco Skill Scanner or Snyk Agent Scan) blocking on high-severity findings; Tier 2 requires manual audit of `allowed-tools` declarations and inspection for undeclared external domain calls or obscured execution payloads (`eval()`, Base64 strings).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Guardrails, Evals, and Forensics:** Defines perimeter network controls, sandboxed code execution, output sanitization, behavioral evaluations, and structured payload capture for post-incident investigation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]

# Lifecycle History

The guide was drafted within the Best Practices workstream and structured around initial WG feedback and industry baselines.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] In September 2026, working group leads froze Draft v0.1 for merge via pull request #9, converting remaining broader feedback into tracking issues and initiating work to generate static analysis rules from the guide's feature matrix.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]

# References

- Deliverable Document: [DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md)
- Feature Matrix: [security-best-practices-feature-matrix.md](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/workstreams/best-practices/security-best-practices-feature-matrix.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Working group deliverable evaluating OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF against eight agentic threat areas to guide new security framework development.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design is an authoritative technical report (Deliverable 2) produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308] Led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Alon Mazor (Ocean Security), the report evaluates whether existing AI security frameworks—specifically OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF—adequately cover threats unique to agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]

The report concludes that while existing frameworks jointly provide adequate threat classification and adversarial technique coding, critical architectural and operational voids persist across five technical areas, requiring dedicated AAIF guidance rather than redundant baseline taxonomy work.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]

# Architecture / Specification

The gap analysis combines three complementary framework perspectives to evaluate coverage across the system lifecycle:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]

- **OWASP (Developer Controls):** Combines the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications with the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (ASI01–ASI10) to assess developer-facing risk categories.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]
- **MITRE ATLAS (SOC Detection):** Employs the ATLAS matrix (v4.6.0 through v5.4.0) to evaluate security operations center detection rules and adversary attack techniques (AML.T codes).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]
- **CSA MAESTRO (Architectural Hardening):** Evaluates threat placement across MAESTRO's seven-layer reference stack (L1 Foundation Models through L7 Agent Ecosystem, with L6 Security and Compliance as a cross-cutting vertical).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]
- **Supplementary Governance:** References NIST AI RMF 1.0, NIST IR 8596 Cyber AI Profile, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, and the CSA AI Controls Matrix v1.0 for risk management framing.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]

The analysis evaluates eight distinct agentic threat categories:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]
1. Memory and context poisoning
2. Multi-agent persuasion and collusion
3. Agent sabotage, derailment, and rogue agent behavior
4. Tool invocation risks and protocol-level vulnerabilities
5. Excessive agency and blast radius containment
6. Delegated authorization boundaries (jurisdiction formally designated to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md))
7. Supply chain integrity (prompts, tool manifests, and models)
8. Commerce and payment-agent risks

# Lifecycle History

The deliverable mandate was established during initial working group sessions in spring 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] Workstream leads published draft revisions during July and August 2026, culminating in Draft v0.1 submitted for formal working group review in late September 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308] Its findings directly inform the scope of the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](./security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md) and the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]

# References

- Report Source: [DRAFT-agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)
- Threat Modeling Workstream: [aaif/wg-security-and-privacy workstreams/threat-modeling](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/22c3f9a2cdac4fcf092502fa06154b08b4df09b8/workstreams/threat-modeling/README.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical, actionable engineering guidance for builders designing and deploying agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066] Whereas architectural catalogs define reusable implementation mechanics, this guide addresses operational decision-making by prescribing recommended controls, external frameworks, and standard tooling for key risk domains.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]

# Architecture / Specification
The guide focuses on core architectural and operational security domains:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]

- **Secrets Management**: Safeguarding credentials, tokens, and API keys across multi-step execution flows and tool invocations.
- **Secure Tool Invocation**: Defenses against prompt injection, unauthorized capability invocation, and parameter tampering at protocol boundaries.
- **Guardrails**: Model-level and harness-level constraint mechanisms that enforce runtime safety and authorization rules.
- **Evaluation Frameworks**: Structured testing pipelines to assess agent resilience against behavioral vulnerabilities and adversarial inputs.
- **Post-Incident Forensics**: Auditing execution trails, preserving decision provenance, and conducting root-cause telemetry investigations.
- **External Framework References**: Curated alignments with established industry standards such as OWASP, MITRE, and NIST rather than re-deriving domain controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]

# Lifecycle History
The guide is developed as a primary deliverable of the Security and Privacy Working Group (see [working-groups/security-and-privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066] Following the initial merge of the draft deliverable, it operates as a living document with Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson) serving as workstream leads and mandatory reviewers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry standard defining portable context propagation, causal execution tracing, and decision-to-tool linkage across heterogeneous agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a standardized telemetry framework that captures causal execution paths, reasoning steps, and tool interactions within agentic AI runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60] It establishes vendor-neutral conventions for propagating behavioral context across model invocations, subagent delegations, and external service calls.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]

# Architecture / Specification
The standard defines trace schemas and context-propagation semantics designed to align with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60] Implementation work incorporates an evidence-first execution plan organized into four sequential phases:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]

1. **Agree**: Establish the foundational scope, dimension boundaries, and initial modeling agreements.
2. **Evidence**: Capture empirical telemetry emissions from production agent implementations to identify real-world inconsistencies in OpenTelemetry support across major coding agents and SDKs.
3. **Interpret**: Maintain a centralized register of observed telemetry gaps and evaluate schema discrepancies across causal dimensions.
4. **Contribute**: Formalize standardized upstream proposals to OpenTelemetry semantic convention working groups.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]

[resources/goose](../resources/goose.md) serves as the primary reference implementation for capturing baseline emissions and validating tracing conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]

# Lifecycle History
Governed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group (see [working-groups/observability-and-traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)), the trace model transitioned from nine parallel workstreams toward a phased empirical roadmap in late 2026 to resolve integration variance observed across active agent frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]

proposed_concept.title: aaif-create-chapter
proposed_concept.description: Operational provisioning and rebranding skill that creates city chapters, formats presentation assets, and computes accurate slide map projections.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-create-chapter` skill automates the provisioning, document cloning, and visual asset rebranding required when launching a new AAIF city chapter.[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49] Operating on Google Drive and local template decks, it enforces consistent asset naming, template inheritance, and geographical map marker placement.[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]

# Architecture / Specification
The core engine script `create_chapter.py` manages document transformation through specific procedural subsystems:[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]

- **Paragraph-Level Rebranding**: Transforms text at the paragraph level by concatenating text runs before mutation and writing back into the primary run, mitigating OOXML run-splitting bugs across presentation shapes.[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]
- **Gall Stereographic Projection**: Recomputes coordinates for the slide-5 world map marker using a Gall Stereographic projection where `lon2x` is linear in longitude and `lat2y` is linear in `(1 + √2/2)·tan(lat/2)`, calibrated against Natural Earth coastline data.[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]
- **Drive Layer Synchronization**: Coordinates folder generation and permission cloning using Google Workspace CLI integrations (`gws files.copy`, `create`, `get`, `update`).[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]
- **Verification Test Harness**: Verifies projection anchors, label offsets, monotonicity, and canvas bounds via `test_create_chapter.py` prior to live production execution.[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]

# Lifecycle History
Maintained under the `community-events` repository as part of the community operations automation suite (see [skills/community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)).[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]

proposed_concept.description: Configuration-driven Slack inspection skill auditing chapter channels, organizer rooms, and membership discrepancies against estate rosters.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-audit-slack` skill provides automated compliance auditing across the AAIF Slack estate, verifying that chapter channels, organizer discussion spaces, and user privileges correspond to accepted intake records.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb] It reconciles Slack conversation state with community database rosters to identify access leaks and unmapped communications.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]

# Architecture / Specification
The audit suite relies on specialized inspection engines, notably the organizer audit engine (`audit_organizers.py`), which produces both HTML and JSON audit outputs:[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]

- **Roster and Channel Mapping**: Reconciles the authoritative channel map on the Chapters List (`Chapters & Teams`) with accepted organizer records in Intake Ops and live Slack workspace data (`conversations.list`, `conversations.members`, `users.lookupByEmail`).[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]
- **Pre-Provisioning State Handling**: Supports the `--planned-ok` flag to downgrade uncreated or held-private rooms to planned status during pre-provisioning, preventing execution aborts while ensuring chapters without public channels are accurately noted.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]
- **Identity Joins**: Matches organizers to Slack accounts strictly via email, treating missing accounts as an upper bound on configuration drift.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]
- **High-Severity Exposure Alerts**: Flags publicly readable `-organizers` channels as critical security findings (`public!`), preventing premature exposure of budgeting, venue logistics, and organizer deliberations.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]

# Lifecycle History
Operated within the `community-events` tooling estate alongside synchronization skills like [skills/aaif-sync](../skills/aaif-sync.md).[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability and Authorization Boundaries
proposed_concept.description: Standardized manifest architecture, directory resolution rules, capability abstractions, and authorization boundaries ensuring agent plugins run portably across heterogeneous runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Plugin Portability and Authorization Boundaries guideline specifies conventions for packaging modular [Agent Plugins](../standards/agent-plugins.md) and [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) so they execute reliably across heterogeneous host environments—such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor—without relying on client-specific path semantics or unvalidated write permissions[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. It enforces portable directory resolution, capability-driven instruction design, namespaced metadata retention, and strict runtime authorization gates across external mutations[^evt-community-events-pr-54].

# Architecture / Specification

### Manifest Structure
Portable plugins declare a canonical root `plugin.json` conformant with the Agent Plugins specification[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. When targeting clients with proprietary configuration schemas (such as Claude Code), client manifests (e.g., `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) are maintained in tandem, but the root manifest remains canonical for identity, description, and version metadata[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Overlays (such as `.codex-plugin` or `.cursor-plugin`) are omitted unless client-specific configuration is strictly required[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

### Directory Resolution and Capability Abstraction
All resource references inside a `SKILL.md` or its companion files must be relative to the directory containing that `SKILL.md`[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Portable skills replace platform-specific environment variables (such as `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`) with the `<skill-root>` placeholder, which the agent harness resolves at runtime from the skill's loaded location rather than passing it literally to a shell[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69][^evt-community-events-pr-54].

Skills define tool dependencies using vendor-neutral capability descriptions rather than vendor-specific tool names[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- **Read bundled files**: Access skill-packaged references or templates; missing resources halt execution[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Run Python and subprocesses**: Execute deterministic helper scripts rather than generating ad hoc mutating shell code[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Read web pages**: Fetch external public state or fallback to manual prompts[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Show local files**: Output local paths and instructions for user inspection[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Request user approval**: Pause workflow execution before crossing write boundaries[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

### Frontmatter and Metadata Compatibility
The portable Agent Skills schema disallows non-standard autocomplete keys in top-level frontmatter; client-specific features (such as `argument-hint`) must be nested under namespaced `metadata` so catalog parsers can extract them without triggering schema validation failures on standard runtimes[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69][^evt-community-events-pr-54].

### Authorization Boundaries and Safety Invariants
Invoking or loading an agent skill does not grant authorization to execute mutations[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Implementations follow the [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) pattern:
- **Plan-by-default**: Default runs are strictly read-only and print a diff or plan[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Explicit mutation flags**: Destructive actions require deliberate command-line flags (`--write`, `--apply`, `--create`)[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Attestation flags**: Flags certifying approval (`--i-have-approval`) must reflect actual human sign-off and must never be injected by an agent autonomously[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Credential containment**: Secrets must never be supplied via command-line arguments or prompts; credentials reside exclusively in environment variables, `.env` files, or OS keychains[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69][^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03**: Established through PR #54 in `aaif/community-events`, migrating 23 operational skills from Claude-specific path conventions to the unified Agent Plugins v1 and Agent Skills portable packaging specification[^evt-community-events-pr-54].

proposed_concept.title: aaif-create-chapter
proposed_concept.description: Operational provisioning, renaming, and backfill skill managing chapter folders, presentation slide decks, and map coordinates under strict plan-first mutation controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` skill handles the lifecycle provisioning, in-place renaming, and presentation deck backfilling for AAIF city chapters[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]. Operating under the [Agent Plugin Portability guidelines](../../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md), the skill implements plan-by-default execution, pre-flight string diff reviews, automated zip-level OOXML surgery, and isolated rollback backups prior to modifying Google Drive assets[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

# Architecture / Specification

### Four-Surface Chapter Renaming (`rename_chapter.py`)
Renaming an existing chapter is an atomic transformation covering four distinct surfaces to avoid state desynchronization[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]:
1. **Drive folder naming**: Modifies the root chapter directory name[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
2. **File and subfolder naming**: Updates child files and directories (e.g., CRM workbooks, image assets)[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
3. **OOXML text streams**: Rewrites internal XML strings across `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` document bundles[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
4. **Document metadata**: Updates internal `docProps` metadata fields[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

Safety invariants during renaming include:
- **Slug decoupling**: Public event platform slugs (e.g., Luma) are not altered unless explicitly requested via `--slug-from` and `--slug-to`, preventing broken external links[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
- **Relationship integrity**: Relationship files (`.rels`) receive slug substitutions only; city name substitutions are excluded to prevent dangling XML targets and corrupted zip archives[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
- **Staged backups**: Original files are mirrored into `backups/rename-<UTC>/` before mutations upload to Drive[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
- **Post-write verification**: The runner re-fetches and verifies remote Drive contents, exiting non-zero if residual old-name references remain[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

### Estate Backfill Operations
Maintenance across existing chapter presentation decks is managed via targeted backfill scripts implementing plan-first checks[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62]:
- **Map Marker Placement (`backfill_map_dots.py`)**: Recalculates chapter marker placement using Gall Stereographic map projection coordinates joined from the canonical `Generated Geolocation` sheet records[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62]. Modifies slides only when drift exceeds `--tolerance` (default 1 px), ensuring idempotent runs[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].
- **Template Backfills**: Updates template host footers (`backfill_host_footer.py`) and project rosters (`backfill_projects.py`) across the estate, supporting dry-run plan outputs and local offline XML testing[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03**: Updated with documented four-surface renaming protocols and Gall Stereographic projection backfill tooling in the `aaif/community-events` repository[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
