proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry standard defining portable context propagation, causal execution tracing, and decision-to-effect verification for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model defines a vendor-neutral observability specification for tracing non-deterministic AI agent reasoning, tool invocations, state mutations, and resulting side effects across distributed boundaries. The specification extends OpenTelemetry semantic conventions to represent prompt lineage, tool call causality, and cryptographic receipts.

Recent standard development introduces a conformance test harness and reference verification suite to ensure portable trace decoding across heterogeneous agent engines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

# Architecture / Specification

### Conformance Test Kit

The trace model test kit establishes automated continuous integration fixtures to validate trace parsers and compliance engines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57]:

- **OTLP/JSON Reference Vectors**: Standardized fixtures encoding canonical agent spans, nested iterations, and action dispatch logs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Receipt and Evidence Evaluation**: Dedicated test cases validating duplicate receipts, missing receipts, and cryptographic receipt signature mutations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Multi-Tenant Integrity**: Fixtures asserting detection when action identifiers (such as identifier reuse across different tenant boundaries) or altered ticket references are introduced [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Decoupled Effect Qualification**: Clear separation between synthetic signature validity and real-world effect correlation, preventing synthetic fixtures from authenticating unverified target side effects [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

# Lifecycle History

- PR #57 contributed six baseline OTLP/JSON test cases, a reference reader, and CI validation using pinned cryptographic dependencies to serve as the gating conformance check for the core trace model [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol alignments, buyer capacity verification, and dispute standards for autonomous commercial transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group standardizes protocols, capability maps, and transaction lifecycle models for autonomous and semi-autonomous commercial interactions. Its scope spans identity delegation, checkout flows, payment settlement interfaces, and dispute arbitration across agent-to-merchant and agent-to-agent transactions.

Workstreams include the comparative evaluation of emerging commerce specifications against legal frameworks governing principal capacity and statutory data retention [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].

# Architecture / Specification

### Capability Mapping and Protocol Evaluation

The working group benchmarks emerging commerce protocols against enterprise and regulatory requirements, prioritizing two missing protocol dimensions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8]:

1. **Buyer Legal Capacity and Age**: Commercial protocols currently lack standardized attributes asserting principal capacity or minor status. Because delegation from minors may be legally void or voidable, and age-restricted goods require legal verification of the [Principal](../taxonomy/principal.md) rather than the autonomous agent, protocol identity layers must explicitly support verifiable capacity attestations [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].
2. **Layered Record Retention Matrix**: Autonomous transactions distribute recordkeeping across new intermediary entities. The group is drafting a multi-layered retention model encompassing:
   - *AI Governance Layer*: Mandated six-month log retention for high-risk deployments under Article 19 and Article 26(6) of the EU AI Act [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].
   - *Personal Data Layer*: Data protection storage limitations defining statutory retention ceilings [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].
   - *Financial Compliance Layer*: Anti-money laundering and electronic funds transfer preservation periods (e.g., five years under the US Bank Secrecy Act and EU AMLD, and two years under Regulation E) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].

# Lifecycle History

- Issue #8 opened discussion on protocol capability scorecards, highlighting gaps in capacity verification and cross-jurisdictional transaction log retention duties [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-8].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Identity and Trust Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Draft foundational specification defining attestation models, accountability structures, revocability semantics, and authority-at-dispatch verification for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Identity and Trust Primitives specification defines foundational mechanisms for asserting, verifying, and scoping the identity and authority of autonomous AI agents. It addresses identity provenance across multiple principals, dynamic privilege delegation, and the cryptographic validation of agent authority at point-of-action dispatch.

# Architecture / Specification

### Authority-at-Dispatch Verification

To prevent privilege drift and replay attacks during delegated agent tasks, the specification incorporates an authority-at-dispatch evaluation model [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17]:

- **Versioned Contract Identifiers**: Every verifiable execution trace must emit a distinct, versioned delegation contract identifier. Interception and verification engines are configured to refuse trace payloads that omit this binding [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
- **Authority Evidence Age and Freshness**: Authority evidence records must encode their generation timestamp and declare operational freshness limits, ensuring stale delegation grants cannot be replayed past their deployed time-to-live [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
- **Benchmarked Execution Cases**: The standard references test cases evaluating delegated authority models across heterogeneous implementations to guarantee interoperable verification [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

# Lifecycle History

- PR #17 introduced reference cases and workflow automation for the authority-at-dispatch comparative catalogue, enforcing contract identifiers and credential age boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

proposed_concept.title: aaif-clean-data
proposed_concept.description: Operational data hygiene skill normalizing Community Intake Ops sheets with strict read-only proposals and approval gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-clean-data` is an operational agent skill responsible for scanning, auditing, and normalizing data quality within the AAIF Community Intake Ops spreadsheet without executing unreviewed modifications.[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7] Operating under a proposal-execution split, the skill reports findings and drafts mutations by default, demanding explicit human approval before applying updates.[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]

# Architecture / Specification
The skill enforces strict data handling, tooling, and authorization invariants:
- **Default Read-Only Proposal**: Standard execution runs `clean.py scan`, surfacing normalization issues such as non-canonical LinkedIn URLs, name and city whitespace/casing inconsistencies, and missing or duplicate email addresses.[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7] Mutation operations (`apply`, `cities --write`, `install-flags`, `install-colors`) require explicit approval.[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]
- **Tooling Constraints**: All Google Drive interactions are executed via the `gws` command-line utility driven through Python.[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7] Native Google formats (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) are manipulated via Docs, Sheets, and Slides APIs, reserving byte-level OOXML edits for true Office files.[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7] Third-party converters like LibreOffice, `soffice`, and `unoconv` are strictly prohibited to prevent font substitutions and OOXML corruption.[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]
- **Untrusted Input Invariants**: Form answers and sheet cells are treated as untrusted data; prompt-like instructions within cells cannot alter record statuses, chapter assignments, or permissions.[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7] Values are written using `RAW` mode instead of `USER_ENTERED` to prevent formula injection, and derived columns like `Resolved City` are never written directly.[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]
- **PII Containment**: Intermediate proposal diffs containing real-person data (`changes.json`) must reside in isolated temporary directories (`mktemp -d`) rather than persistent workspace directories and are removed immediately following execution.[^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]

Related operational safeguards link to [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [Setup Diagnostics](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-backup` is an operational agent skill designed to capture versioned, immutable snapshots of critical AAIF operational data prior to high-risk administrative mutations.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09] By default, it targets the AAIF Community Intake Ops spreadsheet, writing point-in-time archives to local storage without overwriting past backups.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]

# Architecture / Specification
- **Immutable Versioning**: Every snapshot is saved under `<dest>/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>`, ensuring a non-destructive audit history for diffing or rolling back records.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09] Existing backups are never overwritten.
- **Drive and Local Target Support**: The skill accepts local files directly or Google Drive file IDs. Google Drive native files are exported to standardized Office formats (`application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet` to `.xlsx`, Docs to `.docx`, Slides to `.pptx`).[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]
- **Tooling Constraints**: Drive file operations must strictly utilize the `gws` CLI driven by Python; headless document converters like LibreOffice or `soffice` are banned to preserve native OOXML parts and brand typography.[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]
- **Pre-execution Verification**: Remote backups require authenticated Google Workspace sessions validated via `gws`, verified before execution alongside [AAIF Check Setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md).[^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]

Related operational patterns include [Clean Data](../skills/aaif-clean-data.md) and [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-check-setup` is a read-only diagnostic skill that validates the host environment's readiness to execute the AAIF event operations toolkit.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77] It audits local Python runtimes, Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) authentication, spreadsheet permissions, Slack API credentials, Luma integration keys, and headless Chrome availability, delivering actionable remediation instructions tailored for non-technical users.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]

# Architecture / Specification
- **Read-Only Inspection**: The check reads metadata from the target Community Intake sheet, executes Slack `auth.test`, and queries Luma `calendars/get` without mutating remote states.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]
- **Secret Redaction**: Raw tokens, passwords, and private API keys are never printed or echoed to logs; output only indicates credential detection and validation status.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]
- **Graceful Degradation**: Writing and copywriting skills (such as announcement posts, invites, and recaps) operate from manual user input and remain functional even when operational API credentials fail validation.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]
- **Credential Recovery Procedures**: Remediates OAuth scope drift by prescribing specific scoped `gws` sign-in commands rather than interactive prompts, and resolves macOS keychain conflicts by guiding the cleanup of duplicate `gws-cli` entries.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]

Related skills include [Clean Data](../skills/aaif-clean-data.md), [Backup](../skills/aaif-backup.md), and [Slack Audit](../skills/aaif-audit-slack.md).

proposed_concept.description: Inspection skill auditing chapter channels, organizer rosters, and memberships across the AAIF Slack workspace with strict privacy controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-audit-slack` is an operational inspection skill that analyzes channel topologies, organizer assignments, topic channels, and membership health across the AAIF Slack community workspace.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d] It combines cached API pulls, incremental reconciliation, and automated Git privacy guards to generate a consolidated HTML report without risking member data exposure.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]

# Architecture / Specification
- **Caching and Reconciliation Engine**: API pulls are cached atomically in `.slack-audit-cache` with workspace origin tags and timestamp metadata.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d] Rather than executing blanket re-fetches, the engine reconciles incrementally by probing newly approved organizers and re-checking previously unmatched profiles.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]
- **Git Exposure Prevention**: Audit caches and reports contain sensitive member names, email addresses, and administrative privilege flags; they are created with `0600` file permissions inside `0700` directories.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d] Engines assert that output paths are safe from `git add -A` and abort execution immediately if paths could be accidentally tracked in public version control.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]
- **Composite Reporting (`summarize_audits.py`)**: Assembles `slack-full-audit.html` from four distinct audit engines (Chapters, Organizers, Topics, Members) concluded by a prioritized remediation focus page.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d] The report compiles only verifiable cached observations and re-reads live Google Sheets config for topic definitions.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]

Related skills include [Check Setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md) and [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`aaif-create-chapter` is an operational skill that provisions and standardizes local chapter assets across Google Drive, creating localized deck templates, CRM sheets, and branded artwork.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601] As part of ongoing estate maintenance, it coordinates with `restyle_design_system.py` to enforce the AAIF design system across chapter templates without corrupting user data or event-specific artifacts.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]

# Architecture / Specification
- **Strict Template Scope**: Design system sweeps only target known template files listed in `TEMPLATE_FILES` and chapter CRM workbooks (`<City> CRM.xlsx`); personalized event decks and dated organizer materials are explicitly bypassed to prevent accidental overwrites.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]
- **SpreadsheetML Style Isolation**: CRM styling updates target only `xl/styles.xml` and workbook theme XML using ARGB color specifications and SpreadsheetML element schemas.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601] Cell values located in `xl/worksheets/` and `xl/sharedStrings.xml` remain strictly untouched.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]
- **Non-Destructive Rollback Archives**: Before writing updates to Google Drive, the engine archives untouched files into `backups/restyle-<UTC>/`.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601] Pre-existing archive copies are immutable and never overwritten by subsequent passes, ensuring clean rollback states.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]
- **Accessibility and Asset Security**: Visual assets and slide backgrounds are evaluated against WCAG AA legibility standards.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601] Chapter agent artwork is compiled into private build directories prior to upload to prevent predictable `/tmp` directory hijack risks on shared systems.[^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]

Related guidelines and patterns include [Brand Guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md), [Clean Data](../skills/aaif-clean-data.md), and [Backup](../skills/aaif-backup.md).

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Standardized skill suite and portable Agent Plugin runtime managing AAIF chapter provisioning, estate synchronization, and asset rebranding.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations skill suite provides automated tooling and workflow orchestration for local AAIF chapter lifecycle management, event tracker provisioning, asset rebranding, and estate health verification [^evt-community-events-pr-60]. Packaged as a portable Agent Plugin [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c] adhering to the Agent Skills standard [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c], the suite enables operators to execute operational pipelines consistently across environments such as Goose, Claude Desktop, and headless CI/CD automation without manual environment reconfiguration [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

# Architecture / Specification

The toolkit separates read-only evaluation engines, asset transformers, and synchronization coordinators across specialized components:

- **Portability Layer:** Follows cross-client manifests defined in `plugin.json` alongside `.claude-plugin/` compatibility definitions [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c]. Scripts avoid assuming repository-relative roots or active git metadata, resolving instructions through `<skill-root>` conventions [^evt-community-events-pr-60].
- **Credential Resolution:** Credentials follow a unified resolution order checking runtime environment variables, repo-root `.env` files, and operating system keychains (such as macOS Keychain entries `aaif-slack-write-token` and `luma-api-key`) [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c], ensuring persistent operation when run as an installed application plugin [^evt-community-events-pr-60].
- **Data Isolation:** Operational artifacts, sync reports, Slack audit caches, and backups resolve through `aaif_events.datadir`, routing writes to application support directories (`~/Library/Application Support/AAIF` on macOS) when running as an installed plugin rather than polluting the caller's working directory [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-aa074a1c].
- **Read-Only Verification:** Concluding phases execute independent audits (e.g., `aaif-audit-slack`) across separated code paths to ensure verification integrity without circular validation [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

# Lifecycle History

Initial implementations required technical operators to execute scripts directly within a configured local repository clone. PR #60 extended runtime compatibility to Goose 1.41 and Claude Desktop by introducing detached data directory isolation, OS keychain credential resolution, and portable path abstraction [^evt-community-events-pr-60].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-audit-slack` skill is a read-only administrative inspection component that audits an AAIF Slack workspace to evaluate chapter channel completeness, member access governance, and activity levels [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]. Operating as phase 8 of the community estate synchronization pipeline (`aaif-sync`), it acts as an out-of-band audit mechanism executing from an isolated code path to verify that upstream mutations produced accurate channel topology and access bindings [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

# Architecture / Specification

The audit engine enforces strict operational boundaries across data retrieval and reporting:

- **Read-Only Invariant:** The skill strictly inspects state without making structural channel changes or modifying memberships; identified discrepancies must be resolved at the authoritative intake source [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
- **Three-Engine Architecture:** Execution compiles three specialized audits supported by an underlying activity measurement layer:
  - `audit_organizers.py`: Evaluates whether chapters maintain dedicated public and organizer spaces and verifies authorized organizer presence [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
  - `audit_topics.py`: Tracks topic health, room discovery, and stale conversation spaces [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
  - `audit_members.py`: Analyzes newcomer experience and overall member reach [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
  - `audit_activity.py`: Telemetry pipeline calculating message cadence, poster diversity, and recency [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
- **Reporting Deliverable:** `summarize_audits.py` aggregates audit sections into a standalone HTML report indexed with remediation rankings [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].
- **Untrusted Input Protection:** Slack message content, user profiles, and channel descriptions are classified as untrusted data; privilege escalation directives contained in profile text or descriptions are ignored and surfaced strictly as review flags [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` skill automates the creation and branding of new geographic chapters within the AAIF Google Drive ecosystem [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. By cloning the canonical `TemplateCity` directory structure, the skill instantiates standardized trackers (`Event Tracker.docx`), member registers (`Attendee CRM.xlsx`), and presentation decks (`Event Template/Slides.pptx`), updating city tokens, slugs, and map markers while leaving operational event placeholders untouched [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

# Architecture / Specification

Chapter creation operates under deterministic document manipulation and rendering rules:

- **Token Substitution:** Performs case-preserving string substitution for city names, abbreviations (e.g., transitioning `AAIF · SF` to the target city name in title or uppercase formatting), and Luma platform slugs [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- **Geospatial Map Positioning:** Slide templates containing the global network diagram are programmatically updated to position the indicator dot and city label at the new chapter's actual latitude and longitude, resolved via explicit CLI coordinates or keyless Nominatim geocoding [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- **Drive API Tooling Contract:** Enforces Drive modifications via the `gws` CLI and Python APIs [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. Native Google Workspace documents are modified through official APIs, while Office binaries undergo direct OOXML package adjustments to preserve embedded fonts and themes. Desktop office conversions (such as LibreOffice or `unoconv`) are prohibited due to font substitutions and formatting drift [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Ecosystem Landscape is an open taxonomy and project catalog tracking frameworks, runtime systems, protocols, guardrails, and developer tooling across the agentic technology domain [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30]. Managed under the Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group, the landscape models industry initiatives according to standard data schemas, objective descriptive criteria, and non-promotional neutral criteria [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification

Entries in `landscape/landscape.yml` are categorized across primary domains and subcategories governed by strict validation rules:

- **Category Evolution:** Proposals have introduced dedicated subcategories to accommodate emerging architectural patterns [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30]:
  - *Gateways & Control Planes:* Established under Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration to classify traffic-mediating and routing infrastructure like [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md), distinguishing mediation layers from agentic orchestration frameworks and guardrails [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].
  - *Conventions & File Formats:* Structured under Protocols & Discovery Registries to house declarative repository guidelines such as `AGENTS.md`, distinguishing file conventions from network wire protocols like [A2A](../taxonomy/agent-to-agent.md) and [MCP](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-30].
- **Metadata Hygiene:** Projects undergo active URI and repository status verification to ensure canonical domain mappings (e.g., tracking repository migrations across A2A, OpenHands, and CrewAI) and maintain non-redirecting documentation endpoints [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-31].

proposed_concept.title: Mandate
proposed_concept.description: Agentic Commerce taxonomy term defining an explicit authorization and parameter boundary granted by a principal permitting an agent to initiate transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
A **mandate** in the Agentic Commerce taxonomy is an explicit authorization granted by a [principal](../taxonomy/principal.md) that establishes the valid constraints, financial thresholds, and operational scope under which an agent may initiate or mediate commercial transactions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-77].

# Architecture / Specification
Within agentic commerce workflows, mandates define the legal and runtime permissions for transaction execution [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-77]:
- **Pre-authorized Execution**: Serves as the policy boundary allowing [agent-initiated transactions](../taxonomy/agent-initiated-transaction.md) and [delegated payments](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md) to proceed autonomously without per-action synchronous approval, provided operational parameters remain within declared constraints [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-77].
- **Constraint Boundaries**: Encapsulates specific financial ceilings, frequency limits, counterparty conditions, and validity timeframes established during [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md) or onboarding.
- **Lifecycle and Revocation**: Subject to revocation, renewal, and attestation by the authorizing principal or governing institution under [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) frameworks.

The reporting skill standardizes monthly operational reporting across multiple dimensions [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-1]:

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering pre-execution interception hooks, gateway checkpoints, sandbox boundaries, and policy decision points.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide, maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), establishes operational security and defensive implementation baselines for engineering teams deploying autonomous AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]. The guidance establishes patterns for runtime interception, gateway-level traffic mediation, host-environment sandboxing, and policy-driven tool authorization [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41].

# Architecture / Specification

## Interception and Network Boundaries

Defensive runtime mediation operates across two coordinated control surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]:

- **Runtime Hooks**: In-process interception points across the agent lifecycle where the execution harness halts pending operations and dispatches the prospective action, tool identity, and execution context to policy evaluation code before dispatch [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].
- **Gateway Checkpoints**: Network-path controls, exemplified by the AAIF [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) project, that serve as unified endpoints for remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, OAuth negotiation, per-tool authorization rules, and action event payload logging [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]. Runtime hooks and network gateways function cooperatively to ensure both call context and network transport are validated [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].

## Sandboxing and Confinement Scope

Execution sandboxing constrains runtime attack surfaces but requires precise architectural isolation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41]:

- **Containment Scope**: Standard sandbox modes reduce unverified artifact access from the full user account to the immediate working directory, changing the environment risk profile from contained to narrowed [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41].
- **Enforcement Requirements**: Sandboxing cannot prevent egress or host compromise without kernel-enforced mechanisms, specifically filesystem isolation, dedicated namespaces, and strict syscall filtering [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41].
- **Bypass Risks**: Absent kernel enforcement, unmonitored runtime environments (such as embedded HTTP clients) can bypass proxy allowlists, and compromised sandbox workloads can stage malicious files intended for execution by trusted host-side utilities outside the sandbox [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41]. Artifact and tool definition verification must remain active even when sandbox mode is engaged [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41].

## Policy Decision Point (PDP) Authorization System

Tool execution authorization is structured around a policy decision point linked directly to execution hooks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]:

- **Contextual Invocations**: Because tool risk varies with invocation arguments, the decision point evaluates the complete call—including tool name, supplied parameters, and run context—issuing one of four verdicts: allow, deny, modify, or ask [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39].
- **Three-Stage Pipeline**:
  1. *Deterministic Rules*: Evaluate first to apply rigid invariants and automatically block prohibited operations, such as high-risk Tier 4 destinations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39].
  2. *Automated Secondary Inspection*: Requests passing deterministic rules route to secondary classifiers, specialized evaluation models, or external deterministic agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39].
  3. *Human Escalation*: Escalation to human sign-off via a [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) occurs exclusively on an explicit ask verdict [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]. The executing agent has no direct ingress or influence into any decision stage [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39].
- **Fatigue Mitigation**: Automated deterministic pre-checks mitigate documented approval fatigue, where human operators in high-frequency approval modes exhibit rubber-stamping behaviors that allow planted dangerous operations to pass manual review [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39].

# Lifecycle History

- Section 3.1 updated in PR #38 to clarify runtime hook interception and network gateway checkpoints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].
- Section 4 updated in PR #39 to implement the three-stage policy decision point framework [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39].
- Section 3.2 updated in PR #41 to specify kernel containment boundaries and escape vectors in sandbox environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41].

proposed_concept.title: AgentGateway
proposed_concept.description: Open-source traffic mediation and policy enforcement proxy managing MCP and A2A communications as an AAIF project.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

AgentGateway is an open-source traffic mediation and policy enforcement proxy governed under the Agentic AI Foundation, designed to manage Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) network communications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]. Within the foundation's architectural guidance, it operates as an authoritative network checkpoint deployed alongside in-process runtime hooks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].

# Architecture / Specification

AgentGateway provides network-level boundary controls across external agent communications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]:

- **Consolidated Endpoint**: Provides a single network ingress and egress point mediating access to remote MCP servers [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].
- **Authentication & OAuth**: Manages authentication handshakes, token exchange, and OAuth lifecycle flows on behalf of communicating agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].
- **Granular Permission Policies**: Enforces per-tool execution policies on the wire before invocations reach target servers [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].
- **Payload Capture**: Collects and structures complete invocation payloads to produce audit logs and action events [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].
- **Hook Co-Design**: Coordinates with runtime interception hooks defined in the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), where local hooks assess in-process call context while AgentGateway secures the perimeter network path [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].

# Lifecycle History

- Documented as an AAIF project and incorporated into Section 3.1 and Section 7 of the Security and Privacy Working Group's best practices guide via PR #38 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Six-step operating procedure and review workflow defining offline-first evaluation, engagement bars, voting gates, and onboarding for AAIF project candidates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process is the authoritative operating procedure for submitting, reviewing, voting on, and onboarding open-source technical projects into the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]. Implemented by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the Governing Board, and Linux Foundation operational teams, it guides project candidates through formal admission into foundation hosting[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7].

# Process Specification
Candidates file a project proposal issue in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository using the standardized issue template[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-15a00e3a][^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7]. The evaluation workflow defaults to asynchronous, offline execution across six sequential steps[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]:

1. **Initial Intake**: The AAIF CTO, assisted by an automated intake agent, performs completeness and compliance checks, smoke tests the submission, and alerts Technical Committee (TC) chairs[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].
2. **TC Q&A Window**: The Technical Committee reviews the proposal and poses questions asynchronously on the GitHub issue. Rather than requiring an individual champion, the process guarantees a collective engagement bar ensuring a minimum breadth of TC scrutiny[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]. If the bar is unmet, TC chairs may assign an on-demand TC supporter to restart review, failing which the proposal is rejected[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]. Live presentations are scheduled only on demand[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].
3. **TC Vote**: The TC conducts an offline vote via LFX Vote on technical admission and recommended initial stage[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].
4. **Governing Board (GB) Vote**: The Governing Board votes via LFX Vote to confirm organizational readiness and resource allocation[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].
5. **Legal Formation**: In parallel with votes, contributor paperwork is prepared; Linux Foundation Legal coordinates final contribution agreements, technical charters, and trademark transfers[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].
6. **Technical Onboarding**: Linux Foundation IT and project maintainers execute repository transfers and infrastructure setup[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333].

Application states are tracked publicly using issue labels: `New`, `Waiting on Comment`, `Too Early`, `Approved`, and `Declined`[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7].

# Governance and Membership Rules
Project admission is detached from commercial foundation membership: submitting organizations are not required to be AAIF members, and accepted project contributors do not automatically receive member tier status or Governing Board seats[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7]. Stage selection and graduation criteria adhere to the [Project Lifecycle Policy](./project-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy is the governing authority defining the lifecycle stages, admission criteria, graduation thresholds, and annual review procedures for technical projects hosted by the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2]. It establishes structured maturity levels that allow projects to participate, graduate, and receive mentorship and foundation support aligned with their operational maturity[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

# Lifecycle Stages
The policy defines four progressive stages for hosted projects[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2]:
- **Sandbox**: Entry stage for early-stage or experimental initiatives that align with the AAIF mission, designed to incubate innovative agentic capabilities and foster initial open-source community traction[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].
- **Growth**: Stage for maturing projects with multi-organizational contributor diversity, established governance practices, regular release cadences, and measurable production adoption[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].
- **Impact**: Flagship stage for mission-critical, production-proven agentic technologies demonstrating sustained ecosystem reliance, high-velocity maintenance, and resilient governance[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].
- **Emeritus**: Terminal stage for inactive or retired projects that have concluded active technical development and transitioned into maintenance or archival status[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

# Governance and Progression
Proposals for project admission or stage progression are submitted via the [Project Proposal Process](./project-proposal-process.md) through standardized criteria covering permissive licensing, repository infrastructure, and leadership transparency[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2][^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-15a00e3a]. The [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) conducts formal annual reviews for all active projects to evaluate adherence to stage expectations, community health, and graduation eligibility[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines define the preparation and review requirements for proposing new Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Technical Working Groups or reviving concluded groups[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2]. Operating under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md), this guide ensures proposed groups address enduring problem domains distinct from short-lived workstreams and possess concrete first-year deliverables[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].

# Eligibility and Leadership Rules
Submission and leadership thresholds are partitioned by foundation membership status[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2]:
- **Proposal Submitters**: Must represent AAIF member organizations in good standing across Platinum, Gold, Silver, or Associate tiers; non-member submitters must secure a member organization co-sponsor[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
- **Working Group Chairs**: Must be affiliated with Platinum, Gold, or Silver member organizations, distinct from the broader participant base[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
- **General Participation**: Open to all community members regardless of organizational affiliation[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].

# Proposal Structure
Proposals filed in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository must address eight standardized operational areas[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2]:
1. **Submitter Information**: Name, organization, role, and foundation membership tier[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
2. **Working Group Identity**: Formal name and one-sentence scope summary; past repository and charter history for revivals[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
3. **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Core gap analysis, relevance to agentic AI, and justification for an enduring group rather than a workstream[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
4. **Scope & Deliverables**: Normative in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries, target audiences, and year-one output formats (reports, standards, benchmarks, or reference implementations)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
5. **First-Year Plan**: 12-month delivery milestones and meeting cadence, separating ongoing mission from annual charter cycles[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
6. **Leadership & Committed Participants**: Chair nominations and committed participant rosters[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
7. **Overlap & Coordination**: Touchpoints with other AAIF working groups and external standards organizations[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
8. **Impact, Risks & Resources**: Strategic risk assessment and required foundation infrastructure or tooling[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Meeting Notes Generator is an operational agent skill and automation toolkit that synthesizes raw meeting recordings, transcripts, and summaries into standardized AAIF working group meeting minutes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63]. Originally developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the toolkit standardizes documentation across committees by automatically extracting formal decisions, action items, and discussion notes tied to source citations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

# Architecture / Specification
The generator relies on a date-driven command-line interface paired with an LFX Model Context Protocol (MCP) client to extract and format session data[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63]:
- **Data Ingestion**: Queries LFX APIs to retrieve platform-generated summaries and raw meeting transcripts, implementing local credential isolation and transcript fallback routines[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].
- **Structured Output**: Renders markdown minutes conforming to [Taxonomy Landscape Meeting Notes Guidelines](../guidelines/taxonomy-landscape-meeting-notes.md), highlighting clear consensus outcomes and explicit action item assignees[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].
- **Cross-WG Portability**: Uses configurable committee, project, and meeting identifiers to allow execution across different foundation working groups, with shared CLI tooling targeting the central `working-groups-chair` repository[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].
- **Human-in-the-Loop Verification**: Requires explicit maintainer or chair review and verification before generated minutes are merged and published to ensure factual fidelity and citation accuracy[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Operational intake guidelines, applicant eligibility criteria, issue form structure, and review lifecycle for proposing or reviving AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Working Group Submission Guidelines establish the operational process, intake requirements, and tracking workflow for proposing a new working group (WG) or reviving a concluded working group within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b]. All proposals are submitted through GitHub issues using a standardized issue template and tracked publicly on the Working Group Proposals Board [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].

# Architecture / Specification
## Submitter and Leadership Eligibility
Proposals must be authored and submitted by a representative of an AAIF member organization [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-313cc435]. While participation in working group meetings and contributions is open to everyone across the broader open-source community, working group chairs must represent Platinum, Gold, or Silver member organizations [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-313cc435]. Non-member contributors who wish to launch a working group must find an eligible member organization to sponsor and submit the proposal on their behalf [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].

## Application Intake Requirements
Proposals are created via the GitHub issue form `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/working-group-proposal.yml` in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-313cc435]. The application requires:
- **Submitter Information:** Full name, business email address, organization/affiliation (validating AAIF member status), and job role or title [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-313cc435].
- **Proposal Scope:** Working group title, problem statement, charter scope, and justification for why the effort cannot be accommodated as a workstream inside an existing working group [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-313cc435].
- **Revival Specifications:** When proposing the revival of a previously Concluded working group, submitters must link directly to the former working group repository, reference the archived charter, and detail the technical or ecosystem changes justifying reinstatement [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-313cc435].

## Review Workflow and Status Taxonomy
Once submitted, AAIF staff verify completeness, and the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) conducts asynchronous review directly on the issue [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b]. Proposals move through standardized tracking labels:
- `New`: The proposal has been submitted and placed into the review backlog [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].
- `Waiting on Comment`: Reviewers have requested supplementary information or clarification from submitters [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].
- `Too Early`: The proposal is deemed premature, and guidance for reapplication is provided [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].
- `Declined`: The proposal is rejected with rationale documented in issue comments [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].
- `Approved`: The proposal has obtained both Technical Committee and Governing Board approvals, enabling the group to form in the Sandbox lifecycle stage [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].

Approval of a proposal transitions the working group into Sandbox status to begin cadence meetings, start monthly reporting under the [Working Group Monthly Reporting Template](./working-group-reporting-template.md), and draft its formal charter under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md); it does not confer Active status, which requires subsequent Technical Committee charter approval [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question empirical survey measuring real-world agentic failure modes, accuracy challenges, and operational constraints.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Accuracy and Reliability Survey is a platform-neutral 16-question survey specification developed by the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to gather firsthand operational data from practitioners deploying AI agent systems into real-world production environments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891]. The instrument measures the operational stability, error recovery capabilities, organizational constraints, and failure consequences observed across enterprise AI deployments over six-month observation windows [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].

# Architecture / Specification
## Response Structure and Routing Logic
The instrument utilizes four distinct question interaction formats: single-select, multi-select, single-response Likert matrix, and conditional inline text fields [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891]. Participation requires approximately 20 minutes and adheres to strict privacy constraints: respondent identity and contact credentials are intentionally omitted, responses are aggregated, and raw text entries are stripped of identifying corporate information prior to storage by AAIF [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].

Eligibility is governed by Question 1 (Experience during the past six months):
- **Continuing Paths:** Serious pilot, limited deployment, broad deployment, paused or retired, and unspecified real-world use allow the participant to advance into the core survey [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].
- **Early Exit:** Prototypes/demos, secondhand knowledge, or absence of relevant experience route respondents directly to an early-exit closure section [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].

## Survey Sections and Catalog
The remaining 15 questions target a single focal system identified during eligibility screening [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891]:
- **About the System (Q2–Q6):** Assesses direct engineering or supervisory roles (Q2), primary domain/work area (Q3), structural architecture (Q4), human verification mechanisms (Q5), and organization headcount (Q6) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].
- **Benefits and Challenges (Q7–Q8):** Evaluates the primary realized benefit (Q7) paired against deployment constraints such as latency, cost, and safety boundaries (Q8) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].
- **Accuracy and Reliability (Q9–Q13):** Analyzes the recurrence of unacceptable results (Q9), underlying technical factors triggering failures (Q10), detection latency prior to real-world impact (Q11), severity of worst-case consequences (Q12), and reliance on quality evidence types (Q13) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891]. Failure factors in Q10 explicitly capture quality degradation post-system update (models, prompts, versions) and safe recovery failures resulting in dangling or partial actions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].
- **Future Priorities (Q14–Q16):** Identifies industry-wide technical priorities (Q14), preferred shared delivery resources (Q15), and open-ended commentary (Q16) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-a4aae891].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, defensive architecture patterns, builder best practice guidelines, and cross-workgroup review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared engineering discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]. The group develops vendor-neutral threat models, defensive architectural design patterns, security best practices guides, and operational security review checklists to assist builders, consumers, and peer working groups in sharing responsibility for trustworthy agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6].

# Governance and Operations
The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google), with an initial term spanning March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]. In October 2026, the Technical Committee aligned chair term boundaries with the annual anniversary of charter approval [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

To accommodate international contributors across multiple time zones, the working group maintains two alternating biweekly meetings where attending either session keeps contributors current [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]:
- **Primary Meeting**: Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM US Pacific Time [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6].
- **APAC Meeting**: Biweekly on Mondays at 9:00 PM US Eastern Time, scheduled on alternate weeks to serve Asia-Pacific working hours [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group actively stewards five primary deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93]:
1. **Threat Modeling Framework**: Following completion of the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), active threat modeling work extends foundational methodologies such as STRIDE and PASTA with MITRE ATLAS and OWASP Agentic Security Initiative catalogs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
2. **Design Patterns Catalog**: Curated vendor-neutral security and privacy design patterns in the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md). Initial production drafts have merged for [approval checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [attested isolated runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [kill switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
3. **Security Best Practices Guide**: The [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) document has published its first draft and is open to external community contributions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
4. **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: The [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) facilitates security alignment across AAIF initiatives, including joint telemetry review with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](observability-and-traceability.md) and identity synchronization with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
5. **Taxonomy and Landscape**: Cross-working group collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) checking in foundational security and privacy definitions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-02-17**: Initial orientation and scope definition [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **2026-04-14**: Charter, mission, and five core deliverables approved by working group vote [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **2026-05-26**: Charter officially approved [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **2026-09-29**: First draft of Security Best Practices merged via PR #9 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **2026-10-13**: First three architectural design patterns merged to main; Best Practices Guide opened to outside contributions; APAC meeting adjusted to Monday 9:00 PM ET [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Architectural catalog defining vendor-neutral, reusable design patterns addressing recurring security and privacy challenges in agentic AI deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is an open, vendor-neutral repository of reusable architectural patterns maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93]. The catalog equips system designers, platform engineers, and security architects with standardized mitigations for vulnerabilities that emerge when autonomous or semi-autonomous software agents invoke external tools, process untrusted instructions, and delegate execution authority [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].

# Architecture / Specification
Patterns within the catalog are structured around common operational surfaces and threat boundaries in agent harnesses. Each pattern defines concrete invariants, component responsibilities, failure modes, and implementation guidance.

Key design patterns actively developed and merged into the main repository include [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93]:
- **[Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)**: A runtime authorization checkpoint binding human or policy approval records to exact execution payloads and parameter hashes before privileged actions take place [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **[Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)**: An architectural security pattern isolating policy evaluation and cryptographic evidence generation within a hardware-attested or isolated environment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **[Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md)**: An out-of-band operational control plane mechanism capable of immediately revoking agent delegation, terminating execution loops, and isolating impacted systems during containment events [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07-21**: Design patterns catalog structural framework drafted and submitted for architecture guidance review [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **2026-09-01**: Initial review of kill-switch and containment pattern proposals [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **2026-10-13**: Working group merged initial baseline drafts of the approval checkpoint, attested runtime isolation, and kill switch patterns to the main catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering pre-execution interception hooks, gateway checkpoints, sandbox boundaries, and secret management for agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical, actionable engineering guidance for practitioners building and operating agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c]. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the document outlines defense-in-depth principles across tool execution, prompt injection defense, credential isolation, and runtime sandboxing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].

# Architecture / Specification
The guide focuses on modular, defensible architectures for agentic deployments:
- **Interception Hooks and Gateways**: Recommends inline policy enforcement points and gateways (such as [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md)) to inspect and filter tool invocations, sanitize payloads, and apply rate and budget limits [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **Isolation and Sandboxing**: Recommends strict process and network isolation for autonomous execution environments (such as [OpenSandbox](../resources/opensandbox.md) and [Nono](../resources/nono.md)), preventing lateral movement and prompt-driven host compromise [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **Secret Handling and Redaction**: Prescribes secret masking and gateway-level token replacement to prevent LLM contexts and tool call traces from leaking sensitive keys or personal data [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07-21**: Best practices workstream initiated initial authoring sessions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **2026-09-01**: Document frozen for final working group review prior to initial release [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **2026-09-29**: First draft merged via pull request #9 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a722423c].
- **2026-10-13**: Guide officially published in the repository and opened to external community pull requests and issue contributions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry models, execution trace specifications, and protocol boundary observability for agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21]. The group addresses the operational opacity of multi-turn and multi-agent systems by developing unified semantics across models, runtime harnesses, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and underlying infrastructure [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].

# Architecture and Initiatives
The working group focuses on several foundational standards and cross-ecosystem integration initiatives:
- **Cross-Boundary Observability**: Defining structured telemetry across runtime boundaries, including agent-to-tool, agent-to-MCP, and agent-to-agent interactions, using models such as the [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].
- **OpenTelemetry and OCSF Alignment**: Collaborating with the OpenTelemetry (OTel) GenAI Special Interest Group to resolve seams and inconsistencies in telemetry for coding agents, agent SDKs, and AI gateways, while partnering with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) to map observability and attestation seams to OCSF [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].
- **Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) Integration**: Incorporating standardized observability profiles and subsections into the [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].
- **Execution Verification and Cryptographic Audit**: Evaluating runtime context engines and action capsule models (such as CIGAR and Agent Action Capsules) to ensure verifiable execution replays and tamper-evident audit logs across decentralized substrates [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-10-14**: Working group reviewed CIGAR verification protocol, coordinated nine proposed telemetry extension seams for OTel GenAI SIG, and advanced joint OCSF mapping with Security and Privacy representatives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream standardizing agentic AI vocabulary, managing Domain Editor reviews, and cataloging ecosystem technologies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative tasked with curating a common, rigorous vocabulary across all technical working groups and maintaining an ecosystem landscape of agentic technologies.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-19b34556] The workstream is co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]

# Operational Model and Review Governance
The workstream operates through nominated Domain Editors representing individual AAIF working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a] Domain Editors submit candidate terms originating in their respective working groups, draft definitions in alignment with their domains, and conduct formal peer reviews.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]

Under the merge governance approved in September 2026:
- **Asynchronous Merges:** Definition pull requests merge asynchronously once two Domain Editors approve and all active review comments are resolved.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]
- **Live Votes:** Synchronous voting sessions are reserved exclusively for contested terms or unresolved disputes.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]
- **Ready for Review Milestone:** Pull requests that have completed preliminary intake and group review are assigned to a structured milestone to insulate reviewers from unsolicited or AI-generated submissions.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]

# Deliverables and Status
- **Taxonomy:** As of September 2026, 8 core definitions have merged (including terms covering human oversight and identity fundamentals), with dozens more undergoing cross-working-group review across Observability, Workflows, Security, and Commerce domains.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]
- **Landscape:** Work on the technology landscape deliverable was formally paused in September 2026 to focus full bandwidth on resolving the core taxonomy, pending the establishment of neutral inclusion criteria approved by the Technical Committee (`../governance/technical-committee.md`).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]

# Lifecycle History
Formed in mid-2026, the workstream established initial schemas and intake pipelines in June 2026, initiated systematic backlog reviews in July and August, and established its asynchronous two-editor approval standard in September 2026.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-19b34556][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) aligns emerging international regulatory instruments, risk management taxonomies, and compliance standards with operational agent implementations.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7] The group is chaired by Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase) and co-chaired by Sriram Natarajan (Google).[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7]

# Deliverables and Workstreams
- **Regulatory Gap Analysis:** The working group benchmarks regional and international agentic AI policies and regulatory instruments against an established 16-theme baseline.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7] In Phase 2, the group standardized prompt-driven policy evaluation methods to ensure consistent cross-jurisdictional assessments by regional contributors.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7]
- **Operationalizing Agent Governance:** A core proposal submitted to the Technical Committee (`../governance/technical-committee.md`) defining practical frameworks for implementing runtime risk controls, policy gates, and organizational oversight across agent fleets.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7]
- **Legal Context Schema:** An upcoming structural schema for expressing legal, compliance, and jurisdictional constraints in machine-readable formats for agent reasoning and execution.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7]
- **Agentic Evidence Collection Best Practice Guide:** Builder guidance specifying verifiable logging and evidence preservation techniques required for regulatory auditability and accountability.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7]

# Lifecycle History
Following a leadership transition in autumn 2026, Deborah Eng assumed the chair role and Sriram Natarajan was elected co-chair to coordinate workstreams and inter-working-group alignment across the AAIF ecosystem.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-60f28464dd94-576a1dc7]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering pre-execution interception hooks, gateway checkpoints, sandbox boundaries, and confidential computing limits.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide provides operational recommendations for engineering teams deploying autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents. It addresses interception mechanisms, architectural isolation, sandbox containment, and credential boundary controls to prevent unauthorized actions and data exfiltration.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42]

# Execution Boundary Controls and Credential Exposure
Runtime security for agent execution environments depends on understanding the precise isolation guarantees provided by host and hardware sandboxes:
- **Pre-Execution Interception:** Agent tool calls and external interactions must pass through policy checkpoints prior to execution.
- **Confidential Computing Boundaries:** While confidential computing technologies (such as Intel TDX or AMD SEV) protect guest memory and CPU state from untrusted hosts or hypervisors, hardware isolation does not automatically mitigate bearer token exposure.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42] Once a bearer token is released to software inside the guest environment, exposure is dictated strictly by that token's permissions, validity lifetime, and operational hygiene rather than hardware protection alone.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42]
- **Least-Privilege Token Scoping:** Tokens injected into agent runtimes should be cryptographically bound, short-lived, and scoped strictly to intended tasks to prevent replay in the event of guest-level compromise.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42]

# Lifecycle History
Authored within the Security & Privacy Working Group (`../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`), Section 2 was updated to refine threat modeling around confidential computing, clarifying that host memory protection does not negate bearer credential vulnerability inside the guest environment.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Working Group Meeting Notes Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill and CLI toolkit automating LFX transcript retrieval, structured decision synthesis, and meeting record publication.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-wg-meeting-notes` skill provides an automated toolkit and agent workflow for retrieving, parsing, and summarizing AAIF working group meetings hosted on the Linux Foundation LFX platform.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-3] It extracts transcripts, structures agenda discussions, and synthesizes formal decision records in accordance with foundation reporting standards.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-3]

# Architecture / Specification
The toolkit comprises modular components designed for reproducible and secure execution:
- **LFX MCP Client:** Interfaces with the LFX platform over the Model Context Protocol using OAuth via `mcp-remote` or bearer token authentication, supporting tool discovery and result pagination.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-3]
- **Transcript Utilities:** Downloads and parses Zoom transcripts in WebVTT or plain-text formats, featuring an optional Playwright fallback for resilient retrieval.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-3]
- **Structured-Output Model Client:** Submits extracted dialogue through OpenAI-compatible endpoints enforcing strict JSON Schema completions for meeting agendas, action items, and formal consensus decisions.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-3]
- **Execution Safeguards:** Enforces date and URL validation, private no-overwrite local JSON export, and credential-safe error messaging to prevent token leakage in CI/CD logs.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-3]

# Lifecycle History
Developed across the working group chairs coordination repository, the toolkit evolved from custom scripts into a standardized package featuring pinned dependencies, unit tests, and multi-auth LFX clients.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-3]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry models, execution trace formats, harness evaluation criteria, and cross-boundary diagnostics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, causal trace structures, and verification models across agent execution lifecycles. Its efforts center on cross-boundary observability across models, agent harnesses, tool runtimes, and external services.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66]

# Workstreams and Technical Scope
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** Developing common execution schemas (`../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md`) capturing agent prompts, tool invocations, state mutations, and causal dependencies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66]
- **Evidence Harness Evaluation:** Scoping auditable publication requirements for evidence harnesses to allow third parties to independently verify and falsify harness evaluation claims.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66] The proposed framework establishes eight auditable properties: commitment before observation, coverage identity, pinned trust roots, separation of observation from judgement, typed outcomes with first-class refusals, benign cost accounting, adversarial maintenance, and temporal ordering of authorization bounds and withdrawals.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66]
- **Cross-Boundary Diagnostics:** Correlating telemetry across Model Context Protocol boundaries (`../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md`) and direct subprocess invocations (`../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md`).

# Lifecycle History
Formed as a core technical workstream within the AAIF, the group expanded its charter from telemetry trace formats to include harness evaluation auditability and conformance test kits.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66]
