proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, defensive architecture patterns, builder best practices, and security taxonomies across the AAIF ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI ecosystem, producing open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and reusable design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Leadership
The working group is led by appointed leadership representing member organizations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]:
- **Chair**: Alex Frazer (@awfrazer), Runlayer
- **Co-Chair**: Junjie Bu (@mindpower), Google

The chairs were appointed by Platinum and Gold working group members for a term extending from March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e].

## Meeting Structure
To ensure global participation across time zones, the working group maintains two alternating biweekly meetings, with the chair bridging notes and action items across both sessions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]:
- **Primary Meeting**: Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT (USA Pacific Time) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e].
- **APAC Meeting**: Biweekly on Mondays at 9:00 PM ET (USA Eastern Time), landing on alternating weeks from the primary meeting to serve Asia-Pacific working hours [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].

## Active Workstreams and Key Deliverables
The working group organizes its technical outputs into distinct collaborative workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]:
- **Threat Modeling**: Evaluates structural risks across agentic frameworks and catalogs coverage gaps across existing security standards, published in [agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **Builder Best Practices**: Produces practical implementation guidelines and static analysis rules for agent developers, detailed in [agentic-ai-security-best-practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Curates architectural patterns addressing recurring security boundaries, including [approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md), collected in [security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape**: Contributes security- and privacy-domain terminology to the cross-cutting taxonomy efforts coordinated by [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-02-17**: Orientation meeting establishing AAIF governance framework and preliminary ideation on security and privacy domains [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **2026-03-03**: Alex Frazer introduced as elected chair; charter refinement begins [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **2026-04-14**: Scope, initial deliverables, and charter approved by formal working group vote [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **2026-05-26**: Working group charter officially approved by the Technical Committee; Junjie Bu confirmed as Taxonomy lead [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **2026-06-23**: Working group repositories made public; monthly Technical Committee reporting cadence adopted [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **2026-08-04 to 2026-09-29**: Security best practices guide frozen and merged; threat modeling gap analysis advanced; APAC alternate-week meeting trialed and scheduled [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **2026-10-13 to 2026-10-27**: Core design patterns merged into catalog; 90-day attestation and verification pilot proposed; discussions held on agent action capsule Merkle attestation and KYC-backed internet kill-switch protocols [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].

proposed_concept.title: Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses
proposed_concept.description: Standardized profile defining administrative harness lifecycle events, external authorization checkpoints, invocation chain delegation, and audit logging.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses profile standardizes the programmatic interfaces an agentic harness exposes to administrative systems for lifecycle observability and external authorization gating.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44] It establishes an interoperable contract for policy decision points (PDPs) and enforcement points, bridging runtime execution with organizational security baselines.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

# Architecture / Specification
The profile composes several industry standards and AAIF specifications into a unified runtime enforcement architecture:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Authorization Checkpoints**: Uses OpenID AuthZEN to mediate external authorization requests at critical decision checkpoints prior to tool or model execution.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Lifecycle Events**: Binds event definitions to the portable hook names from [Agent Plugins](../standards/agent-plugins.md) and formats audit records using Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Invocation Chain and Delegation**: Leverages OAuth token exchange to enforce monotonic privilege narrowing and sub-agent scope issuance across child agent delegations (`parent_uid`).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44] Root authority is issued by the server and pinned to the administrator-configured PDP.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Context Provenance and Integrity**: Labels context sources across sessions (such as `untrusted` and `sensitive`) combined with `net:egress` network scopes, enabling policy decision points to enforce dual-control rules like the Rule of Two.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]
- **Failure Modes**: Formulates normative closed-world behaviors, standardizing `fail_closed_deny` for integrity failures and client connection timeouts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

The profile directly realizes concrete implementations of design patterns cataloged in [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md), including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md), while standardizing differences between stateless PDP verification and stateful single-use action IDs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

# Lifecycle History
Introduced in WG Security and Privacy PR #44 as draft profile v0.3 under the design patterns workstream, pending formal deliverable adoption and cross-working group review with the [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-44]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry models, execution trace formats, harness evaluation, and semantic conventions for agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry models, causal execution trace representations, and logging conventions across agentic frameworks, runtimes, and execution environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f] It collaborates closely with upstream standards bodies including the OpenTelemetry GenAI Special Interest Group to harmonize agent telemetry semantics.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group drives several technical workstreams:
- **Turn and Step Semantics**: Formalizing the definition of an agent "turn" (a single input triggering a sequence of internal actions) and distinguishing it from individual execution "steps" to establish uniform OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and token usage attribution.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]
- **Telemetry and Evidence Seams**: Defining five architectural seams connecting OpenTelemetry GenAI spans to cryptographically signed action and evidence records: span-to-record join, decision and approval binding, effect target and status reporting, evidence origin provenance, and integrity without content disclosure.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]
- **Multi-Language SDK Alignment**: Coordinating cross-language support (Go, Rust, Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript) across foundational infrastructure components and client SDKs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]
- **Cross-Domain and Attestation Liaison**: Coordinating with the [Attestation and Evidence](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md) and [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) working groups on cross-boundary provenance and tamper-evident tracing.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

# Lifecycle History
In October 2026, the working group initiated contributions to the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG regarding turn definitions, submitted proposals on evidence layer integration seams, and launched coordination on attestation trials and memory context working group proposals.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]

mutations.rationale: Incorporate OpenTelemetry GenAI telemetry integration seams connecting spans to signed action and evidence records.

proposed_concept.title: OpenTelemetry
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral observability framework and collector pipeline standardizing traces, metrics, logs, and GenAI agent semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
OpenTelemetry is an open-source observability framework providing vendor-neutral APIs, SDKs, and instrumentation for collecting distributed traces, metrics, and logs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f] Within the AAIF ecosystem, OpenTelemetry serves as the primary distributed tracing substrate, with active workstreams mapping GenAI semantic conventions to agentic workflows and verifiable evidence records.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]

# Architecture / Specification
OpenTelemetry's agentic integration focuses on extending semantic conventions and establishing clean seams to runtime governance artifacts:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]
- **Turn vs. Step Tracing**: Standardizing span hierarchies where a top-level turn captures a user interaction and nested child spans trace individual model invocations, tool calls, and execution steps.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]
- **Evidence Seam 1 (Span to Record Join)**: Linking OpenTelemetry trace and span identifiers directly to external signed records such as [Action Records](../taxonomy/action-record.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]
- **Evidence Seam 2 (Decision and Approval)**: Capturing policy evaluation results and human approval states inside telemetry spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]
- **Evidence Seam 3 (Effect Target and Status)**: Recording target resource identifiers, mutation state, and side-effect outcomes within trace attributes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]
- **Evidence Seam 4 (Evidence Origin)**: Propagating cryptographic origin and witness metadata across span context.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]
- **Evidence Seam 5 (Integrity without Disclosure)**: Preserving trace content authenticity via hashes without leaking sensitive payload data in trace collectors.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]

# Lifecycle History
In October 2026, the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) drafted proposals to align OpenTelemetry semantic conventions with signed action and evidence record specifications.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-67]

proposed_concept.title: Attestation and Evidence Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF working group establishing decentralized standards, evidence classes, and witness mechanisms for agent verification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attestation and Evidence Working Group is a cross-cutting AAIF body establishing vendor-neutral standards, evidence models, and witness architectures to verify agent provenance, authority, and runtime actions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f] It provides foundational verification mechanisms that bridge telemetry traces, identity assertions, and compliance audits.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

# Architecture / Specification
The group focuses on resolving verification gaps across multi-agent environments:
- **Interim Working Group Trial**: Operating under a 90-day trial initiated in late 2026 to evaluate whether the initiative should transition into a permanent working group, workstream, or cross-working group under the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]
- **Cross-Group Coordination**: Collaborating with [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to integrate tamper-evident logging and signed evidence structures into operational harnesses.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]
- **Proof of Control and Verification**: Partnering with industry groups and projects to develop attestation models for autonomous agent decision-making and cross-domain action validity.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

# Lifecycle History
Formed as an interim working group undergoing a 90-day evaluation period as reported to the Observability and Traceability Working Group on October 28, 2026, aimed at formulating long-term recommendations for the Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e1eff34e54a6-f9dca54f]

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing technical vision, project lifecycles, and foundation standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), responsible for steering foundation-wide technical vision, establishing standard practices, and managing the lifecycle of foundation projects and working groups [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]. Appointed by the AAIF Governing Board, the TC oversees standards development, evaluates project proposals, and reviews periodic working group deliverables.

# Architecture / Specification
## Composition and Leadership
For the term spanning March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026, the Technical Committee comprises eight appointed members across industry organizations [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]:
- **Chair**: David Soria Parra (Anthropic)
- **Co-Chair**: Caitie McCaffrey (Microsoft)
- **Members**: Alan Blount (Google), Bradley Axen (Block), James Ward (Amazon Web Services), Nick Cooper (OpenAI), Sambhav Kothari (Bloomberg), and Steve Faulkner (Cloudflare)

## Governance Responsibilities
The TC enforces and maintains core operating procedures and technical policies:
- **Technical Charter**: Specifies the committee's purpose, voting rules, and technical jurisdiction [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852].
- **Project Lifecycle Policy**: Dictates admission criteria, stage progressions (Sandbox, Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and periodic health reviews [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852] (see [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)).
- **Project Proposal Process**: Establishes offline evaluation bars, intellectual property agreements, voting protocols, and onboarding steps [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852] (see [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md)).
- **Working Group Governance**: Governs creation, renewal, and reporting policies for foundation working groups [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852] (see [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)).

## Project Oversight
The TC actively oversees foundational initiatives across lifecycle tiers [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]:
- **Agent Router** (Growth Stage): Traffic control plane for agent communications.
- **Agent Skills** (Impact Stage): Open packaging specification for agent capabilities and domain skills (see [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md)).
- **Agent2Agent (A2A)** (Growth Stage): Open protocol for interoperable agent-to-agent communication.

# References
- [AAIF Technical Committee Repository](https://github.com/aaif/technical-committee) [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-fc8fa852]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Schema
proposed_concept.description: Classification schema defining structural workflow dimensions and active proposals for cross-boundary interaction categorizations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification Schema establishes a structured taxonomy for cataloging and analyzing enterprise and horizontal agentic workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-60]. Developed under the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), the schema provides structural dimensions to describe agent initiation, autonomy gates, coordination models, and execution linearity.

# Architecture / Specification
## Established Classification Dimensions
The core schema organizes agent workflows across five foundational architectural dimensions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-60]:
1. **Trigger / Initiation**: Event-driven versus schedule- or human-initiated workflows.
2. **Governance Gate**: Autonomy level and presence of human checkpoints (e.g., approval gates).
3. **Agent Topology**: Single-agent sufficient versus multi-agent coordination models.
4. **Execution Flexibility**: Fixed or scripted logic versus dynamic path selection.
5. **Orchestration Pattern**: Sequential pipelines, parallel fan-outs, or iterative convergence loops.

## Proposed Boundary Dimension
An open proposal within the working group introduces an organizational boundary dimension to distinguish workflows based on data and approval demarcation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-60]:
- **Same team**: Workflow outputs and operational scopes remain within a single internal team (e.g., automated resume screening).
- **Across teams**: Workflows cross organizational boundaries requiring external handoffs and inter-department approvals (e.g., access request fulfillment or legal hold notifications).
- **Across companies**: Workflows negotiate or execute interactions across independent commercial entities (e.g., autonomous inventory reordering).

This proposed dimension addresses routing, verification, and boundary-crossing constraints that alter workflow governance across entries in the [Agentic Use Case Inventory](./agentic-use-case-inventory.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-60].

# References
- [WG Workflows and Process Integration Issue #60](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/issues/60) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-60]

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral specifications, attestation models, and delegated-authority conformance frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust Working Group develops vendor-neutral specifications, trust frameworks, and verification architectures for agent identity, authentication, and delegated authority [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]. It establishes normative standards for verifiable principal attribution and credential lifecycles across decentralized and cross-domain agent interactions.

# Architecture / Specification
## Delegated-Authority Conformance Framework
The working group is developing a conformance evaluation framework to validate systems implementing Reference Architecture v1 delegation rules [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]. A central principle of this framework is mandatory residual disclosure, requiring candidate designs to state explicitly which failure modes remain uncovered alongside their trade-offs [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22].

The framework defines eight core conformance test cases [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]:
1. **Delegator Revocation Cascade**: Verifying that revocation of a principal cascades across all derived downstream authority within declared time bounds.
2. **Object and Action Binding**: Preventing replay or scope escalation across unauthorized objects, counterparties, or operations.
3. **Stale Revocation Handling**: Enforcing bounded revocation propagation windows and prohibiting reliance on an agent's self-reported authorization status.
4. **Escalation and Approver Unavailability**: Ensuring authority fails closed and never widens when designated approvers are unreachable.
5. **Attenuation Across Multi-Hop Chains**: Verifying that downstream hops strictly narrow authority and cannot amplify permissions beyond delegator grants.
6. **Authority vs. Identity Expiration**: Ensuring authority checks verify grant-specific lifetimes independently of underlying identity validity.
7. **Delegation Chain Privacy**: Preventing delegation paths from leaking internal graph topology or principal linkages to untrusted counterparties.
8. **Disputed or Wrongful Revocation**: Requiring tamper-evident audit trails for revocation actions, formal contestation procedures, or explicit non-reversal residual disclosures.

# References
- [WG Identity and Trust Issue #22](https://github.com/aaif/wg-identity-and-trust/issues/22) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Slack Audit Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only Slack workspace inspection skill auditing channel topology, organizer presence, member demographics, and spam patterns as phase 8 of community estate sync.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-audit-slack` skill is a read-only community inspection procedure that evaluates an AAIF Slack workspace's health, chapter channel coverage, organizer memberships, subject-matter topic activity, and member roster composition [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e]. It operates as phase 8 of the community estate synchronization pipeline orchestrated by [aaif-sync](../skills/aaif-sync.md), providing an independent validation layer executed through a separate code path from the estate mutation scripts [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].

# Architecture / Specification
The audit architecture executes three core reporting engines over the workspace alongside a shared activity measurement layer and an on-demand spam detection utility [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e]:

- **Organizers Audit (`audit_organizers.py`):** Verifies that every local chapter has designated public and private `-organizers` channels and confirms that accepted organizers are present in their corresponding chapter channels [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].
- **Topics Audit (`audit_topics.py`):** Inspects subject-matter discussion rooms to identify stale, quiet, or overlapping channels and verify discoverability for newcomers [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].
- **Members Audit (`audit_members.py`):** Analyzes the overall workspace structure, user accounts, and newcomer onboarding experience [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].
- **Activity Measurement (`audit_activity.py`):** Captures operational telemetry including timestamp of the last human message, historical message volume, and distinct active posters per channel to feed topic and member analyses [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].
- **On-Demand Spam Scanner (`audit_spam.py`):** Scans public channels, message threads, and fixed phrase searches across visible direct messages for promotional pitches, partnership solicitations, or credential rentals, outputting leads strictly to terminal output without automated mutation [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].
- **Report Aggregation (`summarize_audits.py`):** Compiles findings into a consolidated single-page HTML report indexing the four audit dimensions with a ranked priority list of remediation actions [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].

Operational invariants enforce read-only execution: all discrepancy findings must be resolved at their primary data sources—such as [aaif-clean-data](../skills/aaif-clean-data.md) or chapter registration sheets—prior to re-running the sync pipeline [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e]. Workspace files and exports must be processed using Python and the Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) interacting with native cloud document APIs, prohibiting desktop office software like LibreOffice from modifying or converting templates [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-92673e4e].

# References

- [AAIF Estate Synchronization](../skills/aaif-sync.md)
- [AAIF Data Cleaning](../skills/aaif-clean-data.md)

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral specifications, attestation models, and delegated authorization frameworks for AI agents across internal, B2B, and B2C interactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an AAIF technical body defining vendor-neutral frameworks, attestation models, identity primitives, and authorization boundaries for autonomous agents [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f]. Co-chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE), the working group focuses on core concepts including agent identity, delegation, action records, and consent receipts across enterprise and open-network boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables across three dedicated sub-working groups [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f]:

- **Taxonomy Sub-WG:** Coordinates with the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream to formalize definitions for trust, attestation, delegation, and identifiers [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f].
- **Reference Architecture Sub-WG:** Adopts a bottom-up, primitive-first strategy that authors foundational primitives—commencing with the agent [identity](../taxonomy/identity.md) primitive—before assembling them into composite reference architectures and runtime profiles [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f].
- **Critical Use Cases Sub-WG:** Formulates illustrative agent lifecycle models spanning internal, business-to-business (B2B), and business-to-consumer (B2C) topologies across six lifecycle stages: naming, deployment, delegation, access control, audit/compliance, and retirement/revocation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f].

Core functional requirements established by the working group include verifiable delegation chains, dynamic per-request authorization gates, content-private [action records](../taxonomy/action-record.md) with selective disclosure, and principal-attested credential revocation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f]. The group integrates external industrial architectural patterns into its evaluation pipeline, including NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace reference design and Uber's agentic identity model [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-922f59c26329-928a222f].

# References

- [Action Record](../taxonomy/action-record.md)
- [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)

mutations.rationale: Update the kill switch pattern to incorporate open-internet agent revocation mechanisms, decentralized ledger status anchoring, propagation latency bounds, and multi-tier revocation triggers.

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch
proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern establishing an independent out-of-band containment loop to halt, isolate, or revoke agent operational authority across local runtimes and open networks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Kill Switch pattern establishes an out-of-band architectural control plane mechanism capable of halting agent execution, isolating running workloads, and instantly revoking operational credentials when anomalous, compromised, or policy-violating behavior is detected [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]. Operating independently of the agent's primary decision loop, it ensures that neither context drift, prompt injection, nor runtime subversion can suppress an authorized shutdown or revocation command [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern supports containment across both enterprise boundaries and open-internet environments through layered revocation paths and verification mechanisms [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]:

- **Runtime and Principal Termination:** A direct interrupt triggered either locally by the agent runtime sandbox or externally by an authenticated [principal](../taxonomy/principal.md) bearing a cryptographic revocation credential [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Cascading Credential Revocation:** A hierarchical invalidation trigger that cascades from a principal's identity root to synchronously revoke all subordinate [subagents](../taxonomy/subagent.md) and delegated capabilities issued under that principal [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Issuer Status Root Invalidation:** Out-of-band emergency revocation executed by an identity issuer or credential authority, updating global status roots across verification endpoints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Decentralized Status Anchoring:** For open-network deployments outside enterprise perimeter identity providers (such as SPIFFE or CAEP-enabled IdPs), revocation states may be recorded on decentralized ledgers or append-only status registries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]. This ensures verifiers maintain local access to fresh revocation proofs even during centralized DNS or hyperscaler network partitions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Propagation and Enforcement Latency:** Production implementations define strict bounds for global verifier convergence; for example, open-network zero-knowledge verification frameworks target guaranteed verifier refusal bounds within 245 seconds of on-chain recording, with empirical test runs demonstrating refusal within 34 seconds [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Protocol Event Integration:** Revocation signals can be injected as asynchronous control events into gateway and tool mediation protocols (such as Model Context Protocol servers), denying tool invocation at authentication and dispatch checkpoints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

# References
- [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an AAIF technical body developing defensive architectural patterns, threat modeling methodologies, security best practice guides, and cross-workstream review checklists for agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]. The group collaborates across AAIF technical projects and external industry consortia to provide actionable security baselines without duplicating established application security catalogs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains several active technical workstreams and operational initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a]:

- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Conducts structured architectural reviews of emerging AAIF deliverables, with active liaison representation from [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) and pending representation from governance workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Project Builder Alignment:** Developing bi-directional feedback mechanisms using GitHub automated workflows to dispatch issues into AAIF project repositories upon deliverable publication, alerting builders to breaking changes and gathering deployment feedback [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Design Patterns and Threat Modeling:** Curates reusable mitigation patterns such as the [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) and evaluates runtime verification models including context intelligence graph runtimes and agent action capsules [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Taxonomy Alignment:** Coordinates with the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream to standardize security and privacy terms within the official foundation vocabulary [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].
- **Cross-Ecosystem Coordination:** Engages external bodies including the x402 Identity Working Group and the Open Secure AI Alliance to align terminology and identity standards while focusing AAIF efforts on net-new agentic security challenges rather than competing with established application security lists [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-51e9e85a].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model Specification
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry standard defining execution context propagation, causal execution tracing, and turn-based decision reconciliation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry standard defining portable execution context propagation, causal execution tracing, and decision-to-action reconciliation across AI agent harnesses, multi-agent orchestrations, and tool boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71] Governed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), it aligns agent-specific operational concepts with the [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) ecosystem.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]

# Architecture / Specification
The specification formalizes execution semantics across agent lifecycles:

- **Turn and Step Execution Model**: Defines a normalized turn structure and downstream execution units for agent interaction cycles.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72] The model formalizes the concepts of a "Turn" and "Agent step" (with "Step" as an alias) for vocabulary alignment, while preserving "Turn segment" as an OpenTelemetry span construct to structure upstream GenAI Special Interest Group (SIG) proposals.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]
- **Telemetry Gap Analysis**: Identifies seven foundational gaps in how contemporary coding agents, agent SDKs, and AI gateways adopt OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71] These encompass missing semantic conventions, divergent span interpretation issues, unadopted existing conventions, and instrumentation defects across runtime boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71]

# Lifecycle History
In October 2026, the working group introduced working documents covering the seven-part OpenTelemetry gap analysis ([PR #71](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/pull/71)) and the turn proposal specification ([PR #72](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/pull/72)) to coordinate upstream alignment with the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Structured catalog detailing operational agent observability use cases, cross-cutting telemetry requirements, and regulatory audit criteria.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog documents structural, operational, and regulatory observability scenarios across autonomous agents, multi-agent frameworks, and external tools.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68] Developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the catalog establishes standardized telemetry requirements across runtime environments.

# Architecture / Specification
Use cases within the catalog define granular functional requirements across evaluation, debugging, auditability, and compliance:

- **E4 Compliance and Auditability Requirement**: Requires tamper-evident storage with a declared retention basis rather than immutable write-once-read-many (WORM) storage.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68] Record integrity must remain cryptographically verifiable through hash chaining and external timestamping without requiring personal identifiers to be preserved beyond the lifespan permitted under GDPR (e.g., Art. 17 right to erasure, Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation) and EU AI Act retention mandates (Art. 19(1) for providers and Art. 26(6) for deployers).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68]
- **Typed Tombstones**: When personal identifiers or authorization records are excised under policy or data-subject erasure requests, the evidence record must retain a typed tombstone.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68] This mechanism permits verifiers to distinguish legitimately expired attributes from unpopulated or tampered fields.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68]

# Lifecycle History
In October 2026, the working group updated use case E4 via PR #68 to eliminate strict write-once storage constraints in favor of declared retention periods and typed tombstone markers to reconcile cryptographic auditability with European data protection regulations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68]

proposed_concept.title: URACE (Unified Runtime for Autonomous Collaborative Evolution)
proposed_concept.description: Open-source P2P-first lifecycle control plane and execution runtime governing autonomous AI-assisted software improvements.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
URACE (Unified Runtime for Autonomous Collaborative Evolution) is an open-source, peer-to-peer (P2P) lifecycle control plane and execution runtime designed to govern autonomous AI-assisted software evolution.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67] Proposed for the AAIF Growth lifecycle stage under the Apache 2.0 license, URACE enables AI executors to discover, propose, qualify, and distribute verified code improvements across decentralized networks without central coordination.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]

# Architecture / Specification
URACE provides a governed runtime architecture bridging agent model outputs with production codebases:

- **Governed Improvement Loop**: Enforces an operational pipeline transitioning objectives to executor plans, qualification gate evaluation, accepted operations, and an immutable HMAC-chained ledger.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67] AI executors are prevented by schema enforcement from modifying governance rules, authority boundaries, or qualification criteria.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]
- **Decentralized P2P Feature Marketplace**: Facilitates tokenized exchange and borrowing of verified code improvements between network peers using a physics-calibrated token economy with Sybil-resistant reputation scoring based on the Wilson lower-bound algorithm.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]
- **Cryptographic Security**: Employs hybrid post-quantum cryptography combining ML-KEM-768 with classical TLS, alongside self-signed certificates and tamper-evident audit trails.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]
- **Composability**: Exposes an `AGENTS.md` machine-readable onboarding API surface, allowing integration with external agent frameworks as gated executors while generating compatible software provenance records.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]

# Lifecycle History
Originally developed as an independent research and production codebase with 280 source files and 2,677 tests, URACE was submitted to the AAIF Technical Committee in Issue #67 as a candidate for Growth stage adoption under the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md).[^evt-project-proposals-issue-67]

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry models, execution trace formats, and harness evaluation benchmarks for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body established to standardize vendor-neutral telemetry models, causal execution tracing, and runtime observability across AI agent workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-74] The group maintains key deliverables including the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) and the [Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its operational agenda across several technical tracks:

- **Trace Model and Telemetry Standardization**: Develops the Agent Behavior Trace Model, identifying telemetry gaps across coding agents, agent SDKs, and gateways, and formalizing turn and step execution semantics for upstream standardization.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72]
- **Upstream Standards Coordination**: Maintains formal liaison channels via a designated liaison roster to coordinate directly with the [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) GenAI Special Interest Group (SIG) and related industry standards bodies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-73]
- **Compliance and Audit Telemetry**: Reconciles cryptographic execution logging and evidence verification with regulatory privacy mandates such as GDPR erasure duties and EU AI Act retention periods.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-68]

# Lifecycle History
In October 2026, the working group published gap analyses for OpenTelemetry agent adoption ([PR #71](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/pull/71)), formulated a Turn semantic model for the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG ([PR #72](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/pull/72)), established an upstream liaison roster ([PR #73](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/pull/73)), and filed its monthly progress report ([PR #74](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/pull/74)).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-71][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-72][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-73][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-74]

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity standards, design tokens, typography specifications, surface constraints, and motif rules governing Agentic AI Foundation digital and print artifacts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) brand and design system establishes normative visual presentation rules, typography standards, surface constraints, and graphical motif bounds across foundation reports, digital artifacts, and community assets [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. All generated outputs—including HTML operational reports and compiled PDF documents—must strictly conform to the shared design system tokens and layout invariants [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].

# Architecture / Specification

### Source of Truth and Token Pipeline

The foundational source of truth is `design/aaif-design-system.html`, a self-extracting bundle defining tokens, component specifications, and sample layouts [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. The CSS token definitions (`design/aaif-tokens.css`) are generated from this bundle via `scripts/extract_design_tokens.py` and must never be edited manually [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. Continuous integration enforces token currency using automated stale-check verification [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].

### Color Palette and Accents

- **Primary Accent**: The primary action accent is black (`--accent: var(--ink)`) [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **Spectrum Accents**: Spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) serve exclusively as internal accents within an individual surface, with only one hue leading at a time [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. Coral is designated as `--spec-8` and is not the organizational brand accent [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **Surfaces**: Artifacts exist on two first-class surfaces: white editorial and black plate [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. General reports utilize the white editorial ground (`--paper`), using `--paper-2` for occasional section banding and `--paper-3` for tinted panels [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. Dark mode (`prefers-color-scheme`) is strictly prohibited [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].

### Typography and Structural Elements

- **Typeface**: Instrument Sans (SIL Open Font License) is the singular typeface across UI and display surfaces in weights 400, 500, 600, and 700 [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. Monospace typography is drawn from a system stack and restricted to metadata, labels, and eyebrows [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **Headings**: Primary headings utilize weight 500, tracking `-0.02em`, and line-height 1.05–1.15; weight 600 is reserved for h5/h6 levels (`--t-xl`/`--t-lg`) [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **Flat Aesthetic**: Elevation drop shadows are barred; visual separation relies on 1px hairlines, surface tinting, and inset strokes [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7]. Cards, tables, and metric chips maintain square corners (`border-radius: 0`), reserving rounded radii (`--radius-pill`) exclusively for badges and pill buttons [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].

### Mark Integrity and Agent Motif

- **Logomark SVGs**: The official SVGs (`aaif-mark.svg`, `aaif-mark-square.svg`, and `aaif-logo-white.svg`) must be used directly without redrawing or geometric approximations [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].
- **Agent Motif**: The robot illustration constructed from logomark primitives is limited to empty states, loading indicators, event collateral, and visual dividers; it is strictly banned from governance, board, or press communications [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-bbae69b7].

# References

- [`../skills/aaif-brand-guidelines.md`](../skills/aaif-brand-guidelines.md)
- [`../skills/community-event-operations.md`](../skills/community-event-operations.md)

proposed_concept.title: aaif-create-chapter
proposed_concept.description: Operational provisioning and lifecycle skill managing TemplateCity cloning, OOXML rebrand transformations, map dot repositioning, and four-surface chapter renames.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` operational skill provisions new AAIF city chapters within the Google Drive estate by cloning the standard `TemplateCity` directory, performing deterministic string and asset rebranding, recalculating geographic coordinate indicators, and executing multi-surface chapter renames [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a] [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].

# Architecture / Specification

### Tooling Invariants and File Handling

All Google Drive operations are mediated strictly through Python calling the `gws` command-line utility [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]. File manipulation follows strict format separation:
- Native Google Workspace assets (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) must be modified via the Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides APIs [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- Stored Office files (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`) undergo in-memory OOXML zip-part surgery to preserve embedded brand typography and untouched structural elements [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- Desktop office tooling such as LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` are categorically prohibited for rendering or editing because they substitute system fonts and corrupt proprietary OOXML elements [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].

### Rebranding Scope and Map Dot Positioning

Chapter creation replaces the template tokens `San Francisco`, `SF` abbreviation variants, Luma slugs (`aaif-<slug>`), and corresponding file/folder labels, leaving event-specific speaker and scheduling placeholders untouched [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]. In addition, the skill repositions the network map marker on slide 5 ("THE NETWORK") of `Event Template/Slides.pptx` to the target city's real geographic coordinates via keyless Nominatim lookups or explicit `--lat`/`--lon` arguments [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].

### Four-Surface In-Place Chapter Renaming

When renaming an existing chapter via `scripts/rename_chapter.py`, the skill coordinates updates across four decoupled surfaces [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c]:
1. **Chapter Folder**: Top-level directory renaming on Google Drive [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
2. **File and Subfolder Names**: Nested file assets and icon directories [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
3. **OOXML Text**: Internal text runs inside `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` document parts [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
4. **Document Metadata**: Standard OOXML core properties (`docProps`) [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].

Luma slugs are explicitly decoupled from the city name pass to prevent link breakage on live community pages, relationship files (`.rels`) only receive slug changes, and pre-change assets are archived under `backups/rename-<UTC>/` prior to Drive upload [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].

# References

- [`../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md`](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md)
- [`../skills/community-event-operations.md`](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- [`../skills/aaif-sync.md`](../skills/aaif-sync.md)

proposed_concept.description: Procedural estate synchronization orchestrator reconciling community sheets, gating chapter listings to accepted organizers, and rendering unified navigation across run report pages.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-sync` operational skill synchronizes AAIF community records, Google Drive folders, and chapter listings, enforcing strict organizer validation rules and generating interconnected HTML operational reports [^evt-community-events-pr-62] [^evt-community-events-pr-63].

# Architecture / Specification

### Accepted Organizer Gating and Removal Safeguards

Chapter folder creation triggers and public chapter listings are restricted exclusively to locations with accepted organizers [^evt-community-events-pr-62]:
- **CRM Sync Validation**: The `sync_crm` module lists only cities with an accepted organizer for chapter provisioning, suppressing unverified applicants, pipeline hosts, and AAIF operations staff into anonymous counts [^evt-community-events-pr-62].
- **Human-Gated Removal**: The `sync_chapters` module flags organizer names listed under non-qualifying status records and proposes their removal [^evt-community-events-pr-62]. To prevent public form submissions from evicting legitimate organizers, standard `--write` runs cannot delete entries; removals require explicit human inspection and the `--apply-removals` flag [^evt-community-events-pr-62].
- **Stale Cell Protection**: Cells targeted for update are re-read immediately prior to execution, aborting if concurrent external edits are detected [^evt-community-events-pr-62].

### Unified Multi-Page Report Navigation

A full synchronization run generates a six-page report suite consisting of `report.html`, coverage, activity, topics, members, and Slack audit views [^evt-community-events-pr-63]:
- **Cross-Page Top Bar**: The execution runner (`sync.py`) passes the ordered list of rendered pages via `AAIF_REPORT_NAV` to `report_style.page()`, which renders a sticky, flat, hairline top navigation bar [^evt-community-events-pr-63].
- **Dead-Link Prevention**: The reporting renderer (`render_report.py`) prunes failed or unwritten pipeline stages to ensure the navigation bar references only valid sibling HTML files [^evt-community-events-pr-63].
- **Print Isolation**: Top navigation bars are automatically hidden during print styling to preserve standalone PDF exports [^evt-community-events-pr-63].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Check Setup Skill
proposed_concept.description: Diagnostic agent skill validating local dependencies, Google Workspace connection files, Slack user tokens, and Luma credentials across CLI and plugin environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-check-setup` skill is a standalone diagnostic utility within the AAIF Community Events Toolkit that executes read-only preflight verification across local software runtimes, API access keys, and cloud service credentials[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7]. It provides actionable remediation advice when prerequisites are absent, guiding non-technical operators through setup without relying on an external administrative helper[^evt-community-events-pr-66].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill executes strictly using Python standard library modules to ensure portability when packaged as a standalone archive or deployed inside containerized and desktop agent harnesses like Goose and Claude Desktop[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].

## Verification Scope
The diagnostic workflow evaluates prerequisites sequentially, surfacing binary pass/fail indicators and plain-text remediation instructions[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7]:
- **Runtime Environment:** Confirms Python availability, required packaging structure, and headless Google Chrome installation for browser automation tasks[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].
- **Google Workspace (`gws`):** Validates the presence of the operator's Google connection configuration file and verifies active edit permissions on the central Community Intake Ops spreadsheet, surfacing missing configuration files rather than prompting invalid interactive logins[^evt-community-events-pr-66][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].
- **Slack User Credentials:** Confirms availability of an authorized Slack user token (`xoxp-`) possessing directory read and channel provisioning permissions[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27].
- **Luma API Access:** Checks connectivity and authorization against the community event calendar API[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].

## Credential Resolution Precedence
To support unprivileged installed plugin runtimes that lack inherited shell environments, credential resolution follows a pinned fallback order[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]:
1. Explicit process environment variables.
2. Repository root `.env` configuration files.
3. macOS Keychain entries (`aaif-slack-read-token`, `aaif-slack-write-token`, and `luma-api-key`), with per-run caching to mitigate interactive operating system authorization prompts[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].

# Lifecycle History
Originally conceived as an administrative helper-assisted check, `aaif-check-setup` was updated to support independent operator self-service, eliminating references to an external setup assistant and adapting error reporting to account for distinct first-time administrator versus subsequent operator provisioning pathways[^evt-community-events-pr-66][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27].

# References
- [Community Event Operations](community-event-operations.md)
- [Agent Plugins Standard](../standards/agent-plugins.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Toolkit
proposed_concept.description: Standardized agent skill suite and portable plugin runtime managing AAIF chapter provisioning, estate synchronization, and community event operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations Toolkit is an integrated operational skill suite and portable Agent Plugin packaged for cross-client execution across agent harnesses such as Goose, Claude Desktop, and Claude Code[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27]. It automates event tracking, community intake triage, Google Drive template cloning, OOXML rebrand transformations, Slack channel provisioning, and Luma event publishing[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].

# Architecture / Specification
The toolkit is distributed via standard [Agent Plugins](../standards/agent-plugins.md) manifests (`plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) and standard [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) definitions (`SKILL.md`)[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27].

## Execution and Portability Model
Installed plugins operate under execution models that differ substantially from active git checkouts[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]:
- **Path Resolution:** Commands referenced inside skill definitions invoke scripts relative to `<skill-root>` rather than hardcoded repository root paths, allowing execution across versioned, non-git directories under Claude Desktop or cloned repositories under Goose[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9].
- **State and Working Directory:** Persistent files write to dedicated paths managed by `aaif_events.datadir`, while ephemeral intermediate files isolate into temporary directories (`mktemp -d`) to prevent pollution of user working directories[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9].
- **Credential Fallback Chain:** Because desktop harnesses execute agent sessions without inherited shell environment variables, credential discovery falls back from system environment variables to repo-root `.env` files, and finally to secure operating system credential stores such as the macOS Keychain[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9].

## Operator Onboarding and Identity Partitioning
Operational maintenance bifurcates setup into two explicit phases[^evt-community-events-pr-66][^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27]:
1. **First-Time Administrator Setup:** Initial administrative provisioning establishes the central Google Cloud OAuth client, Luma API keys, and a dedicated Slack custom application defining user OAuth scopes (`channels:history`, `channels:read`, `channels:write`, `channels:write.invites`, `chat:write`, `groups:*`, `search:read`, `users:read`)[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27].
2. **Operator Onboarding:** Non-technical operators install the toolkit and configure dedicated credentials[^evt-community-events-pr-66]. User tokens (`xoxp-`) are bound to individual operator identities rather than generic bot accounts, ensuring channel creation and messaging reflect authorized human delegates[^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27].
Preflight readiness across these layers is verified interactively using [AAIF Check Setup](aaif-check-setup.md)[^evt-community-events-pr-66].

## Privacy and Data Hygiene
Because the toolkit repository is public, strict operational hygiene rules prohibit logging or committing personally identifiable information (PII) from intake spreadsheets, chapter CRMs, or Slack member directories[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]. Automated pre-commit checks enforce synthetic fixtures and prevent live test artifacts from persisting in version history[^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9].

# Lifecycle History
The toolkit evolved from developer-oriented CLI scripts into a standardized, cross-client Agent Plugin. Setup workflows were restructured to separate one-time infrastructure registration from individual operator onboarding, replacing administrative helper dependencies with self-contained preflight verification[^evt-community-events-pr-66][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].

# References
- [AAIF Check Setup](aaif-check-setup.md)
- [Agent Plugins Standard](../standards/agent-plugins.md)
- [Agent Skills Standard](../standards/agent-skills.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry models, execution trace formats, and harness event schemas across heterogeneous agent frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies within the Agentic AI Foundation to establish a shared understanding of agent observability, aligning existing telemetry efforts, identifying gaps, and producing open specifications and guidance where needed [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]. The working group focuses on the intersection of agent reasoning, behavior, and execution with observable signals and trace structures, with an emphasis on cross-framework and cross-tool interoperability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d].

# Governance and Operations
The working group operates under the governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]:
- **Chairs**: Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco, Chair) and Matthew Lee (Datadog, Co-Chair), appointed by Platinum and Gold working group members for the term spanning March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d].
- **Meeting Cadence**: Biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM PT over public Linux Foundation LFX Zoom [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d].
- **Communications**: Public mailing list (`wg-observability-traceability@lists.aaif.io`), dedicated Discord channel, and GitHub repository tracking work via issues and pull requests [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d].

# Deliverables and Workstreams
The working group coordinates several baseline documents and standardizing activities:
- [Prior Work Survey](../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md): Landscape survey capturing existing agent observability standards, tools, and protocols [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d].
- [Agent Observability Use Cases](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md): Shared catalog of operational use cases and practitioner observability requirements [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d].
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md): Nine-task execution plan establishing execution context propagation, causal execution tracing, and turn-based spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d].

# Liaison and Coordination Roster
The working group maintains active liaison channels across external standards bodies, adjacent AAIF working groups, and cross-boundary initiatives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9]:
- **External Standards Bodies**: Primary external coordination with the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG regarding turn definitions and turn span semantics; Agent Trace (Cursor); [AGNTCY](../resources/agntcy.md); libp2p; HOL; and Agent Action Capsule [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9].
- **Internal AAIF Working Groups**: [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) (submitting candidate terms such as turn and agent step); [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](accuracy-and-reliability.md) (evaluating agent evaluation outcomes in traces); [Identity & Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md); [Security & Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md); and [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9].
- **Cross-Boundary Initiatives**: Technical Committee coordinated liaisons including Agentic Resource Discovery ([ARD](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md)), Agent-to-Agent protocol ([A2A](../taxonomy/agent-to-agent.md)), ADK, [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md), and Cloud Trace [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Toolkit
proposed_concept.description: Standardized agent skill suite and portable plugin runtime managing AAIF chapter provisioning, estate synchronization, event planning, and communications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations Toolkit provides packaged agent skills and operational workflows instructing AI assistants—specifically [Goose](../resources/goose.md) or Claude Desktop—how to execute Agentic AI Foundation community operations using AAIF templates, Google Drive folders, Slack workspaces, and Luma calendars [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754]. The toolkit executes administrative, content generation, and chapter lifecycle tasks via plain-English instructions without requiring command-line programming from organizers [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754].

# Architecture / Specification
The toolkit coordinates multiple specialized operational routines across three primary capability domains [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754]:
- **Event Communications and Copywriting**: Drafts launch announcements, Luma descriptions, six-slide LinkedIn carousel narratives, speaker invitations, speaker bios, day-of-event presentation slides, RSVP attendee reminders, and post-event recaps. Attendee-facing communications automatically enforce compliance by embedding AAIF [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md) and Privacy Policy disclosures [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754].
- **Event Planning and Milestone Tracking**: Schedules chapter events in Google Drive Event Trackers, auto-calculates backward milestone due dates based on the event target date, reschedules cascading tasks upon date revisions, and aggregates RSVP counts and overdue tasks without mutating upstream systems [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754].
- **Chapter Provisioning and Estate Management**: Reviews pending community intake queues, audits data hygiene (normalizing capitalization, LinkedIn profile formats, and city records), executes full estate synchronization (`aaif-sync`) auditing Drive, Slack, and Luma assets, and handles automated chapter or online series provisioning via template cloning [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754].

# Lifecycle and Safeguards
The toolkit operates under a strict [Human-Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) paradigm to guarantee operational safety [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754]:
- **Approval Checkpoints**: The assistant must explicitly confirm with the operator before executing changes that mutate public state or affect external stakeholders [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754].
- **Intake Triage Boundary**: While the toolkit aggregates applicant summaries and drafts responses, admissions and acceptance decisions remain strictly with authorized human organizers [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754].
- **Read-Only Inspection**: Health auditing routines (such as Slack topology checks and RSVP status reports) execute purely read-only data extraction [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering pre-execution interception hooks, gateway checkpoints, sandbox boundaries, and cryptographic skill provenance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide provides practical defensive controls, architectural hardening patterns, and supply-chain verification standards for engineering teams deploying autonomous agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-49]. Developed within the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guideline outlines multi-tier verification baselines for runtime sandboxes, model gateway policy checkpoints, and extension packages such as Model Context Protocol servers and [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-49].

# Architecture / Specification

## Multi-Tier Supply-Chain Provenance
The framework establishes tiered controls for package ingestion and tool verification:
- **Build-Linked Artifact Provenance**: Requires MCP server packages to provide cryptographic attestations via npm provenance, PyPI attestations, or cosign signatures linking artifacts to immutable build pipelines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-49].
- **Cryptographic Skill Provenance (Tier 3 Proposal)**: An experimental tier proposes verifying skill publisher authenticity through C2PA Content Credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-49]. The mechanism binds the `SKILL.md` manifest to a validated publisher certificate via frontmatter manifest references and incorporates a digest of subsidiary assets in `metadata` to protect executable scripts [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-49].

## Security Boundaries and Cryptographic Limitations
The proposal notes critical threat boundary limitations regarding content credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-49]:
- **Identity vs. Safety**: Cryptographic signatures validate publisher identity and manifest integrity; they do not attest to runtime behavioral safety or absence of malicious logic [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-49].
- **Stripped Credential Detection**: Because stripped C2PA credentials appear unsigned, registry catalogs must record expected signing identities alongside hash pins to prevent downgrade attacks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-49].
- **Validation Scope**: Standard C2PA validators inspect only the primary manifest (`SKILL.md`), necessitating extended validation routines across the skill package directory structure [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-49].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, defensive architecture patterns, builder best practices, and runtime governance specifications for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-744e843d] The group produces open threat models, shared taxonomy contributions, defensive architecture design patterns, and runtime control standards that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to maintain trustworthy agentic deployments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-744e843d]

# Governance and Operations

The working group operates under the direction of co-chairs appointed by Platinum and Gold members for the term spanning March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-744e843d]

- Chair: Alex Frazer (Runlayer)
- Co-Chair: Junjie Bu (Google)

Operational triage and technical program support across the Technical Committee and working groups are supported by the AAIF Technical Program Manager, Dawn Wages.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

### Meeting Cadence

The group maintains two alternating biweekly meetings to support global participation across time zones:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-744e843d]

- **Primary Meeting**: Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT (1:00 PM ET / 6:00 PM UTC).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-744e843d]
- **APAC Meeting**: Biweekly on Mondays at 9:00 PM ET (Tuesday 2:00 AM UTC / 10:00 AM CST / 11:00 AM JST) on alternate weeks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-744e843d]

# Active Workstreams and Deliverables

The group coordinates several key technical deliverables:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling**: Systematic threat modeling workstreams led by Fernando Lucktemberg, identifying baseline agentic attack surfaces and evaluating industry risk frameworks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Reference repository of reusable security patterns, documenting recurring mitigations such as [attested isolated runtimes](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Concrete implementation guidance for practitioners operating agent workflows.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Coordination mechanism led by Govindaraj Palanisamy to evaluate security and privacy implications in requirements originating from peer groups like [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]
- **Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses**: Specification defining standard hooks, Policy Decision Point (PDP), and Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) integration across agent harnesses, gateways, identity layers, and sandboxes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

# Cross-Working Group Coordination

The group identifies unowned architectural seams across AAIF working groups, most notably ownership of the [kill switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) pattern, which bridges harness containment, identity revocation, and reliability guarantees.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f] The working group actively collaborates with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to define cohesive policy enforcement and attestation layers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

proposed_concept.title: Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses
proposed_concept.description: Standardized specification defining administrative harness lifecycle events, external authorization checkpoints, policy decision and enforcement points, and verifiable containment hooks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Control Surfaces for Agentic Harnesses is a standard specification initiated within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to define predictable, standardized interfaces for execution control and policy interception in agent harnesses such as Claude Code and Cursor.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f] Because diverse harness implementations currently expose ad hoc hooks, this standard provides common contract expectations for operators and tool builders.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

# Architecture / Specification

The specification standardizes how an external Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) and Policy Decision Point (PDP) integrate across agent execution environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f] It defines lifecycle interception hooks across four primary operational surfaces:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

1. **Agent Harness Environment**: Pre-execution, turn-level, and tool-dispatch interception hooks controlling the local agent loop.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]
2. **Gateway Interceptors**: Ingress and egress traffic policy enforcement handling protocol mediation (such as Model Context Protocol calls).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]
3. **Identity and Access Layer**: Authorization context validation and token delegation checkpoints (aligned with AuthZEN and related standards).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]
4. **Execution Sandboxes**: Kernel-level or containerized isolation boundaries enforcing system resource and capability boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

### Verifiable Conformance

The specification targets machine-verifiable compliance testing, allowing conforming harnesses to validate hook contracts and earn standardized trust badges demonstrating compatibility with external policy engines.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-11**: Introduced by Alex Frazer in the Security and Privacy Working Group under PR #45, synthesizing threat modeling, design pattern deliverables, and runtime policy requirements.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]
