proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch
proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern establishing an independent out-of-band containment loop to halt agentic execution loops and revoke authorization credentials.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Kill Switch is an architectural control plane pattern that establishes an out-of-band containment mechanism capable of deterministically halting an agentic loop, terminating subprocesses, or severing interaction with foundation model APIs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f] It provides an emergency containment boundary when autonomous agents violate operational boundaries, encounter prompt injection, or experience cascading failure loops.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern addresses two distinct functional layers within the agentic architecture:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

1. **Harness Kill Switch (Execution Containment)**: Implemented in the agent harness runtime to sever communication between the model and the agent execution loop, freeze tool dispatch, or terminate sandbox containers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]
2. **Access Kill Switch (Authorization Revocation)**: Implemented within the identity and policy enforcement infrastructure to immediately invalidate delegated credentials, session tokens, or API keys.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

### Cross-Working Group Seam

Because the kill switch spans execution harnesses, identity delegation, and reliability metrics, its governance constitutes an active cross-working group seam spanning [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), and [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f] The Agentic Commerce standards mapping team tracks the pattern as an essential shared requirement across standards bodies.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-11**: Discussed in the Security and Privacy Working Group as an unowned horizontal seam requiring coordinated ownership between runtime harness control and authorization layers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-6623dd4920c0-d9c3520f]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing telemetry models, execution trace formats, agent trajectory schemas, and cross-boundary harness observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, open telemetry formats, and architectural reference models for monitoring and auditing agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5] Its scope spans turn-by-turn execution traces, distributed context propagation across multi-agent boundaries, payload attestation signatures, and trajectory interchange formats.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5]

# Active Deliverables and Collaborations

The working group drives several core standards and cross-foundation alignment initiatives:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5]

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A standardized schema defining execution context propagation, causal execution tracing, and turn-by-turn agent state transitions, developed in active collaboration with the OpenTelemetry (OTel) GenAI Special Interest Group.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5]
- **ATIF v2 Trajectory Standardization**: Collaboration with Google, Harbor, and industry partners to standardize Agent Trajectory Interchange Format (ATIF v2) semantics, establishing mappings between OpenTelemetry traces and autonomous trajectory datasets.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5]
- **Agentic Observability White Paper**: Foundational practitioner guide distinguishing established distributed tracing practices from emerging agent-specific paradigms, targeted for review across IETF and IRTF working groups.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5]
- **Payload Attestation Signing**: Investigation into non-intrusive signature schemes that validate observation records and execution payloads without breaking trace propagation or modifying OTLP data models.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5]

# Cross-Working Group and Standards Coordination

The group coordinates closely with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) on defining foundational execution primitives such as "turn" and "step", with the emerging Attestation and Evidence working group, and with external standards bodies including the IETF, OpenTelemetry, and Cloud Security Alliance.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5]

proposed_concept.title: WG Toolkit
proposed_concept.description: Python utility library providing LFX MCP client interfaces, Zoom transcript download fallbacks, and structured model completion for AAIF working group automation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The WG Toolkit is a shared Python package (`wg-toolkit`) maintained in the `aaif/working-group-chairs` repository that provides foundational building blocks for Agentic AI Foundation automation scripts reading LFX meeting platform data [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-537f2936247b-4efa392f]. It provides common infrastructure for scripts that generate meeting minutes, compile status reports, and process committee transcripts across working groups [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-537f2936247b-4efa392f].

# Architecture / Specification
The package is organized into four core functional modules:
- `wg_toolkit.lfx`: Manages LFID OAuth and authentication through an `mcp-remote` bridge or explicit bearer token, dynamic tool discovery by name suffix, and automated pagination via `collect_pages` [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-537f2936247b-4efa392f]. Environment token isolation withholds credentials such as `LFX_MCP_TOKEN` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` from helper child processes [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-537f2936247b-4efa392f].
- `wg_toolkit.transcripts`: Handles WebVTT and plain-text cue parsing, implementing `TranscriptDownloader` to pull Zoom VTT files directly or fall back to a headless Playwright automation flow via the Zoom recording player [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-537f2936247b-4efa392f].
- `wg_toolkit.llm`: Exposes `StructuredModelClient` and `ModelConfig` executing strict JSON Schema completions against OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoints, evaluating refusal, transport failures, and token truncation [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-537f2936247b-4efa392f].
- `wg_toolkit.common`: Standardizes date and HTTPS URL validation, file output collision protection with owner-only permissions, and credential-safe error messages [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-537f2936247b-4efa392f].

The toolkit is designed to be declared as an editable path dependency in downstream automation scripts, including [skills/aaif-wg-meeting-notes](../skills/aaif-wg-meeting-notes.md) and [skills/aaif-wg-monthly-report](../skills/aaif-wg-monthly-report.md) [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-537f2936247b-4efa392f].

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch
proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern establishing an independent out-of-band containment loop to halt agent operations, revoke credentials, and prevent cascading harm.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Kill Switch pattern defines an independent out-of-band containment mechanism that interrupts autonomous agent execution, revokes identity credentials, and halts delegated authority across systems to contain anomalous or malicious behavior [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-40179adf]. Formulated as a core deliverable within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the pattern addresses operational containment across both enterprise trust boundaries and open-internet interactions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-8b0afa11][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-1f9fb425].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern formalizes containment and revocation across several layers of the agent stack:
- **Runtime Interception**: Direct execution halts commanded by local runtime watchdogs, policy decision points, or administrative control surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-40179adf].
- **Credential Revocation and Identity Invalidation**: Rapid invalidation of active bearer tokens, delegated session keys, and authority grants [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-40179adf]. In enterprise contexts, containment relies on centralized Identity Providers (IdPs) and protocols like OpenID Continuous Access Evaluation Profile (CAEP), whereas open-internet and cross-domain architectures explore decentralized ledger state or broadcast status registers to avoid single points of failure and ensure revocation checks remain verifiable during network partitions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-40179adf].
- **Cascading Revocation**: Hierarchical revocation mechanisms ensuring that pulling a principal kill switch transitively invalidates subagents, ephemeral execution keys, and delegated subtask mandates spawned during the session [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-40179adf].
- **Propagation Bounds**: Enforces deterministic upper bounds between revocation publication and universal verifier rejection (e.g., verifying refusal within bounded propagation windows) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-40179adf].

# Lifecycle History
Initial draft specifications for the kill switch pattern merged into the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md) in October 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-1f9fb425]. Working group reviews subsequently expanded the pattern to reconcile enterprise CAEP models with open-internet zero-knowledge and distributed credential architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-40179adf].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, defensive architecture patterns, builder best practices, and runtime security standards for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is a charter-approved AAIF body focused on establishing vendor-neutral threat modeling methodologies, defensive design patterns, security guidelines, and runtime containment specifications for agentic artificial intelligence [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-8b0afa11]. The group coordinates cross-cutting security reviews with other working groups and aligns vocabulary with the Foundation's taxonomy workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-8b0afa11][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-1f9fb425].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group drives five primary workstreams and deliverables:
- **Threat Modeling**: Completed the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis-and-framework-design.md) assessing traditional frameworks against non-deterministic systems, and conducts active modeling incorporating MITRE ATLAS and OWASP standards [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-1f9fb425].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Authors repeatable defensive patterns in the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md), including [Approval Checkpoints](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [Kill Switches](../patterns/kill-switch.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-1f9fb425].
- **Security Best Practices Guide**: Publishes the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guide, open to external contributions and covering pre-execution hooks, gateway mediation, and sandboxing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-1f9fb425].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Operates the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) with delegates across Commerce, Observability, and Governance workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-1f9fb425][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-40179adf].
- **Attestation & Verification Collaboration**: Coordinates with the [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) groups on Merkle tree execution traces and an experimental 90-day attestation pilot [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-faf61688d774-40179adf].

# Lifecycle History
Formed in early 2026 under chair Alex Frazer, the group's charter received formal Technical Committee approval in May 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-8b0afa11]. In late 2026, the group delivered its threat modeling gap analysis, published the first release of the security best practices guide, established APAC meeting cadences, and integrated draft control plane specifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-8b0afa11][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-1f9fb425].

proposed_concept.title: Meshllm
proposed_concept.description: Distributed compute pooling framework enabling safe LLM inference across edge, consumer, and isolated server hardware through standard APIs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Meshllm is an open-source distributed compute pooling project proposed to the Agentic AI Foundation that aggregates consumer edge devices, isolated servers, and GPUs to host and serve large language model workloads [^evt-project-proposals-issue-70]. The project seeks to make underutilized distributed hardware accessible for agentic reasoning and model inference through standardized consumption APIs [^evt-project-proposals-issue-70].

# Architecture / Specification
Meshllm implements several core capabilities:
- **Cross-Platform Compute Pooling**: Aggregates compute capacity across diverse hardware architectures and operating systems into a unified execution pool [^evt-project-proposals-issue-70].
- **Standardized API Interfaces**: Exposes inference endpoints using standard interfaces including [OpenResponses](../standards/open-responses.md), allowing chat interfaces, agent harnesses, and client applications to consume pooled models transparently [^evt-project-proposals-issue-70].
- **Agent Framework Integration**: Built adjacent to the [Goose](../resources/goose.md) agent framework to enable community compute sharing, with integrations supporting the Model Context Protocol (MCP), [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md), and [Agent Client Protocol](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-70].
- **Planned Synergy**: Explores mediation through [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) for traffic routing and integration with [OpenSandbox](../resources/opensandbox.md) for pooled workload execution [^evt-project-proposals-issue-70].

# Lifecycle History
Submitted as an open project proposal to the Technical Committee under issue #70 licensed under Apache 2.0 [^evt-project-proposals-issue-70].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Routers and Gateways Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Proposed AAIF working group defining shared architecture, intermediary protocols, and conformance tests for agent routers and gateways.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Routers and Gateways Working Group is a proposed technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with standardizing the intermediary layer connecting AI agents to models, tools, and peer agents[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-7]. In production deployments, routers and gateways mediate communication flows across protocols including Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and model provider APIs.

The proposal addresses architectural fragmentation where implementations partition data planes, control planes, policy enforcement, and credential brokering incompatibly, while protocols lack prescriptive specifications for proxy behavior regarding streaming, tool lists, and error propagation[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-7].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's proposed scope includes:
- Developing a layered reference architecture distinguishing the data plane, control plane, registry or catalog integration, policy decision/enforcement points, credential brokering, usage accounting, and telemetry export across central, sidecar, mesh, and embedded deployment topologies[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-7].
- Defining intermediary behavior profiles specifying mandatory and prohibited proxy actions when handling MCP, A2A, and LLM requests[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-7].
- Establishing vendor-neutral interfaces between gateways and surrounding policy engines, identity providers, and registries[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-7].
- Implementing an open, implementation-agnostic conformance test suite and coordinating interoperability validation[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-7].

Explicit boundaries place threat modeling under the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), telemetry data models under the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), identity protocols under the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), and Kubernetes Gateway APIs under upstream working groups[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-7].

# Lifecycle History

- Proposed in November 2026 by Charna Parkey (IBM) via AAIF working-group-proposals issue #7[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-7].

proposed_concept.title: Aertun
proposed_concept.description: Open-source evidence and verification layer reconciling agent telemetry against gateway logs, target audit trails, and Merkle-tree audit logs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Aertun is an open-source, self-hosted evidence and verification layer designed to evaluate AI agent operational accounts against external, third-party audit evidence[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71]. Implemented as a single Go binary, Aertun reconciles self-reported telemetry from an agent against intermediary gateway logs and independent target system audit trails[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71].

Verification outcomes are rendered as cryptographic in-toto Statements packaged in Dual-Signature Envelope (DSSE) envelopes, dual-signed using Ed25519 and post-quantum ML-DSA-65 keys[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71]. Each assertion produces an offline-verifiable verdict categorized as proven, refuted, or inconclusive with defined statistical bounds[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71].

# Architecture / Specification

Aertun's capabilities include:
- **Three-Way Agent Reconciliation**: Compares agent [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) traces against gateway interaction records (such as [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md)) and target system access logs to detect unreported or phantom actions[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71].
- **Revocation Efficacy Proofs**: Demonstrates whether access ceased across enterprise identity providers following [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) invocation or credential revocation[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71].
- **Log Completeness and Bitcoin Anchoring**: Generates Merkle-tree audit proofs demonstrating logs have not been truncated or forked, anchoring log roots to the Bitcoin blockchain for proof-of-existence[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71].
- **Agent Interface**: Exposes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server supporting OAuth 2.1, DPoP-bound tokens, Shared Signals and Events (SSF), and emergency termination triggers[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71].
- **Detection Wind Tunnel**: Automates attack replay (such as prompt injection or MCP rug-pulls) alongside benign baseline workflows in CI environments to benchmark false-negative and false-positive detection rates[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71].

# Lifecycle History

- Initiated in October 2026; release v0.2.0 published in November 2026[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71].
- Proposed for AAIF Sandbox project incubation under the Technical Committee review process via issue #71[^evt-project-proposals-issue-71].

proposed_concept.title: anySQL
proposed_concept.description: Open-source Python library and relational telemetry schema mapping LLM agent interactions and RAG pipelines into queryable Apache Arrow tables.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

anySQL is an open-source Python library that captures telemetry from LLM applications, autonomous agents, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, formatting the records into standardized relational tables queryable via standard SQL[^evt-project-proposals-issue-72]. It operates without hosted dependencies, buffering traces in memory or local SQLite files and executing in-process queries using DuckDB[^evt-project-proposals-issue-72].

The library normalizes heterogeneous execution streams into six canonical Apache Arrow tables: `llm_responses`, `eval_results`, `pipeline_runs`, `agent_tool_calls`, `agent_trace`, and `rag_chunks`[^evt-project-proposals-issue-72]. Shared join keys—notably `session_id`, a monotonic `step_order`, and `query_id`—enable cross-boundary relational analysis across retrieval, tool calling, and model evaluation stages[^evt-project-proposals-issue-72].

# Architecture / Specification

anySQL incorporates:
- **Client Instrumentation**: Provides transparent interceptors for OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs alongside specialized agent and RAG tracers[^evt-project-proposals-issue-72].
- **Relational Schema**: Six fixed Apache Arrow tables bound by `session_id` and sequential `step_order`, enabling multi-turn step attribution, tool-loop detection, and prompt-injection tracing via declarative SQL joins[^evt-project-proposals-issue-72].
- **anysql-proxy**: A local HTTP mediation proxy that intercepts traffic from coding assistants (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Continue) to record tokens, latency, cost metrics, and editor context directly into DuckDB[^evt-project-proposals-issue-72].

# Lifecycle History

- Created by Karthikeyan Sadayamuthu in March 2026 (v0.1.0)[^evt-project-proposals-issue-72].
- Served as the measurement engine for academic research on prompt-injection compromise detection in agent telemetry (accepted at IEEE CSTA 2026)[^evt-project-proposals-issue-72].
- Proposed for AAIF Sandbox project incubation under the Technical Committee review process via issue #72[^evt-project-proposals-issue-72].

proposed_concept.title: hippo-memory
proposed_concept.description: Local-first, zero-LLM-call persistent memory layer for AI coding agents and Model Context Protocol clients with git-mirrored storage.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
hippo-memory is an open-source, local-first memory layer designed for AI coding agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73]. It persists operational context, developer feedback, and learned heuristics into a local SQLite store alongside git-committable Markdown mirrors under `.hippo/`, enabling coding agents such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor to share working memory across tools without vendor lock-in [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73].

In contrast to cloud memory services that trigger model queries on memory persistence and retrieval, hippo-memory executes zero LLM calls on its standard save and recall path [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73]. Built on Node.js built-in `node:sqlite` without runtime dependencies, it packages a local Hugging Face Transformers embedding pipeline configured during initialization [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73].

# Architecture / Specification
hippo-memory provides modular state retention, synchronization, and governance primitives [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73]:

- **Biologically Inspired Memory Lifecycle**: Operates a typed provenance model (`MEMORY_ENVELOPE.md`) defining envelope metadata such as category kind, scope, owner, artifact references, session identifiers, and confidence ratings [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73]. Lifecycle routines include outcome feedback (`hippo outcome --bad`) to degrade memories associated with faulty responses, fact supersession (`hippo supersede`), decay for idle items with pinned invariants, and sleep consolidation (`hippo sleep`) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73].
- **Git-Native Transparency**: Synchronizes local SQLite tables with plain-text Markdown mirrors in `.hippo/`, allowing teams to review, diff, and audit agent-learned memories in code reviews and pull requests [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73].
- **Self-Hosted Team Service**: Supports multi-user deployments via `hippo serve`, exposing MCP and HTTP interfaces protected by role-based authorization, per-user API tokens, and append-only audit trails [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73].
- **Protocol Integration**: Ships 13 memory control tools exposed over the Model Context Protocol, facilitating integration into agent runtimes, shell environments, and intermediary control proxies such as [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73].

# Lifecycle History
hippo-memory was created in March 2026 by Kit Fun (Keith) So of KITFUNSO LTD [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73]. In November 2026, the project was proposed for Sandbox-stage hosting in the Agentic AI Foundation under issue 73 [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73]. The proposal aligns with objectives across [Working Group Agent Context & Memory](../working-groups/agent-context-and-memory.md), [Working Group Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), and [Working Group Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73].

# References
- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/kitfunso/hippo-memory) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73]
- [AAIF Project Proposal #73](https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/73) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-73]

proposed_concept.title: Event Domain Modeling
proposed_concept.description: Procedural agent skill guiding event-management domain modeling, lifecycle transitions, registration invariants, and architecture decisions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Event Domain Modeling is a procedural agent skill governing technical event domain models, entity glossaries, lifecycle transitions, and architecture trade-offs for AAIF community initiatives [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786]. Established within the AAIF Dallas community infrastructure, it formalizes domain boundaries, registration constraints, and operational invariants for agent-assisted community event management [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1a18650fe092-ea310fad].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill establishes strict procedural gates when reviewing or updating event management software, data schemas, and agent interactions [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786]:

- **Terminology Harmonization**: Mandates strict disambiguation between conflicting entity concepts (e.g., separating member, user, attendee, and presenter identities) and synchronization with canonical domain glossaries [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786].
- **Edge Scenario Verification**: Instructs agents to challenge ambiguous requirements against failure modes, including publishing incomplete event records, cancellations with active registrations, capacity exhaustion, overlapping session schedules, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool retries [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786].
- **Architecture Decision Rigor**: Prompts an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) whenever non-obvious operational or architectural trade-offs emerge, such as prioritizing static-first web generation over mutable runtime APIs to minimize operational attack surface and isolate attendee registration data [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1a18650fe092-ea310fad].

## Domain Invariants
The skill codifies core invariants that agentic and human workflows cannot violate [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786]:
1. Public registrations are accepted only for published community events [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786].
2. An attendee may hold at most one active registration per community event [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786].
3. Session schedules must remain bounded within the parent community event time window [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786].
4. Cancellations must preserve immutable audit records [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786].
5. Organizer modifications require explicit authorization gates [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786].
6. Agent and MCP actions must never bypass domain validation logic [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786].

# Lifecycle History
The skill was established in the AAIF Dallas community repository alongside ADR 0001, defining operational boundaries for the Dallas Agentic AI Summit web platform [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1a18650fe092-ea310fad].

# References
- [AAIF Dallas Community Repository](https://github.com/aaif/aaif-dallas-community) [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-1fe3ce7fd6b7-ca482786]

proposed_concept.title: Event API Contracts
proposed_concept.description: Procedural agent skill defining design standards, boundary validation, authorization enforcement, and testing rules for AAIF Dallas HTTP APIs and MCP tools.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

`event-api-contracts` is an operational agent skill governing the design, evolution, and contract testing of HTTP APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and agent workflows across AAIF Dallas event services.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-333926b09e66-2184428a] It enforces strict architectural boundaries across process and transport layers, requiring that validation, authorization, and domain invariants reside in service code rather than relying on agent prompts or client-side controls.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-333926b09e66-2184428a]

# Architecture / Specification

The skill specifies contractual requirements across shared service layers and protocol-specific interfaces:[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-333926b09e66-2184428a]

- **Shared Contract Rules**: Request and response schemas must derive from a single canonical type definition; endpoint paths, schemas, and tool definitions must align with domain vocabulary established in [Event Domain Modeling](../skills/event-domain-modeling.md); untrusted input must be validated prior to invoking application logic; and mutations or retries must preserve idempotency.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-333926b09e66-2184428a]
- **HTTP API Checklist**: Every endpoint specification must explicitly define the requesting actor, authentication scheme, authorization rules, request/response payload schemas, domain-specific error codes, rate and abuse constraints, and idempotency guarantees.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-333926b09e66-2184428a]
- **MCP Tool Standards**: Each MCP tool must perform a single bounded operation with a strictly typed JSON schema, declare all preconditions and side effects within its description, reject unauthorized invocations, return stable structured payloads, and maintain automated contract and failure-path tests.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-333926b09e66-2184428a]
- **Agent Operational Boundaries**: Agents are restricted to invoking approved tools and prohibited from direct database persistence; prompts guide context and task objectives but cannot substitute for server-side validation or authorization gates; and agent execution traces must avoid persisting secrets or unnecessary attendee personal data.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-333926b09e66-2184428a]

# Lifecycle History

Introduced in the AAIF Dallas community repository to standardize service integrations between event management agents and external HTTP/MCP endpoints.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-333926b09e66-2184428a]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

`event-requirements` is an interactive agent skill used to clarify technical event-management requests, eliminate unstated assumptions, and capture canonical domain terminology and architectural decisions for the AAIF Dallas community.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-47d3099d5d03-c0922d27] Executed with model invocation disabled, it guides practitioners through a structured design-tree interview to resolve decision frontiers before any code implementation begins.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-47d3099d5d03-c0922d27]

# Architecture / Specification

The skill organizes requirements intake across systematic procedural phases:[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-47d3099d5d03-c0922d27]

- **Design Tree Interviewing**: Groups inquiries into dependent rounds, queries the active decision frontier simultaneously, and provides recommended defaults to accelerate human confirmation.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-47d3099d5d03-c0922d27]
- **Core Domain Dimensions**: Evaluates primary actors (attendee, presenter, organizer, volunteer, administrator), lifecycle state transition permissions, registration and waitlist rules, check-in constraints, privacy and authorization boundaries, and target workflows governed by [Event API Contracts](../skills/event-api-contracts.md).[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-47d3099d5d03-c0922d27]
- **Artifact Synchronization**: Resolves ambiguous terminology using [Event Domain Modeling](../skills/event-domain-modeling.md), records canonical terms in repository glossaries, captures irreversible trade-offs in architecture decision records (ADRs), and formats final requirements into structured issue tracker entries.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-47d3099d5d03-c0922d27][^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-3f6ddafc4eae-6a744dcf]

# Lifecycle History

Established in the AAIF Dallas community repository to enforce disciplined requirements gathering and terminology alignment before changes to event automation systems.[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-47d3099d5d03-c0922d27]

proposed_concept.title: Full-Stack Event Delivery Skill
proposed_concept.description: Procedural agent skill implementing AAIF Dallas event-management features as narrow, tested vertical slices across frontend, backend, APIs, MCP tools, and agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`fullstack-event-delivery` is an operational agent skill governing end-to-end implementation of AAIF Dallas event-management capabilities as narrow, tested vertical slices spanning user interfaces, backend logic, APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and autonomous agent workflows[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c][^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-b33563055168-618b63aa]. The skill enforces strict architectural boundaries to avoid speculative infrastructure, ensuring that business rules reside in shared application services rather than being duplicated across adapters or presentation layers[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c][^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-a54ff182c7e8-97bf5d62].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill operates according to vertical-slice engineering principles adapted from Matt Pocock's workflow, prioritizing complete user capabilities over horizontal layer isolation[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c][^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-b33563055168-618b63aa]:

1. **Slice Definition**: Identify the target actor, action, result, and expected failure modes prior to implementation[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c].
2. **Boundary Testing**: Validate public test seams before authoring logic[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c].
3. **Domain Centralization**: Encapsulate domain rules once within shared application services, preventing policy drift across frontend or transport interfaces[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c].
4. **Adapter Exposure**: Surface capabilities via typed HTTP handlers and consume them from presentation components without copying domain invariants[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c].
5. **Tool and Agent Integration**: Add MCP tools or agent workflows strictly when required by the specification, routing execution through identical service authorization paths[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c].
6. **Verification and Review**: Run targeted and full test suites, concluding with an independent review via [`./event-review.md`](./event-review.md) against specification acceptance criteria[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c].

### Architectural Boundaries
The skill defines strict component responsibilities[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c]:
- **Frontend Components**: Manage presentation and local interaction state without owning lifecycle rules.
- **HTTP Handlers**: Handle protocol serialization, transport parsing, and authentication.
- **Application Services**: Encapsulate use-case orchestration and business flows.
- **Domain Modules**: Guard domain invariants and state transitions.
- **Persistence Adapters**: Execute transactions and queries without deciding product policy.
- **MCP Tools**: Function as thin, typed adapters enforcing explicit authorization and bounded inputs.
- **Agents**: Formulate plans and invoke approved tools without directly mutating underlying storage.

# Lifecycle History
- **Merged Skill Specification**: Authored and integrated into the `aaif/aaif-dallas-community` repository under `.github/skills/fullstack-event-delivery/SKILL.md` to guide engineering workflows for the static-first event platform release[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-6cb8eb7b0e35-372ed90c][^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-a54ff182c7e8-97bf5d62].

proposed_concept.title: Event Change Review Skill
proposed_concept.description: Procedural agent skill independently reviewing event-management code changes against engineering standards and originating issue specifications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`event-review` is a maintainer and verification agent skill that evaluates AAIF Dallas pull requests and commits against documented engineering standards and originating feature specifications[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-cfb0e91cc971-992f230f][^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-a54ff182c7e8-97bf5d62]. It separates findings into two distinct evaluation axes—the Standards axis and the Specification axis—to detect security vulnerabilities, logic bypasses, and scope discrepancies before changes are integrated[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-cfb0e91cc971-992f230f].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill operates as a verification gate executed prior to declaring full-stack delivery complete[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-a54ff182c7e8-97bf5d62][^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-cfb0e91cc971-992f230f]:

### Review Axes
1. **Standards Axis**: Audits code for architectural hygiene, operational safety, and defensive engineering practices[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-cfb0e91cc971-992f230f]:
   - Detection of duplicated lifecycle logic across interface adapters.
   - Prevention of unauthorized access or validation bypasses across UI, API, MCP, and agent boundaries.
   - Protection against leaking secrets or sensitive attendee data into logs, traces, prompts, or serialized responses.
   - Identification of schema drift between transport layers and domain behaviors.
   - Mitigation of implementation-coupled test patterns, speculative abstractions, missing idempotency, or lost registration histories.
2. **Specification Axis**: Evaluates the change against the originating GitHub issue or specification[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-cfb0e91cc971-992f230f]:
   - Missing or partially implemented requirements.
   - Unrequested behavior or out-of-scope implementations.
   - Semantically incorrect behavior despite passing syntactical tests.
   - Acceptance criteria lacking test coverage.

### Operational Workflow
- The reviewer requires a fixed commit, branch, or merge-base reference and confirms the diff is non-empty[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-cfb0e91cc971-992f230f].
- Mechanical issues enforced by the existing compiler and linting toolchain are explicitly bypassed[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-cfb0e91cc971-992f230f].
- Output reports cite specific file paths and line numbers alongside violated requirements, summarizing the total finding count and highest-severity risk for each axis[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-cfb0e91cc971-992f230f].

# Lifecycle History
- **Merged Skill Specification**: Standardized in `aaif/aaif-dallas-community` at `.github/skills/event-review/SKILL.md` as the final quality gate in the agentic development workflow[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-cfb0e91cc971-992f230f][^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-b33563055168-618b63aa].

proposed_concept.title: Event Test-Driven Development
proposed_concept.description: Procedural agent skill enforcing a red-green-refactor loop to verify event functionality across domain, API, MCP, and agent seams.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `event-tdd` skill guides agents and engineers through a red-green-refactor workflow to verify community event behaviors across public, observable seams[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2]. Rather than coupling tests to internal implementation details, prompts, or database schemas, the skill prioritizes verification at the highest observable abstraction level agreed upon with human operators[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill defines testing seams, core operational rules, and glossary-driven naming patterns for test-driven development[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].

## Verification Seams
Before authoring tests, agents confirm public observation seams with operators, selecting from[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2]:
- **Domain and Use-Case Logic**: Scenarios validating event domain invariants without transport overhead (complementing `../skills/event-domain-modeling.md`).
- **HTTP API Contracts**: End-to-end HTTP request and typed response validation (aligning with `../skills/event-api-contracts.md`).
- **Frontend User Interactions**: Interface behavior tested against controlled adapters.
- **MCP Tool Invocation**: Tool execution exercised directly through a running Model Context Protocol server.
- **Agent Behavior Graders**: Evaluations measuring observable agent tool calls, argument validity, and terminal outcomes.
- **Production-Like Integration Slices**: Transactional state persistence and schema migration validation.

## Operational Rules
1. Write a single failing behavioral test first[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].
2. Author the minimal production code needed to satisfy the test[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].
3. Iterate to the next independently valuable behavior[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].
4. Refactor only after achieving green tests, never during behavior implementation[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].
5. Compare outputs against independent sources of truth[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].
6. Avoid asserting private function invocations, database table structures, or prompt phrasing when public outcomes can be evaluated[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].
7. Mock external system boundaries only, preserving domain validation rules[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].
8. Cover authorization gates, input boundaries, idempotency/retry handling, and user-facing error modes on external interfaces[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].

## Naming and Execution
Tests use domain glossary phrasing (for example, verifying attendee registration, retry idempotency, or organizer cancellation workflows)[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2]. Agents execute the minimal relevant test target after each loop and run the full test suite before handing off for code review (coordinating with `../skills/fullstack-event-delivery.md` and `../skills/event-review.md`)[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].

# Lifecycle History
- Introduced as an authoritative operational skill in `aaif-dallas-community` via `.github/skills/event-tdd/SKILL.md`[^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-fb3c2f0e279b-737452f2].

mutations.rationale: Establish the AAIF Dallas Community Web Platform resource documenting its typed JSON content architecture, CI/CD verification workflows, and OIDC AWS deployment infrastructure.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Dallas Community Web Platform
proposed_concept.description: Static web architecture, typed JSON content domain schema, and OIDC deployment pipeline powering the AAIF Dallas community summit portal.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Dallas Community Web Platform is the official static web portal and operational content estate powering the AAIF Dallas community summit [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4]. Implemented in Vite, TypeScript, and React, the site decouples public summit presentation from content management through a typed JSON content architecture, automated GitHub Actions change workflows, and a keyless OpenID Connect (OIDC) deployment pipeline targeting Amazon S3 and CloudFront [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-28802fbf11c8-a0805ead] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-7f6254f34e12-91809500]. It directly serves event tracks, speaker rosters, committee assignments, and registration checkout while enforcing strict privacy boundaries against publishing attendee data or credentials [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-pr-4].

# Architecture / Specification

## Content Domain Architecture
The site reads static domain data from structured JSON documents located under `src/content/` [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4]:
- `event.json`: Summit metadata, event dates, registration references, and external student poster submission URLs [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4].
- `schedule.json`: Conference tracks, individual sessions, scheduled time slots, assigned rooms, speakers, and topical tags [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-pr-4].
- `speakers.json`: Presenter biographies, social profiles, and session associations [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4].
- `partners.json`: Organizing communities, community partners, and sponsoring organizations [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4].
- `organizers.json`: Core team and committee membership records with affiliations and headshots [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-pr-4].
- `committees.json`: Operational workstreams and organizational responsibilities [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4].
- `resources.json`: Public attendee lab preparation materials and prerequisites [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4].
- `news.json`: Editorial updates and summit announcements [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4].

Static image assets are segregated into typed directories under `public/images/`, including dedicated directories for CORE team portraits (`public/images/core-team/`) and committee member headshots (`public/images/committee-team/`) with initials fallbacks for missing assets [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-509a7fef8a34-033bfcc9] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-f6d36ab592c3-3152c916].

## Data Validation and Privacy Rules
Data integrity and privacy constraints are strictly enforced before deployment:
- **Privacy Boundary**: Committing attendee exports, participant CSV files, private contact information, Luma API keys, or organizer secrets into the repository is prohibited [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4].
- **Schema & Relational Integrity**: Local and continuous integration checks (`npm run validate:content`) execute Zod schemas from `src/content/schema.ts`, verifying field types, date formats, and cross-reference links between speakers and sessions [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-28802fbf11c8-a0805ead] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4].
- **Content Mutation Flow**: Non-developer maintainers submit content via a GitHub Actions workflow ("Prepare content change") which validates full object replacement payloads and opens a structured pull request [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-2ac4893aa049-e1fe43a4].

## Deployment Pipeline and Infrastructure
Production deployment is fully automated through GitHub Actions upon merge to `main` [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-28802fbf11c8-a0805ead] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-7f6254f34e12-91809500]:
- **Runtime Environment**: Built using Node.js 22 within an `ubuntu-latest` runner governed by the `production` environment and single-concurrency lock `production-static-site` [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-28802fbf11c8-a0805ead].
- **Keyless Authentication**: The workflow exchanges GitHub OIDC tokens (`token.actions.githubusercontent.com`) for an AWS IAM role (`AAIFDallasStaticSiteDeployment`) scoped strictly to the repository and environment [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-28802fbf11c8-a0805ead] [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-7f6254f34e12-91809500].
- **Hosting Topology**: Static assets sync to an Amazon S3 bucket, followed by a CloudFront cache invalidation, with DNS managed via Cloudflare and TLS certificates hosted in ACM `us-east-1` [^evt-aaif-dallas-community-file-7f6254f34e12-91809500].
